arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; gradient flow shown by blue reverse arrows
arrangement.shared: the 3D Gaussians hub is shared by projection and density control branches

insights.structure: A short left-to-right lead-in (SfM point scatter -> Initialization -> 3D Gaussians) feeds a loop in which Projection (top) and Adaptive Density Control (bottom) sit between the Gaussians and the Differentiable Tile Rasterizer, which then pairs with an Image box at far right.
insights.data: The two data ends are drawn as data rather than boxes: SfM points as a scatter of black dots and the 3D Gaussians as a cluster of soft blurred green ellipses; Camera and Image are white boxes, processing steps are grey boxes.
insights.emphasis: The only coloured, non-rectangular element is the green Gaussian cluster with a bold label, placed at the hub where every loop arrow starts and ends.
insights.flow: Black curved arrows carry the forward operation flow clockwise around the loop while light-blue arrows run beside them in the opposite direction for gradients, keyed in a two-entry legend at the bottom right.
insights.avoid: The Camera box enters only Projection with a long straight arrow and floats unaligned above the loop; the rasterizer-to-Image arrows are a cramped pair.

figures.lesson: Make the scene representation the hub of the optimisation loop and draw it as its own primitives (soft coloured ellipses), with paired black forward and light-blue gradient arrows so the differentiable path reads without words.

figures.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering

arrangement.inputs_as: a rendered 3D character and its Gaussian blob thumbnail stacked at the far left, with x,y,z and t as math labels on curved arrows entering the encoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two dotted rounded containers sit side by side, encoder left and three-head decoder right, with input and output Gaussians as renders outside on the left and right edges.
insights.data: The 4D field is drawn as six small 4x4 grids in two rows (xt, yt, zt above xy, yz, xz), each in its own border colour with faded copies behind, feeding a tall orange feature column.
insights.emphasis: The encoder's multicolour plane grid takes the largest area, and each decoder head ends in its math output (Δx,Δy,Δz, Δr, Δs) so the predicted deformations are named directly.
insights.flow: Curved black arrows carry x,y,z and t from the left render into the encoder, a straight arrow runs through feature column and MLP, then fan out to three heads, and a curved arrow loops up and right to the deformed Gaussians and down via 'Splatting' to the final render.
insights.avoid: The container labels sit below the dotted frames in plain small type and the right label touches the crop edge, and the symbol key is a dense grey text box crowding the top right.

figures.lesson: Draw a factorised spatio-temporal field as its labelled planes (xt, yt, zt over xy, yz, xz) in pair-specific colours with faded copies behind for resolutions, so the decomposition reads without text.

figures.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (training-free); a 'Reward Feedback' arrow returns from Evaluation to Expert Recruitment

insights.structure: Four tinted stage panels form a clockwise 2x2 cycle inside a dashed 'x N rounds' frame, with Goal and Outcome boxes outside on the left edge and a dotted zoom fan-out to a three-round example strip underneath.
insights.data: Everything is pictorial: agents are pixel faces, expert profiles are face-plus-text-line cards, the environment state is a house emoji (outline, broken, sparkling) and actions are tool emoji, with no tensors or text prompts.

figures.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation

arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'image input' and 'text input' under each tower
arrangement.losses_at: the contrastive loss between the two towers; ITM and MLM as boxes on top of the fusion encoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Inside one dashed cream container, an image encoder (12x) at lower left and a text encoder (x6) at lower right feed a central Image-Text Contrastive Loss box and a multimodal encoder (x6: self-attention, cross-attention, feed-forward) at upper right topped by ITM and MLM heads; a separate dashed yellow Momentum Model box sits outside on the right.
insights.data: Encoder outputs are rows of small 3-D cubes (green tokens with a yellow [CLS] cube at the end), and the contrastive box shows CLS cubes plus stacked negative cube rows with an ellipsis.
insights.emphasis: Layer sublayers are colour-coded (blue feed-forward, orange attention) and the momentum mechanism is pulled out as a big separate box linked by two fat coloured arrows (blue momentum update, orange momentum distillation) keyed in the right legend.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top: inputs enter at the bottom, encoders rise to token rows, rows go sideways into the contrastive box and up to the fusion encoder; a dashed arrow carries 'hard negatives' from the contrastive box to ITM.
insights.avoid: The legend and momentum box crowd the right edge and the momentum model is only a labelled box, so which modules it copies is not drawn.

figures.lesson: Put the objective that is the paper's idea where the two towers meet, before the module that fuses them, so the order of the title reads in the drawing.

figures.title: Anomaly Transformer: Time Series Anomaly Detection with Association Discrepancy

taxonomy.task: time-series anomaly detection via association discrepancy

arrangement.units: left: a rounded card with two horizontal tinted bands plus a pink objective column; right: a dashed box with a vertical block stack
arrangement.inputs_as: letter X with fan-out arrows
arrangement.losses_at: right side of the left panel (discrepancy column)
arrangement.shared: one Linear projection feeds both association branches

insights.structure: Left: a large card (stacked behind two ghost copies for multi-head) with an orange Prior-Association band over a blue Series-Association band and a pink Minimize/Maximize Discrepancy column at right; right, behind a vertical dashed separator, an L x block stack (Anomaly Attention, Add, Layer Norm, Feed Forward, Layer Norm) with 'Reconstruction' on top.
insights.data: The prior branch shows its Gaussian kernel as an explicit column vector of G(|j-i|; sigma) entries; Q, K, V and operations (MatMul, Scale, SoftMax, Rescale) are plain tilted text labels, not boxes.
insights.emphasis: The minimax objective gets its own pink column with red 'Minimize' and blue 'Maximize' text, and coloured Grad arrows with dashed Stop-Grad crossings show which branch each step updates.
insights.flow: Input X enters bottom-left, splits up into the two tinted bands left-to-right, and the V path runs along the bottom to an output Linear; the block-stack panel reads bottom-to-top.
insights.avoid: The tilted operation labels and crossing Stop-Grad curves in the middle are hard to parse, and the stacked ghost cards add clutter without labels.

figures.lesson: Paint two competing branches as full-width tinted bands and give their objective a separate column, with gradient arrows coloured like the band they update and grey bar-headed arrows for stopped gradients.

arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example sentences in italic inside pastel boxes, each headed by a bold underlined task name
arrangement.shared: the single Atlas hub and one retrieved-passage stack are drawn once and serve every task's arrows

insights.data: Inputs, outputs and the retrieved passage are all real sentences about one shared example (the Bermuda Triangle), italic in pastel boxes, so the retrieved text visibly contains the answers.

figures.title: Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas

taxonomy.task: pancreas segmentation with attention gates in skip connections

arrangement.units: one rounded frame with unenclosed blue (learned) and white glyph (fixed) boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: italic symbols g and x^l on incoming lines
arrangement.shared: x^l is used both as gate input and as the gated signal via a bottom skip

insights.structure: A single horizontal pipeline inside one rounded light-grey frame: two parallel 1x1x1 convolutions W_g (top) and W_x (bottom) merge at a plus node, then ReLU, psi 1x1x1, Sigmoid, Resampler, and a multiply node producing x_hat^l.
insights.data: Each tensor edge carries its shape as italic text below it (F_g x H_g x W_g x D_g etc.), and the nonlinearities and resampler are drawn as glyph boxes (ramp, S-curve, grid).
insights.emphasis: Learnable convolutions are the only blue-filled boxes, while parameter-free steps are white glyph boxes, so trainable parts stand out.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with hollow-triangle arrowheads; a long skip line runs along the bottom from x^l to the final multiply node, closing the gating.
insights.avoid: Tensor shape labels in small italic math crowd under every edge and some lack the multiply signs, making them hard to read.

figures.lesson: Draw each fixed nonlinearity as a white square holding a sketch of its curve (a ramp for ReLU, an S for sigmoid) and reserve the one tint for the learned 1x1x1 convolutions, so learned and fixed steps read apart without a legend.

figures.title: AudioLDM: Text-to-Audio Generation with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: text-to-audio generation, inpainting and style transfer

arrangement.units: three uncontained captioned panels of rounded coloured module boxes; (a) left full-height, (b) and (c) stacked on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: waveform thumbnails, spectrograms and quoted text prompts
arrangement.losses_at: centre-left of panel (a) (contrastive objective between audio and text encoders)
arrangement.shared: the same VAE, text encoder and latent diffusion modules reused in all three panels

insights.structure: Three captioned panels: a tall left panel (a) for training and sampling, and two stacked right panels (b) audio inpainting and (c) style transfer that reuse the same row of VAE Encoder, Text Encoder, Latent Diffusion and VAE Decoder boxes.
insights.data: Audio appears as blue waveforms and real magma-coloured mel spectrograms, text prompts as quoted bold sentences, embeddings E^x and E^y as vertical cell strips, and latents z_0 as small 3-D cuboids annotated with their R^{C x T/r x F/r} shapes.
insights.emphasis: Modules are colour-coded by role (blue encoders, yellow VAE with a small spectrogram icon, green Latent Diffusion), and the same colours repeat across panels so (b) and (c) read as reuses of (a).
insights.flow: Solid arrows mark training and dashed arrows sampling (legend under panel a); panel (a) runs top-to-bottom from audio to generated audio, panels (b)/(c) run left-to-right with dotted arrows.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) mixes solid, dashed and dash-dot grey arrows that cross around Latent Diffusion, and the latent shape formulas in tiny math add clutter.

figures.title: Autoformer: Decomposition Transformers with Auto-Correlation for Long-Term Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: long-term time-series forecasting with series decomposition

arrangement.units: two horizontal rounded containers (encoder above, decoder below) holding flat coloured blocks
arrangement.inputs_as: line-plot thumbnails of the input series and initialisations
arrangement.shared: encoder output feeds decoder cross auto-correlation

insights.structure: Two rounded containers stacked vertically: the Autoformer Encoder (N x) on top and a wider Autoformer Decoder (M x) below, each a row of Auto-Correlation, Series Decomp and Feed Forward blocks with add nodes; a decomposition example panel sits at top right.
insights.data: Inputs are small line-plot thumbnails (encoder input with a dashed 'To Predict' region, seasonal init with orange zero tail, trend-cyclical init with blue mean line), and a three-row plot at top right shows a series split into seasonal and trend parts.
insights.emphasis: Blocks are colour-coded by type (green Auto-Correlation, blue Series Decomp, pink Feed Forward), making the repeated decomposition blocks the dominant visual rhythm.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each container; the encoder output drops by an elbow line into the decoder's second Auto-Correlation, and the decoder's trend path runs as a separate bottom line accumulating at add nodes before the final Prediction.
insights.avoid: The decomposition example panel floats in the top-right corner unconnected to any block, and the K/V/Q micro-labels on block inputs are too small to read.

figures.lesson: Explain the decomposition block with a small stacked inset of the input series, its seasonal part and its trend part drawn as real curves, and draw the trend as a separate lower lane that accumulates each decomposition block's output through circled pluses.

figures.title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks

taxonomy.task: CTR prediction via self-attentive feature interaction

arrangement.units: unenclosed flat coloured cards and a weight column, no containers
arrangement.inputs_as: stacked blue embedding cards e_M and a single e_m
arrangement.shared: the same e_M stack is projected to both keys and values

insights.structure: One attention head drawn as a scatter: stacked blue feature-embedding cards e_M at top left, a single query embedding e_m at bottom left, projected into gold value cards (top right), grey key cards (middle) and a peach query card, which combine via curly braces into the output e~_m^(h) at right.
insights.data: Embeddings are flat coloured rectangles stacked like cards with dots for elision, and attention weights alpha are a vertical column of dark-gold cells with sample values 0.1, 0.8, ..., 0.02.

figures.lesson: Show attention over feature fields as a short column of small squares printed with example weights (0.1, 0.8, …, 0.02) between the keys and the values, braced together into the output, so the reader sees the weighting rather than reads about it.

figures.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration

taxonomy.note: architecture other: no network is drawn; the figure compares transformations of one weight matrix (round-to-nearest, mixed precision, per-channel scaling)

arrangement.units: three uncontained captioned panels of numeric/colour-shaded matrix grids
arrangement.inputs_as: FP16 weight matrix grid; activation matrix X below in (b),(c)
arrangement.shared: the same activation pattern X appears in (b) and (c)

insights.structure: Three side-by-side captioned panels (a) RTN quantization, (b) keep 1% salient weights in FP16, (c) scale before quantization, each built around a small weight matrix and, in (b) and (c), an activation matrix X multiplied into it.
insights.data: Weights are grids with printed numbers (cream FP16 values, blue INT3 integers), activations are pink grids whose shade marks magnitude with one salient red column, and the per-channel scale is a single pink row labelled alpha.
insights.emphasis: Captions carry perplexity in bold with colour (red 43.2 vs green 13.0), and in (b) one cream FP16 row inside the blue INT3 grid plus a red 'bad hardware efficiency' note marks the trade-off that (c) removes.
insights.flow: Read left to right as a progression of solutions; inside panels a dotted curved arrow goes from the salient activation column to the weight row and an 'average mag.' arrow leads up to the alpha row.
insights.avoid: The tiny numbers in every cell are unreadable at print size and add no information beyond the colour coding.

figures.lesson: Write the bit width as a coloured subscript on the matrix name (Q(W) INT3, MixPrec) and leave the high-precision channel as a differently tinted row inside the low-bit matrix, so precision is read from colour rather than from text.

figures.title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction

taxonomy.note: training 'other': redundancy-reduction objective that drives the cross-correlation matrix of two views' embeddings to the identity

arrangement.units: Two unframed horizontal lanes (branch A above, branch B below) separated by whitespace, sharing one input box at the left and one matrix comparison at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a white box labelled X (no photo); the two distortions are boxes Y^A, Y^B reached by arrows labelled T ~ calligraphic T
arrangement.losses_at: right end, after both lanes converge: matrix C, then a double arrow labelled L_BT, then target matrix I
arrangement.shared: the shared network is drawn once per lane as identical blue trapezoids; a single brace f_theta under the top lane names it

insights.structure: One input box forks into two stacked lanes, each data box -> blue encoder trapezoid -> smaller projector trapezoid -> embedding box, and both lanes meet at a cross-correlation grid followed by an identity grid at the far right.
insights.data: Images and embeddings are white outlined boxes with math symbols only (X, Y^A, Z^A), while the cross-correlation is drawn as an actual grey-level grid and the target as a black-diagonal grid, with 'feature dimension' marked by a double arrow under C.
insights.emphasis: The two matrices are the only picture-like elements and sit at the end of the reading path, joined by an L_BT double arrow, so the loss is the visual punchline.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: diagonal arrows fan out from X to the two lanes, run straight through the trapezoids, then converge diagonally into C; a dashed curved arrow rises from between encoder and projector to the 'Representations' label above.
insights.avoid: The labels 'Encoder' and 'Projector' sit only under the bottom lane while f_theta's brace sits under the top lane, so the naming is split across two places.

figures.lesson: Draw the loss as a picture of its target: render the computed cross-correlation as a noisy grey grid and the target as a clean identity grid side by side, linked by a double arrow carrying the loss symbol.

figures.title: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers

Bottom lane: patch row along the bottom edge with stacked encoder and head bars above it; the left column holds the input image, patch grid and masked grid as a vertical lead-in.

insights.structure: A top lane for the tokenizer (image -> tokenizer -> token-id grid -> dashed-boxed decoder) sits above a bottom lane where a flattened patch row feeds a wide encoder bar and a wide head bar, with a left column of labelled image stages leading down into the patch row.
insights.data: The input is a real photo cut into thumbnail patches, masked patches are flat grey squares and [M] cells, position embeddings are numbered blue cells with '+' between rows, and visual tokens are drawn as actual integer ids in a bracketed matrix.
insights.emphasis: The encoder is the widest and tallest shape with the model name in large type, and dashed green arrows — the only coloured lines — connect shaded target ids to the predictions at masked positions.
insights.flow: Reading starts top-left: right along the tokenizer row, down the left column through patching and masking, right along the bottom 'Flatten' arrow, then up through encoder and head, with green dashed arrows descending from the token grid.
insights.avoid: The decoder box is drawn at full prominence and only a small tag says it is unused, so it competes for attention with the pre-training path.

figures.lesson: Link prediction targets to their source with a distinct colour of dashed arrow (green here) that crosses from the tokenizer row to the head's outputs, and box the parts unused in pre-training with a dashed outline and a plain-language tag.

figures.title: BEiT v2: Masked Image Modeling with Vector-Quantized Visual Tokenizers

arrangement.units: unenclosed peach ViT boxes and yellow l2-norm pills; codebook in a dashed rounded box above
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo
arrangement.shared: one codebook used by both the lookup and the decoder input

insights.structure: A left-to-right pipeline: input bird photo -> ViT tokenizer encoder -> l2-norm -> nearest-neighbour lookup against a dashed codebook box at top -> grid of visual token ids -> ViT decoder -> semantic reconstruction feature map, with a Teacher box above the output.
insights.data: Patch features are grey bar stacks (N x D), codebook entries are coloured vertical bars v_1..v_k in a dashed rounded box, visual tokens are a 4x4 grid of integer ids, and the target is a dark heatmap of teacher features.
insights.emphasis: The codebook is set apart at the top in a dashed box with pastel bars, and a red curved arrow labelled 'Straight-Through Gradients' under the token grid singles out the non-differentiable quantization step.
insights.flow: Curved black arrows lead from photo to encoder and decoder to output; grey dashed arrows pass through the token grid, while the codebook feeds down through l2-norm into both lookup circles.
insights.avoid: Light grey annotation text ('Nearest Neighbor Lookup', 'Visual Tokens', shape labels) is too faint, and the Teacher's input is not drawn.

figures.lesson: Show vector quantisation by recolouring the feature bars: grey before the lookup, each bar in its codebook entry's colour after, with the codebook drawn as a row of the same coloured bars in a dashed container above.

figures.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

taxonomy.task: bidirectional language-model pretraining then task fine-tuning

arrangement.units: two light-grey rounded panels, 'Pre-training' (left) and 'Fine-Tuning' (right, a fanned stack of three task cards MNLI / NER / SQuAD), titled below each panel
arrangement.inputs_as: pink token tags ([CLS], Tok 1 ... Tok N, [SEP], Tok 1 ... Tok M) bracketed into two segments with a text label under each bracket and a blue arrow pointing at the pair description
arrangement.losses_at: on top of the unit they train: red block arrows above the output cells labelled NSP and Mask LM (pre-training) and Start/End Span (fine-tuning)
arrangement.shared: the same BERT box is drawn again in each panel; three dotted grey arrows connect the pre-training box to the stacked fine-tuning cards to show the weights carry over

insights.structure: Two grey rounded stage panels sit side by side, the right one fanned into three overlapping task cards, and each holds the same blue BERT box sandwiched between an embedding row and an output row.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as a row of pink tags under yellow embedding cells, with brackets grouping them into Sentence A / Sentence B (or Question / Paragraph) and green output cells along the top edge.
insights.emphasis: Red block arrows above the output row name each objective or head, making the heads the only coloured accent that changes between the two stages.
insights.flow: Within each panel the eye goes bottom-to-top (pair description, tokens, embeddings, BERT, heads), and three dotted arrows carry it left-to-right from pre-training into the stacked fine-tuning cards.
insights.avoid: The ghosted network of grey circles inside the BERT box is too faint to read and adds texture without information.

figures.lesson: Show fine-tuning on several tasks as a fanned stack of identical cards with only the front one drawn in full, so many downstream tasks cost the space of one.

figures.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer

taxonomy.note: modality is a sequence of item IDs from user interaction histories; 'tabular' is the closest list item

arrangement.units: four sub-figures captioned (a)-(d) below: (a), (c), (d) enclosed by dotted rectangles; (b) the proposed model unframed and widest; each panel holds a column-per-position stack of embedding and Trm/GRU boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: italic item ids v1 ... v_{t-1} and the literal [mask] token under each column, feeding pink+peach embedding boxes
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the predicted item v_t sits on top of the Projection box at the top of (b)
arrangement.shared: the Trm block is detailed once in (a) and reused as identical green 'Trm' boxes in (b) and (c); the same pink embedding boxes appear in all model panels

insights.structure: Four captioned sub-figures in a row: (a) the Transformer layer in a dotted frame at far left, (b) the proposed model large and unframed in the centre, (c) SASRec and (d) the RNN baseline stacked in dotted frames at right, all drawn as one column per sequence position.
insights.data: Inputs are italic item symbols v1 ... v_{t-1} and a literal [mask] under each column, turned into pink item-embedding and peach position-embedding boxes joined by bold '+' signs; outputs are hidden states h^L and the predicted item v_t on top.
insights.emphasis: The proposed model is the biggest, the only one without a frame, and the only one with a [mask] token and a bright green Projection head, while baselines reuse the same green Trm/pink embedding blocks so the difference is only in the arrow pattern (all-to-all vs left-to-right vs GRU chain).
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside every panel; between layers the arrows encode the attention direction (every block to every block in b, only to same/later positions in c, horizontal chain in d), and an L× brace at the left of (b) groups the repeated layers.
insights.avoid: The all-to-all crossing arrows between Trm rows in (b) form a dense thicket of diagonals, and the sideways 'Embedding Layer' label is hard to read; do not copy the crossing-arrow mesh for more than three columns.

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed sequence model and its baselines with identical blocks (same green Trm boxes, same pink item cells v1 … vt) so that the only visible difference is the connection pattern between positions: all-to-all for bidirectional, forward-only for causal, a chain for recurrent.

figures.title: Self-supervised Learning with Random-projection Quantizer for Speech Recognition

taxonomy.task: self-supervised speech pretraining with a random-projection quantizer
taxonomy.note: BEST-RQ = BERT-based speech pretraining; the frozen random projection + random codebook produces the discrete targets

arrangement.units: no enclosures; the encoder is a flat green box, the codebook a rounded white container titled 'codebook', branches separated only by space
arrangement.inputs_as: a real log-mel spectrogram strip at bottom left (and its masked copy above it)
arrangement.losses_at: implicit at the top: encoder arrows point into the row of target indices; no loss label
arrangement.shared: the same unmasked spectrogram feeds both the masking path and the Projection branch

insights.structure: Two unframed branches side by side: at left the learning path (raw spectrogram -> masked spectrogram -> green ASR Encoder), at right the target path (Projection box -> small orange vector -> rounded 'codebook' container), meeting at a row of integers across the top.
insights.data: Speech is drawn as real purple-orange spectrogram strips, with masked spans shown as flat light-grey blocks cut out of the second strip; targets are a literal row of code indices (897 139 23 4981 2750 6079) and the codebook is a row of grey vertical code-vector bars with an ellipsis.
insights.emphasis: The quantizer's novelty is marked by light-blue text 'random init, frozen' placed beside both the Projection box and the codebook, the only coloured annotation in the figure.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top on the left via hollow block arrows (Masking, encoder), a thin diagonal line from the unmasked spectrogram to Projection at bottom right, up through the codebook, and an 'index' line that loops over the top and drops onto the integer row, where encoder arrows point up at the masked positions.
insights.avoid: No loss is named: the reader must infer that the encoder arrows into the integer row are a prediction target, and the index line wraps around the top edge instead of feeding the targets directly; label the objective explicitly.

figures.lesson: Training status is written as a coloured margin note ('random init, frozen' in light blue) beside each frozen box, instead of a hatch pattern, lock icon or legend.

figures.title: BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers

arrangement.units: no containers; three standalone BEV grids and one stacked photo deck, each captioned beneath

insights.emphasis: The two attention mechanisms are colour-coded routes: blue 'Spatial Attention' through the camera images on top, green 'Temporal Attention' through the previous BEV below, each with a circled lens on the region attended.

insights.avoid: The top-row narration duplicates the paths with dotted drops to the grids, and the dark-grey camera deck is low contrast against the faint labels; as a teaser it shows no network blocks, so it cannot stand in for an architecture figure.

figures.lesson: Explain a BEV query with a question-and-answer line across the top ('What's in here at timestamp t?' -> 'There is a car!') whose dotted drop-lines pin both ends to the same black-outlined cell of the input and output BEV grids.

figures.title: BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers

taxonomy.task: BEV detection and segmentation from multi-camera images

arrangement.units: main unit (a) = input column + light-grey encoder rectangle with ×6; two detail units (b), (c) as dashed rounded containers on the right, each captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: real multi-camera photos around a car icon at bottom-left; History BEV and BEV Queries as cube grids under the encoder
arrangement.losses_at: none; a 'Det & Seg Heads' callout at the top of (a)
arrangement.shared: the camera feature planes and the BEV cube grids reappear in the detail panels (b) and (c)

insights.structure: (a) Overall Architecture fills the left two-thirds: a left column (six camera photos ringed around a top-view blue car, a three-pill backbone, a bracketed set of six coloured camera feature planes) feeding a light-grey encoder-layer block with ×6; (b) Spatial Cross-Attention and (c) Temporal Self-Attention are dashed rounded zoom panels stacked on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are real camera photos arranged around the ego car; camera features are flat coloured parallelograms; BEV maps (history B_{t-1}, queries Q, current B_t) are small 3-D cube grids in orange and blue; sampled reference points are coloured dots and triangles.
insights.emphasis: The two novel attention layers are the only tinted blocks in the encoder stack (beige Spatial Cross-Attention, gold Temporal Self-Attention), and each is zoomed by grey dashed lines into its own detail panel.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside the encoder (History BEV and BEV Queries enter at the bottom, Current BEV and a 'Det & Seg Heads' callout exit at top); camera features enter from the left on a long curved arrow; dashed zoom lines fan right into (b) and (c).
insights.avoid: The curved arrow from the feature planes to the cross-attention block is long and the zoom wedges cut across white space; the 3-D geometry in (b) packs pillars, points and hit-view circle with tiny math labels that are hard to read.

figures.lesson: Draw the BEV as an oblique slab of cube cells whose colour gives its role (blue = queries, peach = BEV at t-1 and t) and reuse those slabs in the zoomed detail panels, where one highlighted pillar of cells with sample points shows where a query looks into the camera features.

figures.title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation

taxonomy.task: multi-sensor BEV 3D detection and map segmentation

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; task heads are shown as output images
arrangement.shared: the BEV encoder and fused features are drawn once in the merged trunk feeding all heads

insights.structure: Camera and LiDAR branches run as two parallel rows of identical step types (encoder, features, view transform, BEV grid), converge diagonally into one stacked block in the middle, and a single shared trunk then forks into a right-hand column of task heads.
insights.data: Inputs and task outputs are real images (a stacked set of street photos, a black LiDAR sweep, a coloured BEV map, a LiDAR BEV with orange boxes), while intermediates are drawn as stacked sheets for 2D camera features and gridded 3-D cuboids for voxel and BEV features.
insights.emphasis: The fused BEV block stacks an orange camera grid on a blue LiDAR grid so the fusion is visible as geometry and colour, and every downstream element turns teal to mark the unified space.
insights.flow: Short thick black arrows run left to right along each row, two short diagonal arrows bring both BEV grids into the centre block, and a bracket-shaped arrow splits the fused features to the two head images at the right edge.
insights.avoid: The view-transform icons (a tiny frustum, a flatten press) are small black pictograms that are hard to decode at print size, and the elided heads are only a bare ellipsis between two images.

figures.lesson: Colour each sensor branch in its own family through every element and show fusion as the two coloured feature grids literally stacked into one block, then switch to a third colour for everything downstream.

figures.title: BiomedCLIP: a multimodal biomedical foundation model pretrained from fifteen million scientific image-text pairs

insights.flow: Panel C runs left to right from article to encoders to the similarity matrix, then a heavy grey arrow turns the flow downward into panel D's three side-by-side task vignettes.
insights.avoid: Half of the canvas is dataset histograms and a radial chart, so the method diagram is squeezed into a third of the height; and the product logos (PubMed, Azure) add brand noise that a method figure does not need.

figures.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

insights.flow: Left to right into the Q-Former, then bottom-to-top inside each tower; the image features enter cross-attention 'for every other block'; between the towers a labelled bundle (bidirectional / multimodal causal / uni-modal, the last dashed with x marks) shows the attention-masking choices.
insights.avoid: The horizontal three-line 'Attention Masking' bundle between the towers is cryptic (dashed line with x marks, a 'mutlimodal' typo) and only becomes clear after reading the right half.

figures.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

insights.emphasis: Frozen blocks are saturated blue with white snowflakes and the trainable Q-Former and projection pale yellow, so the small trainable bridge reads at a glance between large frozen parts.
insights.flow: Straight arrows run left to right through each row, and a curved arrow carries the projected query row down under the LLM bar before turning up into it.
insights.avoid: The grey variant-label cards at the far left take as much width as the image, which pushes the whole pipeline right; a short row title would save space.

figures.lesson: To show one adapter plugging into two kinds of backbone, repeat the identical row twice under a thin rule and let only the right-hand end differ, with a grey label card at each row's left naming the variant.

figures.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation

insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside each tower; one caption fans up to three towers; the image embedding runs along a line across the top of the figure and drops into the Cross Attention blocks of the two image-grounded towers.
insights.avoid: The image line runs over the top edge and crosses unit boundaries to reach two towers, and nothing in the figure states that matching colours mean shared parameters.

figures.lesson: One tower per objective, all the same shape, each with its loss on top and one shared input fanned out beneath them, makes several objectives read as a comparison.

figures.title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning

arrangement.units: Rows = the online and target branches as tinted bands (blue, red) labelled at the right; columns = the stages (view, representation, projection) as outlined frames spanning both rows, titled on top.

insights.data: Everything is a math symbol in a rounded box: input x, views v and v', representations y_θ / y'_ξ, projections z_θ / z'_ξ, prediction q_θ(z_θ); function names f, g, q label the arrows between columns.

insights.avoid: No real images: the input and views are bare symbols, so the augmentation idea is invisible; the prediction stage has no column frame while the other stages do.

figures.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society

figures.title: A Deep Cascade of Convolutional Neural Networks for Dynamic MR Image Reconstruction

figures.title: Crystal Diffusion Variational Autoencoder for Periodic Material Generation

arrangement.units: three unenclosed horizontal rows (denoising training, property prediction, generation) branching from one latent; only the property row has a grey dashed rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a dashed unit-cell square with coloured atoms labelled M = (A, X, L)
arrangement.losses_at: right end of the top two rows (L_Dec, L_Agg)
arrangement.shared: the latent z feeds all three rows; PGNN_Dec(M|z) appears in both the training and generation rows

insights.structure: Input crystal at left -> encoder -> a vertical latent bar z in the middle, from which three rows run right: top a noise-and-denoise row ending in L_Dec, middle a grey dashed box of predicted properties ending in L_Agg, bottom a Langevin-dynamics generation row.
insights.data: Every material is a dashed black square unit cell holding red and teal atom discs; the latent is a vertical strip of grey cells; the predicted composition, lattice and number of atoms are drawn as atom discs with 0.5, an empty dashed square and the number 4 joined by plus signs.
insights.emphasis: Arrow colour separates the two phases (black training, blue generation) explained by a two-entry legend; the generation row shows shrinking intermediate cells to convey iterative Langevin refinement.
insights.flow: Left to right from input to z, then fanning right into three parallel rows; a dashed 'Add noises' line loops over the top from the input to the noisy cell; a blue 'Rand. init.' arrow drops from the property box into the generation row.
insights.avoid: The legend is squeezed directly under the input cell and the long dashed noise arrow over the top crosses above everything; the rows have no enclosure, so training and generation rows are separated only by arrow colour.

figures.lesson: Draw the crystal as one reusable glyph — a dashed unit-cell square with a few two-colour atom discs — and repeat it for every state (input, noised, denoised, random start, mid-Langevin, generated), colouring arrows black for training and blue for generation with a two-line legend.

figures.title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking

arrangement.units: four unframed data stages, each captioned (a)-(d) at the bottom, separated by tall rounded network pills
arrangement.inputs_as: a real top-down lidar point-cloud render

insights.data: The input is a real top-down lidar render in magenta; map-view features are a grid of grey 3-D cubes with a few coloured cells; first-stage outputs are blue box outlines with red centre dots over a faded point cloud; second-stage features are a stack of coloured cubes feeding MLPs that output 'score 0.765' and a 3D box.
insights.emphasis: Feature colours tie stages together: the coloured cells sampled in the map-view grid reappear as the coloured cube stacks in the second stage, and two thick dark curved arrows show where they come from.
insights.flow: Left to right through the pills; the two heavy arcs run backwards from the second-stage stacks over the top and under the bottom into the map-view grid.
insights.avoid: The two backward arcs are the heaviest marks in the figure and dominate the forward pipeline; the caption '(a) Point. cloud' has a stray period.

figures.lesson: Colour the BEV feature cells that are sampled for each box and repeat those colours on the box-edge points and on the stacked per-box features, with thick dark curved arrows reaching back from the second stage to the grid.

insights.data: Inputs and outputs are drawn as the literal Q:/A: prompt text (the tennis-ball and cafeteria-apples problems), not as abstract boxes, with a red cross after the wrong answer and a green check after the right one.
insights.emphasis: Only the inserted reasoning sentences carry colour, as blue (exemplar) and green (generated) highlighter backgrounds in the right column, matching the blue Model Input and green Model Output pill tags.
insights.flow: Read left column then right column, each top to bottom from input to output; there are no arrows, the vertical stacking alone implies input-then-output.

figures.lesson: When the method is a change to text, show the same prompt twice side by side and mark only the inserted words with a highlighter background in the colour of the box tag they belong to.

figures.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development

taxonomy.task: role-playing LLM agents developing software through a phased chat chain

insights.emphasis: Colour is reserved for the agent sprites; the chain of solid arrows and loop glyphs in the middle row, with sprites above and below each loop, makes the instructor-assistant dialogue per subtask the figure's centre.
insights.flow: Everything reads left to right: hollow block arrows step through phases and subtasks in the top rows, and solid arrows run along the chat chain, with short vertical lines connecting each loop node up to its instructor and down to its assistant.
insights.avoid: Row labels (Instructor, Chat Chain, Assistant) are bold and larger than the content, and the Design phase box is the same width as its single subtask, so the phase-to-subtask nesting is only shown by faint dotted guides.

figures.lesson: Draw a multi-agent workflow as row lanes (phase, subtask, instructor, chain, assistant) so each chat step reads as one column: who instructs above, who answers below, and the artefact passed along on the chain.

figures.title: Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model

insights.data: Structures are rendered space-filling bead models coloured by chain region (blue, green, purple, magenta, red, yellow) consistently across snapshots; intermediate geometry in (b) is a faded copy with small three-colour axis triads at circled residues; conditions in (c) are small flat icons (symmetry pinwheel, helix, rabbit shape, CATH tiles).
insights.emphasis: Networks are never boxes: the two learned parts are triple-arrow transitions labelled 'Random Graph Neural Network' and 'Equivariant Geometry Solver', so the structures carry the figure.

insights.avoid: Seven near-identical blob renders take much of the width while the method steps in (b) get small text; the photo-like renders make the figure heavy and hard to reproduce as vector art.

figures.lesson: Draw generation and training as one row of structure snapshots under two opposed full-width arrows, then zoom one snapshot with a translucent wedge into a lower panel showing a single denoising step, with the intermediate geometry (residue frames) overlaid on a faded copy of the structure.

figures.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series

taxonomy.task: probabilistic time-series forecasting with a language model
taxonomy.note: Chronos tokenizes scaled, quantized values and trains an off-the-shelf LM (T5 family) with cross-entropy over bins.

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by full-height thin vertical rules, each titled in large bold text at its top
arrangement.inputs_as: a raw blue line plot ('Historical Time Series') at top-left; the other columns start from the context-token row at their top
arrangement.losses_at: the cross-entropy is a dotted vertical link labelled 'cross entropy' between the predicted-probability histogram and a pink 'Next Token ID' cell at the bottom of the Training column
arrangement.shared: the context-token row and the language-model box are redrawn identically in Training and Inference

insights.structure: Three stage columns separated by thin vertical rules and titled in bold at the top (Time Series Tokenization, Training, Inference); Training and Inference share an identical skeleton of context-token row -> pink 'Time Series Language Model' box -> output box.
insights.data: The input is a blue line plot, quantization is drawn as small squares on the curve dropping grey leaders onto a tick-marked number line, tokens are blue cells with integer IDs (2400, 2142 ...) in a light-blue rounded bar, predicted probabilities are a purple histogram on the number line, and the forecast is a red line with a shaded uncertainty band.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the role: blue = observed context tokens, pink/red = model and predicted/sampled tokens and forecast; the same numbered token row reappears in all three columns so tokenization visibly feeds training and inference.
insights.flow: Each column reads top to bottom with straight vertical arrows; columns read left to right; step names (Mean Scaling, Quantization, Dequantization and Unscaling) are rotated purple labels on each column's left edge.
insights.avoid: The many grey quantization leaders from curve squares to the number line cross each other and are hard to follow; the token row is drawn three times identically, spending space.

figures.lesson: Keep one colour for observed context (blue curve, blue tokens) and one for predictions (pink tokens, red forecast curve with an uncertainty band), and print each token's actual integer ID inside its square so the quantization is concrete.

figures.title: ClimaX: A foundation model for weather and climate

insights.flow: Left to right along the strip; arcs run over the top, one hue per patch position, without arrowheads.
insights.avoid: Arcs overlap and cross each other between groups and have no arrowheads or target, so what the aggregation produces is not shown; the figure is unreadable without its caption.

figures.lesson: Show aggregation across variables at one location by drawing one coloured arc per patch position that links the matching patches in every variable group, with the groups named by brackets underneath.

figures.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

insights.emphasis: Only the diagonal cells of the matrix (and the chosen I1·T3 cell in panel 3) are tinted blue, so the positive pairs / prediction pop out; encoder colour (lilac text, green image) is kept consistent across all panels.
insights.flow: Left to right with orthogonal bus lines fanning from each encoder to its embedding cells; panel (2) flows into (3) top to bottom via the shared T row.
insights.avoid: Panels have no frames and (2)/(3) share space tightly, so where panel (2) ends is ambiguous; the ellipsis cells pad the matrix but carry no information.

figures.lesson: Colour each loss name with the hue of the module it trains (orange 'Contrastive Loss' beside the peach encoders, blue 'Captioning Loss' over the blue decoder), so objectives attach to modules without extra lines or a legend.

figures.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

figures.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

figures.title: CSDI: Conditional Score-based Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation

figures.title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks

insights.avoid: Purely abstract: no example images, so the reader must already know what domains mean; monochrome styling gives no colour distinction between G and F.

figures.lesson: Give each loss its own panel of the same structure, so the reader compares the panels instead of untangling one diagram.

insights.avoid: Many lines cross with small hop-over bumps near the concat nodes, making the Q/K routing hard to trace; the legend at bottom right uses shape (rectangle vs pill) that is not visually distinct enough.

figures.lesson: Separate variables from modules by corner shape (square vs rounded, stated in a two-entry legend) and keep the refined state - here the anchor box - in one colour from input to updated output so its path through the layer can be traced.

figures.title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation

arrangement.units: Four identical square matrices side by side, one per attention-mask variant, enclosed only by their own grid edges, each with an (a)-(d) sub-caption below.
arrangement.inputs_as: none drawn; the token sequence is implicit in the matrix rows and columns
arrangement.shared: the 6-token text block on the left of every matrix is identical across panels

insights.structure: Four same-size square mask matrices in a single row, separated by whitespace, each with a lettered sub-caption beneath.
insights.data: Each mask is a binary grid of cream (attend) and dark navy (masked) cells, with thicker grid lines marking the text block and each image row.
insights.emphasis: Only the shape of the cream region changes between panels, so the variant's sparsity pattern is the sole thing that draws the eye.
insights.flow: Read panel by panel left to right; within a panel, the lower-left triangle shows causal order with no arrows.
insights.avoid: No axis labels mark which rows are text and which are image tokens, so the 6+16 split must be learned from the caption.

figures.lesson: Several attention-sparsity variants compare best as identical square binary matrices in a row, two flat colours only, so the reader's eye goes straight to the differences in the allowed band.

figures.title: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language

insights.data: Each modality shows one real sample: a dog photo, a grey waveform and the sentence 'I like tea with milk'; the student row shows the same samples with a grey square pasted over part of each (photo region, waveform span, the word 'with').
insights.emphasis: Only the teacher's top layers are filled blue and gathered by a curly brace, marking that the target is the average of the top-K layer outputs, while the student's layers stay hollow.
insights.flow: Inputs flow left to right by solid arrows only from the Language column into each model; dashed grey arrows go up from the student to the brace ('Predict model representation of original input') and loop round the right side back to the teacher ('Teacher tracks student parameters').
insights.avoid: Only the Language column is wired to the models, so images and speech appear to float unconnected; draw one shared entry for all modalities instead.

figures.lesson: One mid-grey square is used as the mask glyph in every modality (over the image, in the waveform, in place of a word), so a single visual idea carries the claim that the same masking applies across inputs.

figures.title: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a single brown output circle at the top
arrangement.shared: the embedding layer x0 feeds both cross and deep towers in the right panel

insights.avoid: The labels 'Deep Netwrok' are misspelt twice and the two variants carry no (a)/(b) titles, so the panels must be told apart from the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw each layer's vector as a row of circles in a dashed pill, coloured by role (dense/sparse input, embedding, cross, deep) with one legend, and route the x0 skip line up the side into every ⊗ so the cross structure reads without text.

figures.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions; one row of nodes
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey node x_T with a pure-noise thumbnail below it
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Six circular nodes in a single horizontal row, x_T on the left to x_0 on the right, with ellipsis arrows hiding the intermediate steps.
insights.data: Each sampled state is a small square image thumbnail tucked under its node, going from pure noise under x_T to a partly denoised face under x_{t-1} to a clean face under x_0.
insights.emphasis: The one expanded step x_t -> x_{t-1} carries the only equation labels: p_theta solid above and q dashed below, so the two distributions the paper defines are the focus.
insights.flow: Read left to right along the generative direction; the only backward line is the dashed forward-noising arc curving under the highlighted step.
insights.avoid: The data node x_0 is drawn white while all other nodes are grey with no key, and the thumbnails sit off-centre beside the nodes, so the mapping of image to node is loose.

figures.lesson: Explain an iterative process by drawing the whole chain with ellipses and labelling only one representative step, with the learned direction solid above and the fixed direction dashed below.

figures.title: Is Conditional Generative Modeling all you need for Decision-Making?

taxonomy.task: offline decision-making by conditional state-sequence generation

arrangement.units: Three unframed token rows at fixed column positions, separated by two module boxes (a wide diffusion bar, a narrow inverse-dynamics box).
arrangement.inputs_as: condition tabs (returns / constraints / skills) plus the filled blue history tokens
arrangement.shared: token columns align across all three rows so each step can be traced vertically

insights.structure: Three identical rows of state/action tokens (s_{t-2}, a_{t-2} ... s_{t+h}) stacked vertically, with a full-width orange 'state diffusion' bar between rows 1 and 2 and a smaller pink 'inverse dynamics' box between rows 2 and 3.
insights.data: Known past tokens are filled blue (states darker than actions), unknown future tokens are dashed white boxes, and future states being denoised are drawn as pixelated noisy squares in the top row and pale-blue solid boxes once generated.
insights.emphasis: The conditioning chips 'returns', 'constraints', 'skills' sit as tabs above, with only 'returns' active (dark border) and the other two greyed out, and the two module names are coloured to match their boxes.
insights.flow: Top to bottom: returns curves down into the diffusion bar, past states drop into it, generated s_{t+1..t+h} drop to row 2, then s_t and s_{t+1} feed inverse dynamics, whose red arrow fills a_t in row 3.
insights.avoid: The noisy-state pattern is tiny and faint, so the noise-to-sample idea is easy to miss at print size.

figures.lesson: Draw the same token row once per stage and change only each token's box treatment (filled for known, dashed for unknown, noise texture for being denoised, pale fill for just generated), so the stack shows the process without step labels.

figures.title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

taxonomy.task: offline reinforcement learning as return-conditioned sequence modelling

arrangement.units: horizontal rows stacked bottom to top (tokens, embeddings, transformer band, decoders, outputs), unframed except the transformer band
arrangement.inputs_as: circled symbols R-hat_t, s_t, a_t, with concrete examples under the last triple: a grey tile showing the number 21 (return), an Atari game frame (state) and a D-pad with one dark arm (action), each named in grey
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn; predicted a_{t-1}, a_t circles sit above the decoders at the top
arrangement.shared: the linear decoder is drawn as two identical orange bars above the two state positions

insights.data: Inputs are circled letters in R-s-a order, embeddings are bars coloured by token type (blue return, green state, yellow action), and only the last triple gets concrete thumbnails underneath (a '21' tile, a game frame, a D-pad icon).
insights.emphasis: The transformer is the largest element with bold serif type, and the orange decoders appear only above state tokens, which shows at a glance where actions are predicted.
insights.flow: Straight vertical arrows run bottom-to-top through every column; tick marks on the band's top and bottom rules align each input column with its output.
insights.avoid: Row names ('linear decoder', 'emb. + pos. enc.') are in very light grey at the far right and are easy to miss against the coloured content.

figures.lesson: Lay out a sequence model as one wide band over a row of type-coloured token bars, name each row at the right margin in grey, and show one concrete example (a number, a game frame, a joystick) under the last tokens to ground the abstract symbols.

figures.title: Deep Image Prior

taxonomy.task: image restoration with an untrained network prior
taxonomy.note: architecture other: a randomly initialised generator f_theta(z) whose weights are optimised per image by gradient descent (the hourglass network itself is shown only in the appendix Fig. 21). training other: per-image fitting to the single degraded observation, no training dataset.

arrangement.units: One unframed composition of three identical rows (one per iteration), separated by whitespace, with the shared inputs at the top corners.
arrangement.inputs_as: real images: a grey random-noise patch z at the top left and the degraded photo x_0 at the top right, each sending grey dotted lines down to every row
arrangement.losses_at: in each row, an energy box E(f(z); x_0) at the right end of the forward path, with its gradient dE/dtheta box just below it
arrangement.shared: z and x_0 are drawn once and fan into every row along dotted grey lines; the weights theta are one orange vertical axis updated at circled plus nodes

insights.structure: Three identical rows stacked top to bottom, one per gradient step, each holding a weight node, a generated image and an energy box, with the two fixed inputs drawn once in the top corners.
insights.data: Every image is a real thumbnail: the noise code z and the degraded zebra x_0 at the corners, and in the middle column the generator output turns from coloured noise to a blurry zebra to a sharp zebra across the three rows.
insights.emphasis: Colour is used by role, not by module: orange for the weights theta (large orange labels on a vertical axis), blue for forward generation, dark red for gradients, grey dotted for constant inputs.
insights.flow: Each row runs left to right in blue to the energy box, the dark red gradient returns right to left beneath it to a circled plus, and the orange axis carries the updated weights down to the next row, so the loop reads as a downward zigzag.
insights.avoid: Grey dotted lines from z and x_0 run along both outer edges and cross under the rows to every iteration, adding long low-contrast lines that compete with the main zigzag.

figures.lesson: Unroll an optimisation loop into a few identical rows and let the intermediate outputs in one column change visibly from row to row, colour-coding the forward, gradient and parameter-update paths so the loop reads without boxes.

figures.title: DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction

arrangement.inputs_as: rows of light-blue circles with one yellow active circle per field, labelled Field i / j / m
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a sigmoid glyph in the Output Units box is the prediction

insights.emphasis: Red 'Weight-1' arrows trace the FM path from embeddings to inner-product nodes and on to the output, standing out against the black normal connections of the deep part.
insights.flow: Teal arrows rise from each active feature to its embedding, then red and black lines fan upward to the two components, and both converge on the sigmoid output at top right.
insights.avoid: Red and black lines cross densely between the embeddings and the two components, and the low-resolution monospace labels look rough next to the glyphs.

figures.lesson: Give the parameter-free path its own line colour (red weight-1 arrows) and decode it in a small glyph-and-line legend, so the two components sharing one embedding layer stay distinguishable.

figures.title: DeepONet: Learning nonlinear operators for identifying differential equations based on the universal approximation theorem of operators

insights.emphasis: All learned networks share one lavender fill, and the bottom panels differ only in the branch side (p stacked branch nets vs one branch net fanning out to p outputs), so the stacked/unstacked distinction is the visible difference.
insights.flow: Each panel reads left to right: the branch path runs along the top and the trunk path along the bottom, and both columns' outputs slant down/up into a circled multiply that emits G(u)(y) on the right.
insights.avoid: Panels have no frames and the panel B curves are loosely placed with ellipses (vertical dots) for 'more samples', so B reads as a sketch next to the tidy block diagrams.

figures.lesson: State the problem as a single black-box panel first, then redraw that box as the proposed two-network decomposition in the panels below, using the same fill for every learned network so the reader maps the black box onto its parts.

figures.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

taxonomy.task: MoE layer design for language models

arrangement.inputs_as: a two-circle 'Input Hidden' box
arrangement.shared: identical input/router/output skeleton repeated in all three panels so only the expert row changes

insights.data: Hidden states are two-circle boxes (Input Hidden, Output Hidden), experts are numbered rounded rectangles, and the router's scores are a tiny yellow bar chart labelled K = 2 / 4 / 3.
insights.emphasis: The shared expert in (c) is the only green box and bypasses the router with its own solid line from the input, while a corner legend names blue = Routed Expert, green = Shared Expert.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in each panel: input to router, solid black lines to selected experts, yellow dashed curves carry gate weights to circled-x multipliers, then a circled-plus sums into the output; panels read left to right as an ablation progression.
insights.avoid: The many crossing yellow dashed gate curves in (b) and (c) tangle with the black routing lines; route gate weights more simply if copying.

figures.lesson: Build the proposed layer as the last of a row of identical templates, each adding one change, so the reader sees exactly what differs (twice as many narrower experts, then one green always-on expert), and write the number of selected experts K under each router.

figures.title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection

arrangement.units: An unframed input pyramid, then a dashed Encoder frame and a dashed Decoder frame, each with an inner grey dashed 'x 4' repeat box.

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the output is a photo with coloured bounding boxes above the decoder
arrangement.shared: repeated layers collapsed into a grey dashed box marked x 4 in both encoder and decoder

insights.flow: Purple dashed lines run from sampled points on the pyramid up into a reference dot in the encoder; the encoder output is braced and sent right by red dashed lines into every decoder layer, which reads bottom to top to the predictions.
insights.avoid: Dozens of crossing purple dashed lines over the faded photos make the encoder busy; fewer samples would show the mechanism just as well.

figures.lesson: Draw sparse attention by putting the sampling points as small coloured glyphs directly on faded, tilted copies of the input photo at each scale, with dashed arrows from them to the query's reference point.

figures.title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention

arrangement.losses_at: top corners: L_CE above the class token, L_teacher above the distillation token

figures.title: Dynamic Graph CNN for Learning on Point Clouds

figures.title: DiffDock: Diffusion Steps, Twists, and Turns for Molecular Docking

arrangement.units: Three unframed columns separated by thin vertical rules, each with a header label; the middle column holds three time-step snapshots.
arrangement.inputs_as: a 2D ligand structure drawing above a grey protein surface render
arrangement.shared: the same protein surface render repeated across snapshots

insights.structure: Three columns divided by vertical rules: inputs (ligand graph and protein surface) at the left, the DiffDock process as three snapshots of the protein surface at t=T, intermediate and t=0 in the middle, and the top two ranked poses on the right.

figures.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion

figures.lesson: Draw each policy class as the same tiny block diagram (input circle, grey box with its equation, output circle) and pair it with a plot of what it learns on one shared toy target, so the panels compare both the computation and its result.

figures.title: Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs
