insights.data: Inputs are bold italic math with superscripts entering from panel tops, plus two small basis-function thumbnails (radial curves, spherical heat-map) feeding the model column; every layer box shows its formula with an empty square as the input slot.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only nested inset in the figure, a pale-blue labelled box inside the largest blue panel.
insights.flow: Each panel reads top to bottom with thin orthogonal arrows, while per-block outputs exit right through small tan Output boxes toward the Model column's sum circle.
insights.avoid: The Interaction panel has several long parallel input lines on its left edge running down to its bottom Output box, crossing the inset's border and making it hard to tell which input feeds which operation.

figures.lesson: Writing each layer as its formula inside the box (sigma(W box + b), with a square as the input slot) lets detail panels show exact computation with no separate equations, and colour-matching each block type between the model stack and its panel removes zoom lines.

figures.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction

taxonomy.note: architecture other = target attention: a candidate-ad-conditioned attention pooling over user behaviour embeddings

arrangement.units: Two unframed model panels (Base Model, Deep Interest Network, titled at the bottom) plus a double-bordered inset detailing the Activation Unit.
arrangement.inputs_as: coloured ID circles grouped by feature field (User Profile, User Behaviors Goods 1..N, Candidate Ad, Context)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; Output box at the top
arrangement.shared: the embedding layer and MLP tower drawn identically in both panels

insights.structure: Base Model on the left and Deep Interest Network in the middle share the same bottom-up skeleton (feature groups -> embeddings -> pooling -> concat -> MLP), with a double-bordered inset at top right expanding the Activation Unit.
insights.data: IDs are coloured circles (orange goods, blue shop, pink category, white other), embeddings are short multi-coloured vertical strips, pooled vectors are horizontal coloured cell bars, and FC layers are grey labelled boxes ('PReLU (200)').
insights.emphasis: DIN's change is the row of double-bordered Activation Unit boxes, each emitting a 'Goods i Weight' into a red X product circle before SUM Pooling, fed by a line from the candidate ad; the rest is identical to the base model so the difference pops.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in both models; the candidate ad embedding runs horizontally under the activation units to every behaviour, and the user-profile/context branches go straight up to Concat & Flatten.
insights.avoid: Small text and a dense tangle of thin grey arrows around the activation units make the middle panel hard to read at column width.

figures.lesson: Draw each input feature field as a coloured ID dot whose colour carries into its embedding cells, so the concatenated vectors further up visibly show which fields they mix and one small legend of dot colours explains the whole input side.

figures.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers

arrangement.units: Two unframed vertical branches (student, teacher) of stacked boxes, side by side.
arrangement.inputs_as: a single circled x splitting into two circled views x1, x2
arrangement.losses_at: top centre, as a text formula between p1 and p2
arrangement.shared: teacher is an EMA of the student, shown by a horizontal 'ema' arrow between the network boxes

insights.structure: Two mirrored vertical branches, student on the left and teacher on the right, rising from a single input x at the bottom centre that splits into two views x1 and x2.
insights.data: Variables (x, x1, x2, p1, p2) are circles, networks are grey-filled boxes (student g_theta_s, teacher g_theta_t), and post-processing steps are white boxes (softmax; centering + softmax on the teacher).
insights.emphasis: Asymmetry between the branches is the point: only the teacher has an extra 'centering' box and a double-slash 'sg' stop-gradient mark, and a horizontal 'ema' arrow runs from student to teacher.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: x splits by two diagonal arrows into the views, each passes up its branch to p1 / p2, and the cross-entropy 'loss: - p2 log p1' is written as text between the two outputs at the top.
insights.avoid: The loss is only floating text with no lines joining p1 and p2, so the comparison point is implied rather than drawn.

figures.lesson: Draw the two networks as identical grey boxes and mark everything that makes them differ as small inline glyphs on the teacher column (an extra head box, an sg double slash on its output edge, an 'ema' arrow from the student), so the asymmetry is readable without colour.

figures.title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection

arrangement.units: one unframed composition: a grey slab between a row of input query cells and a row of output cells, grouped by brackets into two CDN groups; a separate square inset on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: rows of two-part query cells coloured by positive/negative, bracketed and labelled 'positive'/'negative' and 'CDN group0/1'
arrangement.losses_at: grey label boxes on top of each output group ('reconstruction loss', 'no object')
arrangement.shared: one decoder slab shared by both CDN groups

insights.structure: One wide grey 'Decoder Layers x M' slab spans the left of the figure, with a row of query cells below it and a matching row of output cells above it, both split into two 'CDN group' sets of three positive and three negative queries; a separate square inset sits to the right.
insights.data: Each query is a two-part cell (yellow or olive-brown top over a peach bottom); outputs reuse the same cells, and grey rounded label boxes above them name the target ('reconstruction loss' over positives, 'no object' over negatives).
insights.emphasis: The positive/negative idea is carried only by two fills, yellow and olive-brown, which the inset reuses as a yellow 'positive' square nested inside an olive 'negative' square, with lambda_1 and lambda_2 tick marks for the two noise radii.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: thin black arrows go up from each query into the slab and up again from each output to its label box; the inset has no arrows into the main drawing.
insights.avoid: The inset sits unlabelled and unconnected far to the right, so a reader must work out alone that it explains how the noise ranges make positive and negative boxes; the decoder is a featureless grey slab.

figures.lesson: Encode the two query kinds by one fill each and reuse exactly those fills in a small nested-square inset that shows the noise ranges, so the inset explains the main drawing's colour code.

figures.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

taxonomy.task: automatic curation of a pretraining image dataset (embedding, deduplication, retrieval)
taxonomy.note: family 'other': the figure draws a dataset-curation pipeline for self-supervised pretraining (DINOv2), not a network; training 'other': no training is drawn, the stages are embedding similarity, deduplication and nearest-neighbour retrieval

arrangement.units: Three stage columns (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval) separated by dashed vertical rules, each holding three rows of photo-plus-embedding glyphs; open whitespace on both ends holds the input and output cylinders.
arrangement.inputs_as: two stacked database cylinders (grey uncurated, orange curated) containing real photo thumbnails
arrangement.losses_at: none: a data pipeline with no objective
arrangement.shared: the curated stream is a single long black arrow along the bottom row running through all stages to the retrieval query frame, rather than repeated per stage

insights.structure: Input cylinders on the left and an output cylinder on the right bracket three stage columns split by dashed vertical rules, with bold stage names lined up along the bottom.
insights.data: Every sample is a real food/car photo with a small strip of cells attached as its embedding, and datasets are flat cylinders whose fill colour (grey vs orange) encodes uncurated vs curated.
insights.emphasis: The effect of each stage is drawn on the samples themselves: red X marks over removed duplicates, faded thumbnails for unretrieved images, and a heavy rounded frame around the curated query.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with thick black block arrows entering each column row, and one long thin arrow along the bottom carrying the curated image through to the query frame, from which a short up arrow points to its retrieved neighbours.
insights.avoid: The same ratatouille photo repeats about ten times with only small crop differences, so tracking which copy is which takes effort; distinct samples would read faster.

figures.lesson: Show a data-filtering pipeline by carrying the same real thumbnails through every stage and marking their fate in place (red X for dropped, faded for not retrieved, a heavy frame for the query) instead of drawing process boxes.

figures.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers

arrangement.units: an unframed overview column, then three equal tall rounded panels, one per block variant; the chosen variant outlined in black, the alternatives greyed
arrangement.inputs_as: grey 'Noised Latent' box with tensor size, and small blue 'Timestep t' and 'Label y' boxes; in the block panels 'Input Tokens' and 'Conditioning' boxes at the bottom edge
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs Noise and Sigma boxes at the top of the overview
arrangement.shared: the same layer-type colours across all four columns; dashed zoom lines from the overview's DiT Block to the chosen panel

insights.structure: An unframed bottom-to-top overview column on the left (Noised Latent, Patchify, DiT Block x N, Layer Norm, Linear and Reshape, Noise and Sigma) is followed by three equal-height rounded panels, each showing one DiT block variant, all titled underneath.
insights.data: Tensors are grey-lavender rounded boxes carrying their shape in small text (32 x 32 x 4); timestep and label are small blue boxes feeding an Embed box beside Patchify.
insights.emphasis: The chosen adaLN-Zero block panel has a black outline, grey fill and fully saturated colours, while the cross-attention and in-context panels are drawn in faded grey outlines and washed-out fills, and two dashed lines fan from the overview's DiT Block into the chosen panel.
insights.flow: Every column reads bottom to top with short vertical arrows; residual paths loop up the left side of each block panel into circled plus nodes, and conditioning enters from the right through a vertical line with alpha, gamma, beta labels.
insights.avoid: The faded alternative panels are so light that their labels are hard to read in print; layer-type colours (blue norm, orange attention, green MLP) are never explained by a legend.

figures.lesson: Rejected design variants are drawn at the same size and layout as the chosen one but uniformly faded to pale grey and pastel, so the reader sees the winner first and can still compare structures column by column.

figures.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?

taxonomy.task: long-term time-series forecasting with a linear map over time
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other': a single linear layer mapping the L-step history window directly to the T-step forecast window

arrangement.units: one rounded red-outlined frame holding a bottom-left row of L history nodes and a top-right row of T future nodes, offset horizontally, with a dashed vertical boundary at the end of the history row
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of grey circle nodes, one per history timestep, named by a curly bracket below
arrangement.shared: weight sharing across variates is not drawn

insights.structure: Two node rows sit offset inside one rounded frame, history low on the left and future high on the right, so the time axis reads left to right and the mapping rises diagonally.
insights.data: Timesteps are drawn as identical grey circles and the weight matrix as a dense fan of thin lines from every history node to every future node, with no numbers or values.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is highlighted; the bare bipartite drawing itself conveys how little machinery the baseline uses.
insights.flow: Lines run diagonally up and right from the history row to the future row, and a dashed vertical line marks where observed time ends.
insights.avoid: The fan of lines is so dense that individual connections merge into a dark wedge, and the drawing never shows the trend/seasonal decomposition that distinguishes the paper's DLinear variant.

figures.lesson: A fully connected linear map over time can be shown as two offset node rows (history low-left, future high-right) joined by a fan of thin lines, with brackets naming each row's length symbol.

figures.title: Beyond a Gaussian Denoiser: Residual Learning of Deep CNN for Image Denoising

taxonomy.task: blind Gaussian image denoising via residual (noise) prediction
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a plain feed-forward stack of conv layers predicting the residual noise (no skips, no encoder-decoder)

arrangement.units: one unframed row: input photo, five layer boxes with ellipsis gaps, output image
arrangement.inputs_as: a large real noisy photo titled 'Noisy Image'
arrangement.shared: none; repeated middle layers are drawn as identical blue boxes separated by '...'

insights.structure: A single unframed row runs from a noisy photo through a yellow first layer, repeated blue middle layers separated by '...', and an orange last layer to an output image.
insights.data: Input and output are both large square images the height of the layer boxes: a real noisy butterfly on the left and a grey pure-noise 'Residual Image' on the right.
insights.emphasis: The residual-learning contribution is shown only by the output being the noise rather than a clean image; the first and last layers are separated from the body by distinct yellow and orange fills.
insights.flow: Straight left-to-right with short blue arrows of equal length; '...' marks where layers are omitted.
insights.avoid: Nothing tells the reader the residual is subtracted from the input to give the clean image, and the layer count/depth is not stated in the drawing.

figures.lesson: Make the learning target visible by drawing the actual output (here a pure-noise residual image) at the same size as the input photo, so the reader sees what the network predicts without reading a word.

figures.title: 3D Diffusion Policy: Generalizable Visuomotor Policy Learning via Simple 3D Representations

taxonomy.task: visuomotor imitation learning from 3D point clouds

arrangement.units: two tinted rounded panels on top (training, evaluation), two dashed zoom panels below for the Perception and Decision modules, each titled in bold at its top
arrangement.inputs_as: green database cylinders for demonstrations; a real point-cloud photo at the left edge of the Perception panel
arrangement.shared: the Perception + Decision pair drawn identically in both top panels; Compact 3D Repr. box passed from the Perception panel into the Decision panel

insights.structure: A top row of two pale lavender panels, '(a) End-to-End Training' and '(b) Evaluation', each holding the same Perception trapezoid + Decision box policy; a bottom row of two dashed-outline zoom panels expands Perception (wide, left) and Decision (narrow, right).
insights.data: Expert demonstrations are green cylinders, the point cloud is a real single-view photo then cropped robot points then rainbow height-coloured points, layers are thin vertical colour bars with sizes like (3, 64, 128, 256), and actions are small blue squares a_t^K to a_t^0.
insights.emphasis: The two zoom panels' dashed outlines take the colours of their parents (light cyan for Perception, dark blue for Decision), and dashed wedge lines run from each top-row shape down to its panel.
insights.flow: Top row reads left to right with thick soft-coloured arrows, the evaluation panel closes a loop (Observation up the left, Action down the right to Environment); the bottom row reads left to right, with a grey dashed arrow carrying the Compact 3D Repr. from the Perception panel into the Decision panel.
insights.avoid: The bottom panels carry their own '(a) Point Cloud Processing' / '(b) Compact 3D Representations' sub-labels that clash with the top row's (a)/(b), and the U-Net is a cramped cluster of tiny bars.

figures.lesson: Draw the policy once as a perception trapezoid plus decision box inside an Observation -> Environment -> Action loop, then zoom each half into its own dashed panel whose outline colour matches that half.

figures.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

taxonomy.task: aligning language models to human preferences
taxonomy.note: architecture other: pipeline comparison, no network architecture drawn

arrangement.units: two rounded tinted panels, one per method, bold title in the top-left corner, no inner boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: speech-bubble icons for the preferred and dispreferred completions under a quoted example prompt
arrangement.losses_at: objective names in bold colour under each arrow
arrangement.shared: the same preference-data drawing repeated at the left of both panels; teal 'maximum likelihood' repeated

insights.structure: Two rounded tinted panels side by side: a wide pink 'RLHF' panel (preference data -> reward model <-> LM policy) and a narrower teal 'DPO' panel (preference data -> final LM), so the shorter pipeline is visibly the shorter panel.
insights.data: Preference data is two speech-bubble icons (y_w with a trophy, y_l) joined by a greater-than sign under a quoted prompt 'write me a poem about the history of jazz'; models are faint node-and-edge network glyphs with their names written large over them.
insights.emphasis: Each step's objective is written below its arrow in bold colour: 'maximum likelihood' in the same teal in both panels and 'reinforcement learning' in red only in the RLHF panel, and the DPO panel takes the teal tint.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel with thick black straight arrows; in RLHF two curved arrows form a loop labelled 'label rewards' and 'sample completions'.
insights.avoid: The network glyphs are so faint they read as background texture, so the models are recognised only by their text labels.

figures.lesson: Name the training objective under each arrow in bold coloured words, the same colour for a step both pipelines share and a contrasting colour for the step only the baseline needs, so the reader sees what was removed without a legend.

figures.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems

taxonomy.task: solving noisy (non)linear inverse problems with a pretrained diffusion prior
taxonomy.note: architecture other: posterior sampling that adds a measurement-gradient step to each reverse-diffusion step of a pretrained score model; the figure draws sampling trajectories on data manifolds, not a network. depicts plots: a conceptual geometric diagram of manifolds and a measurement line.

arrangement.units: Two unframed panels of identical size and background, side by side; the left shows a projection-based sampler, the right the proposed one.
arrangement.inputs_as: the measurement as a blue line with a blurred band labelled y = A(x) in bold math, and noise levels as labelled green arcs M_4 ... M_0
arrangement.losses_at: none as boxes; the data-consistency gradient is a magenta step arrow drawn at each point of the trajectory and keyed in the bottom legend
arrangement.shared: the manifolds, measurement line and ground truth x* are redrawn identically in both panels

insights.structure: Two identical geometric scenes sit side by side, nested green arcs M_4 to M_0 crossed by a blurred blue measurement line, and only the sampling trajectory drawn over them differs between left and right.
insights.data: Noise levels are drawn as nested arcs that darken toward the clean manifold M_0, the measurement constraint as a thin blue line in a soft glow, and the ground truth and final sample as small red and blue dots labelled x* and x_0.
insights.emphasis: The baseline's red projection arrows jump off the arcs onto the blue line and its x_0 lands away from x*, while the proposed right panel uses only purple and magenta steps and lands on x*, so the absence of red is the contribution.
insights.flow: Each trajectory starts at the top on M_4 and zigzags downward through the arcs, alternating purple score steps with short magenta gradient steps, ending where the blue line meets M_0.
insights.avoid: The two panels carry no titles naming the methods compared, so the reader must find the baseline/proposed split in the caption; the magenta and purple arrows are also very short and close in hue.

figures.lesson: Explain a sampler by drawing the same geometry twice, side by side, and letting only the trajectory change: colour each kind of update step (score, data-gradient, projection) and key it in a one-line legend under each panel, so the missing step type in the proposed panel is the visible difference.

figures.title: Vision Transformers for Dense Prediction

taxonomy.task: monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation

arrangement.units: three panels separated by thin vertical rules: the overview (no container) and two module details, each detail in a rounded container tinted to match its module colour with a bold title in the bottom corner
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo cut into a patch grid at bottom-left
arrangement.shared: module colour families reused between overview boxes and detail containers

insights.structure: Three untitled panels split by thin full-height vertical rules: an overview at left (a column of four Transformer blocks with rungs out to Reassemble_4..32 boxes and a column of Fusion boxes), then a Reassemble_s detail panel and a Fusion detail panel each in a rounded tinted container.
insights.data: The input is a real photo cut into a grid of patches, tokens are orange 3-D sticks (one red readout token), the reassembled feature is a yellow 3-D block, and the output is a real grey depth map.
insights.emphasis: Each module has one colour family (slate Transformer, green Reassemble, purple Fusion) and its detail panel's container takes a pale tint of the same colour, binding overview box to zoom without any connecting lines.
insights.flow: An upside-down U: input enters bottom-left, goes right through Embed and up the Transformer column, rungs go right to Reassemble and Fusion, then down the Fusion column through Head to the depth map at bottom-right.
insights.avoid: Detail panels have no explicit link to the overview other than colour, and the card's domain tag 'medical-imaging' does not match this natural-image figure.

figures.lesson: Each proposed module keeps one hue across panels, a solid fill for its box in the overview and a pale tint of the same hue for its detail panel's rounded container, so the reader matches block to expansion without a legend or callout lines.

figures.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation

arrangement.units: Two lanes stacked: the subject lane (input photos, fine-tuned model, outputs) above, the prior lane (frozen model, fine-tuned model, outputs) below; no frames, the lanes are separated by space.
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos in a framed group, quoted prompts with an arrow into each model
arrangement.losses_at: each lane's loss is a dashed labelled arc along that lane's outer edge — reconstruction loss along the top, prior-preservation loss along the bottom
arrangement.shared: the fine-tuned model is drawn once in each lane, the copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 arrangement: top row the input-photo frame and the yellow fine-tuned model, bottom row the red frozen model and a second yellow copy, with the two yellow copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow.
insights.data: Each model is a flat bow-tie glyph with 'Text -> Image' across it, a small grey noise square at its left, a quoted prompt ('A [V] dog', 'A dog') in a handwriting font, and a tall frame of three real dog photos as output.
insights.emphasis: Fill colour marks model state (red with a padlock = frozen, yellow = being fine-tuned), and the two losses are dashed elbow arcs labelled in italic serif that run around the outside of the figure.
insights.flow: Prompts enter vertically (from above in the top row, from below in the bottom row); the reconstruction loss arc runs across the top from the generated images back to the input photos, the prior-preservation arc along the bottom between the two generated stacks.
insights.avoid: The noise squares float unconnected to the left of each model, and the frozen model's output stack is not labelled as the target of the prior loss.

figures.lesson: When the figure explains a training procedure rather than an architecture, the network can be one coloured bow-tie glyph labelled 'Text -> Image', with frozen versus trained shown by fill colour plus a padlock and each loss drawn as a dashed labelled arc between the image sets it compares.

figures.title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination

taxonomy.task: visual continuous control by learning behaviours in a learned latent dynamics model

arrangement.units: three unframed panels side by side, each a horizontal chain of latent circles, separated by whitespace and labelled (a)/(b)/(c) underneath
arrangement.inputs_as: real rendered frames (o_1..o_3) along the bottom row with blue labels; reconstructions o-hat in panel (a) as frames under grey decoders
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn as losses; predicted targets (r-hat, v-hat, a-hat) sit as icons above each latent state in the panel that learns them
arrangement.shared: the encoder, latent chain and icons are redrawn identically in every panel; the same colour per component ties them together

insights.structure: Three side-by-side panels repeat one chain of three green latent circles joined by green arrows; encoders and frames hang below the chain and rewards, values and actions sit above it.
insights.data: Observations are real walker frames along the bottom, latent states plain green dots, and predictions are icons (star medal for reward, trophy for value, joystick for action) with hatted symbols coloured like the icon.
insights.emphasis: Panel (b) is visibly emptier at the bottom (one frame only) and fuller on top (value, reward and action per step), so imagination reads as the chain running without observations.
insights.flow: Upward within a step (frame -> blue encoder -> latent -> predictions) and left-to-right along the green transition arrows in time; panels read left to right as phases.
insights.avoid: Meaning rests entirely on colour and icon identity with no legend, so the trophy versus medal distinction (value vs reward) has to be learned from the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw the training phases as the same unrolled chain repeated across panels and change only what attaches to it, so the difference between phases is what the eye picks up.

figures.title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion

taxonomy.note: training: the NeRF is optimised per prompt with a frozen diffusion prior (score distillation); no network is trained on a dataset

arrangement.units: one loop composition with two tinted rounded sub-panels naming the two models (pink NeRF bottom-left, cyan Imagen top-right), each with a white name tag
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in typewriter font at the top of the Imagen panel; Gaussian noise as a photo tile in the middle
arrangement.losses_at: the residual image tile at bottom-right with the gradient return arrow labelled 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights'
arrangement.shared: the gradient-filled return arrow joining the two panel colours

insights.structure: Left half a 3-D render chain (pink NeRF panel holding density and albedo cubes, then normals, shading and colour cubes, a sun and a camera); right half the rendering plus noise passed into a cyan Imagen panel with text prompt, frozen Transformer and U-Net.
insights.data: Every 3-D quantity is a thin wireframe cube holding the peacock coloured by that quantity; images (rendering, Gaussian noise, noised latent, denoised output, residual) are square photo tiles with math labels underneath.
insights.emphasis: A long bottom arrow 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights' filled with a pink-to-cyan gradient joins the two panel colours and closes the loop back to the NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Broad light-grey block arrows run left to right through rendering, then down and back right-to-left along the bottom to the NeRF panel; light enters as a yellow band arrow from the sun.
insights.avoid: Many grey block arrows of the same weight cross the middle with no labels, and the camera frustum lines tangle with them, so the order between shading, camera and rendering is hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Draw each rendered quantity (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour) as its own wireframe cube holding the object coloured by that quantity, and close the loop with one long gradient-tinted return arrow whose two end colours match the two model panels it connects.

figures.title: DreamGaussian: Generative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Content Creation

taxonomy.task: image-to-3D and text-to-3D generation with Gaussian splatting and mesh export

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded light-orange frames, each titled in italic gold: stages i and ii share the top row, stage iii spans the bottom row
arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'Text/Image' above each diffusion-prior bow-tie with a down arrow; stage iii also starts from a UV texture map at its left
arrangement.losses_at: inside the stage they train: 'SDS Loss' in blue under the stage-i diffusion prior; 'MSE Loss' in blue on a long return arrow along the bottom of stage iii
arrangement.shared: the diffusion prior is drawn twice as the same grey bow-tie, once in stage i and once in stage iii; '3D Gaussians' are drawn again at the start of stage ii

insights.structure: Three dashed rounded frames: two short stages side by side on the top row and the long texture-refinement stage across the full bottom row, each with an italic numbered title in its corner.
insights.data: Intermediate results are renders of the actual generated character at each step (blurry Gaussians, densified Gaussians, a half-wireframe textured mesh, a UV atlas, refined views), and the diffusion model is an abstract grey bow-tie.
insights.emphasis: Blue is reserved for optimisation - the 'Optimize' arrows and the 'SDS Loss' and 'MSE Loss' labels - so the training signals stand apart from black data arrows.
insights.flow: Read stage i then ii across the top and then stage iii left to right below; inside stage iii the forward path goes right through the diffusion prior and a long blue arrow along the bottom returns the MSE loss to the random view.
insights.avoid: No arrow links the three stages to each other, so the hand-off from Gaussians to mesh to UV map must be inferred from repeated images and panel numbers.

figures.lesson: Lay out a three-stage pipeline as two short stages side by side above one long stage, each in a titled dashed rounded frame, and colour only the gradient arrows and loss labels blue so the optimisation reads apart from the data path.

figures.title: Learning A Sparse Transformer Network for Effective Image Deraining

arrangement.units: a top band with the full network on one row, then a row of three dashed rounded panels for module details, each titled with full name and acronym at its bottom edge
arrangement.inputs_as: a real rainy photo at the left edge of the top band
arrangement.shared: block-type colours (blue conv, green MEFC, orange STB, grey Reshape) reused across both bands

insights.structure: Two bands split by a full-width dashed rule: the top band unfolds the whole U-shaped encoder-decoder onto one row with the bottleneck STB expanded in place as an orange dashed container; the bottom band holds three equal dashed panels (MEFC, TKSA, MSFN) each titled along its bottom edge.
insights.data: Rainy input and derained output are real photos at the two ends; feature sizes appear only as italic H x W x C text under each stage, and the TKSA panel draws its top-k mask as a small green 0/... grid.
insights.emphasis: The proposed modules get the only saturated fills (green MEFC, orange STB, yellow Top-k) while plain convs are blue, and the bottleneck STB is opened up in situ rather than in a separate panel.
insights.flow: Left to right; skip connections rise above the row as nested orthogonal polylines from each encoder stage to its concat circle in the decoder, and a global residual runs over the top from input to the final add.
insights.avoid: The symbol legend (multiply, concat, addition) is boxed at the far right of the top band and competes with the output photo; module labels are rotated 90 degrees in bold serif, which is hard to read.

figures.lesson: Unfolding the U-shaped network onto a single row, with skip connections as nested arcs over the top, frees a full-width strip underneath for one equal-height dashed detail panel per proposed module, while the bottleneck block is expanded in place inside a tinted container of its own colour.

figures.title: DuDoRNet: Learning a Dual-Domain Recurrent Network for Fast MRI Reconstruction with Deep T1 Prior

taxonomy.task: accelerated MRI reconstruction with a T1 prior

arrangement.units: repeated recurrent blocks, each a dashed grey rounded container labelled in bold below its left corner, with an ellipsis between the 1st and Nth
arrangement.inputs_as: text boxes: Zero-Padding Reconstruction in line, T1 data prior at upper left, Sampled k-space at lower left
arrangement.shared: prior lines (green image, orange k-space) along the top and the sampled k-space line along the bottom, each feeding every block

figures.title: Equivariant Diffusion for Molecule Generation in 3D

arrangement.shared: the same atom colour code in all four drawings

insights.data: Atoms are flat filled circles with thick black outlines coloured by element (grey, pink, blue, small white), bonds are thick black lines, and the noisy states are the same circles scattered without bonds.

figures.lesson: State an equivariance claim as a commutative square: the object and its noised version in one column, their rotated copies in the other, rotation arrows across, diffuse/denoise arrows down, and the invariance equation set under the bottom row with '=' between the columns.

figures.title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

arrangement.shared: the same network phi on both vertical arrows

insights.structure: Four copies of the same four-node graph form an unframed 2x2 commutative square: input top-left, rotated input top-right, network outputs for each directly beneath.
insights.data: Each node is a sage-green circle labelled x1..x4 carrying a tiny three-bar chart (invariant features h_i) and a dashed coloured arrow (vector v_i); the input row uses blue bars and salmon arrows, the output row red bars and teal arrows.
insights.emphasis: There is no network box at all: the method is the single italic phi on the two vertical arrows, and the claim is made by the bars staying identical across each row while the arrows rotate with the graph.
insights.flow: Horizontal arrows labelled S_g (top) and T_g (bottom) with a small dashed rotation glyph carry the transformation left-to-right; vertical phi arrows carry the network top-to-bottom, so the reader checks both paths around the square agree.
insights.avoid: The colour swap between rows (blue/salmon to red/teal) is never keyed in the figure, so a reader cannot tell it means 'output' rather than a different quantity.

figures.lesson: Attach each node's invariant features as a tiny bar chart and its vector as a dashed arrow, and swap the two colours between the input and output rows, so a reader sees the bars stay fixed under rotation while the arrows rotate with the graph.

figures.title: End-to-End Training of Multi-Document Reader and Retriever for Open-Domain Question Answering

insights.data: Each dataset is a filled disc sized by dataset size (large magenta for 12 million predicted structures, small dark purple for ~16,000 CATH) over a faint grey ribbon render; sequences are faint grey wavy lines; the network is a diagonal perspective stack of slabs shaded dark slate (GVP) to purple (Encoder) to light blue (Decoder).
insights.emphasis: The magenta data path (big disc, 'Predicted structures', 'UniRef50 sequences', AlphaFold2 loop) is the only warm colour, so the data-scale argument dominates while the model sits in cool tones inside a plain frame.

insights.avoid: The discs are not area-proportional (12 million vs ~16,000 is ~750x but the large disc is only ~9x the small one's area), and the grey ribbon and wavy-line textures are so faint they barely read as data.

figures.lesson: Show a data-scale argument with filled discs sized by dataset size and one colour per dataset carried to its paired sequences, and draw the structure-from-sequence step as a dotted loop over the model from the sequences back to the predicted structures.

figures.title: ESRGAN: Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks

figures.title: FEDformer: Frequency Enhanced Decomposed Transformer for Long-term Series Forecasting

figures.title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization

taxonomy.task: illustrating objective inconsistency of federated averaging under heterogeneous local steps
taxonomy.note: modality multi = no data modality is drawn; the figure is an abstract parameter-space sketch

arrangement.units: two unframed copies of the same sketch stacked vertically, separated by a grey dashed horizontal rule and titled at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: black start point x^(t,0)
arrangement.shared: identical marker set (local and global optima) in both copies

insights.structure: The same parameter-space sketch is drawn twice, stacked and split by a grey dashed horizontal rule, each titled at its top right in serif text ('Heterogeneous setting', 'Homogeneous setting').
insights.data: Points are markers only: black dots for the start x^(t,0) and the server point x^(t+1,0), blue triangles for local optima x_1*, x_2*, a green square for the global optimum x*; client steps are chains of solid blue arrows and the averaged step a dashed blue arrow.
insights.emphasis: No method is shown; the contrast carries the argument - in the top copy one client's step chain is much longer and the server point on the red dashed line lands far from x*, in the bottom copy it lands near it.
insights.flow: In each copy the eye follows the two step chains outward from the start point, then the red dashed line joining their ends, then the server dot on it relative to the optimum markers; top copy first, then bottom.
insights.avoid: No key explains the triangle / square markers or the solid vs dashed blue arrows, and the optimum markers sit far below the trajectories so the distance being argued is hard to judge.

figures.lesson: Show the bias of averaging unequal local progress by drawing the same parameter space twice, stacked - one client's step chain much longer in the upper copy - with the client end points joined by a red dashed line on which the server point sits, against fixed local and global optimum markers.

figures.title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization

taxonomy.task: normalized averaging of local updates in heterogeneous federated optimization
taxonomy.note: modality multi = abstract parameter-space sketch, no data modality

arrangement.inputs_as: black start point x^(t,0) with black local step chains
arrangement.shared: identical black local step chains and red dashed endpoint line in both panels

insights.structure: Two panels split by a grey dashed vertical rule, each stacking a parameter-space sketch, the rule's bold name, its update equation, a short block arrow down and the objective it optimises; a thick grey block arrow sits between the panels.
insights.data: Clients' local steps are black arrow chains from x^(t,0) to x_1^(t,4) and x_2^(t,2); per-client changes are dashed coloured vectors, the server step a solid coloured arrow to a coloured dot, with a bracket on top marking Delta_1^(t) and its normalized fraction.
insights.emphasis: The proposed rule owns green (bold green name, green equation, green arrow and server dot) against FedAvg's blue, and the change is stated in words on the grey arrow: 'Average normalized gradients instead of local changes'.
insights.flow: Left panel then right panel across the central block arrow; within each panel top-to-bottom from sketch to rule name to equation to the 'Optimizes F~(x)' objective.

figures.lesson: Compare two aggregation rules on the same client step chains: keep the local steps black in both panels, draw each rule's per-client vector and resulting server step in its own colour, and write that colour's update equation and objective directly beneath its sketch.

figures.title: FedProto: Federated Prototype Learning across Heterogeneous Clients

taxonomy.task: federated learning across heterogeneous clients by exchanging class prototypes

arrangement.units: one rounded server panel on top and two identical rounded client panels below (pale fill, thin grey outline), titled outside
arrangement.inputs_as: database icon with real handwritten digit samples above a yellow x_i box
arrangement.shared: server panel with the prototype aggregation equation, linked to every client by dashed up / solid down lines

insights.structure: A pale-green server panel spans the top centre and two pale client panels ('Local Client 1', 'Local Client m') sit side by side below with an ellipsis between them, each titled in serif text outside its panel.
insights.data: Inside each client a left-to-right chain of yellow rounded variable boxes x -> h -> y-hat -> y (arrows labelled f(phi; .) embedding and g(v; .) decision) sits under a second row C_i and C-bar_i; data is a database icon over handwritten digit samples, and class sets are numbered tan discs beside a 'label' tag icon.
insights.emphasis: What is communicated is a named box (C_i up, C-bar_i down) rather than a model, and the server's aggregation is written out as an equation in its own green inner box; losses L_R and L_S are salmon double-headed arrows inside each client.
insights.flow: Uploads go up as brown dashed orthogonal lines from each C_i into the aggregation box, downloads come back as solid green orthogonal lines from the server icon to each C-bar_i; within clients the chain reads left-to-right with h feeding up to C_i via 'Eq. (3)'.
insights.avoid: Upload and download lines run through the same gap between the client panels and cross each other, and the 'Central Server' title floats outside its panel to the right.

figures.lesson: Make the exchanged object a labelled box inside each client panel and route uploads (dashed) and downloads (solid, other colour) as orthogonal lines to a server panel that states the aggregation rule as an equation.

figures.title: Efficient Frequency Domain-based Transformers for High-Quality Image Deblurring

arrangement.units: three lettered panels separated by vertical dashed rules: (a) the network on two rounded tinted backgrounds (grey encoder, blue decoder), (b) FSAS on a pink rounded panel, (c) DFFN on an orange rounded panel
arrangement.inputs_as: tilted real blurry photo slab at the bottom of the encoder tower
arrangement.shared: colour legend shared by all panels

insights.structure: Panel (a) puts the encoder as a rising tower of tilted slabs on a grey rounded panel and the decoder as a descending tower on a blue panel, with panels (b) FSAS and (c) DFFN and a legend box set off to the right by vertical dashed rules.
insights.data: The blurry input photo and the deblurred output are drawn as tilted image slabs at the foot of each tower, matching the 3-D slab style of the feature maps above them, with channel=48/96/192 written beside each level.
insights.emphasis: Each detail panel is tinted in its module's legend colour (pink FSAS, orange DFFN) and the FFT/W step in (c) is wrapped in a purple inset, so the frequency-domain parts pop out of otherwise pastel boxes.
insights.flow: In (a) data climbs the left tower, crosses at the top by one long arrow and descends the right tower, with dash-dot skip lines running horizontally into circled-C concatenations; (b) and (c) read top-to-bottom with a residual line looping around the right edge.
insights.avoid: The legend explains colour by op type but the slabs' stacked colour layers (pink/orange/green) are hard to map to block order, and the dash-dot skips are thin and easy to lose against the panel tints.

figures.lesson: Each module's expanded detail panel is filled with that module's own legend colour (pink FSAS panel, orange DFFN panel), so the overview slab, the legend swatch and the zoomed panel read as one thing without any connector lines.

figures.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

arrangement.units: one composition: vision branch columns left (unframed), a pale-blue borderless panel holding the LM layers right
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos at the bottom of each vision column and a grey band of interleaved image-text data at bottom right
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output text box at top
arrangement.shared: vision encoder/resampler columns repeated per image

insights.structure: Two identical vision columns (photo, frozen trapezoid encoder, Perceiver Resampler) stand on the left; the right half stacks interleaved input, processed text, a pale-blue LM container of alternating LM block / GATED XATTN-DENSE pairs, and the output box.
insights.data: Inputs are real dog and cat photos and a grey band of quoted interleaved text with inline thumbnails; the processed text shows literal '<image>' tokens and the output is the quoted sentence 'a very serious cat.' in a pink box.
insights.emphasis: A two-entry legend in the top-left corner maps blue+snowflake to frozen and lilac to trained-from-scratch, so the new gated layers read as lilac stripes interleaved between frozen blue LM blocks.
insights.flow: Everything reads bottom-to-top; a line under the whole figure carries the images from the interleaved band back left to the vision columns, and resampler outputs run right in elbow lines into every gated layer.
insights.avoid: The resampler-to-xattn lines cross and nest four deep on the left of the LM container, making it hard to see which column feeds which layer.

figures.lesson: A two-entry legend (snowflake on blue = pretrained and frozen, plain lilac = trained from scratch) lets fill colour alone say which boxes the paper trains, and interleaving lilac layers between blue LM blocks shows where they are inserted.

figures.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

arrangement.units: context panel (pale-blue square with dashed selection), dashed zoom panel, grey code panel, side by side
arrangement.inputs_as: letters X and Y labelled 'Vision input' and 'Language input' below the zoom panel
arrangement.shared: same colour coding frozen/new as fig3

insights.structure: Three parts left to right: a small context square with one LM layer over one GATED XATTN-DENSE inside a dashed box, a larger dashed zoom panel expanding the pair into four sub-layers, and a grey pseudocode panel.
insights.data: Inputs are only letters X (purple, vision) and Y (navy, language) with K=V=[X], Q=[Y] tags beside each attention bar; no data images.
insights.emphasis: Frozen sub-layers are blue with snowflakes, new ones lavender with small 'tanh gating' pills above, and the code panel spells out alpha initialised at 0 in coloured comments.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top through stacked bars, each with a residual line rising on the right into a circled-plus; two straight lines flare from the small dashed box to the zoom panel's corners.

figures.lesson: Colour the variable letters themselves (vision X purple, language Y navy) in every input label and K=V=[X] / Q=[Y] tag, so the reader can follow which stream feeds each attention slot without tracing lines.

figures.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

arrangement.units: module panel (lavender, with dashed inner layer box) above its input stack on the left; grey code panel on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames on a time axis
arrangement.shared: vision encoder repeated per frame

insights.structure: Left half stacks video frames, encoders, 3x3 feature grids with time tags, a flatten bar and a long feature row under a large lavender 'Perceiver Resampler x num_layers' panel; the right half is a grey pseudocode panel.
insights.data: Three real skateboard frames sit on a time axis at the bottom; features are blue cell grids, flattened X_f a long row of small blue cells, and the learned latent queries five lavender cells entering from below right.
insights.emphasis: Colour separates the two streams: blue arrows for visual features X_f, purple arrows for latents X, and both meet in the Attention bar labelled K=V=[X_f, X], Q=[X].
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top; many parallel thin blue arrows rise from the feature row into Attention, purple arrows from the latents, and a fixed small set of purple arrows exits the top.
insights.avoid: The dense comb of ~25 thin arrows from the flattened row is visual noise; a single bracketed arrow would say the same.

figures.lesson: Show resampling as a count: a long row of blue feature cells, one thin arrow each, enters the attention bar while only five purple latent cells come in and five purple arrows leave, so the compression to a fixed token number is visible without stating it.

figures.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

taxonomy.note: architecture other: a tiled GPU kernel / memory-hierarchy computation, not a network topology

arrangement.units: context (pyramid), method (tiled loops), result (bar chart), the last set off by a thin vertical rule, each titled underneath or above
arrangement.inputs_as: Q, K^T, V block strips placed around the attention matrix
arrangement.shared: orange = SRAM colour across panels

insights.structure: Three unframed panels in a row: a memory-hierarchy pyramid (SRAM/HBM/DRAM), the tiled computation with Q, K^T, V and output strips arranged around a dashed N x N box, and a stacked runtime bar chart split off by a vertical rule.
insights.data: Matrices are strips of green square blocks with typeset shapes (Q: N x d); a copied tile is a single orange square, and the result is a stacked bar (Matmul/Dropout/Softmax/Mask) against one short 'Fused Kernel' bar.
insights.emphasis: Orange is reused for SRAM in the pyramid and for the on-chip tiles and the words 'SRAM' in the centre panel, tying the method to the fast memory tier.
insights.flow: Red 'Outer Loop' arrows run over K^T and down V, blue 'Inner Loop' arrows down Q and under the output; purple dashed arrows carry tiles into the compute block.

figures.lesson: Colour every tensor block by the memory level it sits in, using the colours of a memory-hierarchy pyramid drawn beside it, so moving a tile between memories reads as a colour change.

figures.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations

taxonomy.note: transformer-stack used loosely for the stack of repeated Fourier layers

arrangement.units: (a) the full architecture as an unframed row; (b) the Fourier layer in a thin-outlined rectangle titled at its top right, stacked below and linked by dashed zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: blue circle a(x) (function as symbol)
arrangement.shared: colour roles reused in both panels

insights.structure: Panel (a) is one left-to-right row a(x) -> P -> Fourier layers 1..T -> Q -> u(x); panel (b), a thin black frame below, opens Fourier layer 2 into a spectral path in a pale-yellow box and a local W path below it.
insights.data: Functions a(x), v(x), u(x) are light-blue circles; between F, R and F^-1 small sine-wave sketches show the spectrum before and after truncation of high modes.
insights.emphasis: The spectral path's pale-yellow box repeats the fill of the Fourier layer boxes in (a), and the zoom is signalled by dashed lines fanning from layer 2 to the frame's corners.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right in both panels; in (b) v(x) forks up into the spectral box and down to W, and both merge at a red '+' before sigma.
insights.avoid: Using the same orange circle for learned maps P, Q, R and W while the sum and activation are a near-identical red-orange makes role colours hard to tell apart.

figures.lesson: Show spectral truncation as data, not a label: put tiny sine-wave sketches between the forward and inverse transform circles, many frequencies before the learned multiplier and only the low ones after it.

figures.title: Protein structure generation via folding diffusion

taxonomy.task: protein backbone generation via angle diffusion

arrangement.units: no frames; chain row on top, two state-illustration columns under its ends, angle-definition schematic in the bottom centre
arrangement.inputs_as: noise state x_T circle with its noisy heatmap and tangled structure below
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Top row is the diffusion chain x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0 in large open circles; below each end sit an angle heatmap and a rendered structure, and the bottom centre holds a ball-and-stick backbone defining the six angles.
insights.data: States are shown three ways: as math circles, as angle heatmaps (noisy vs banded), and as green cartoon tubes (tangle vs helical bundle) labelled 'Corresponding structure'.
insights.emphasis: Torsions phi/psi/omega are orange with dashed circular arrows and bond angles theta1-3 dark green with dashed arcs, making the representation (angles, not coordinates) the visual centre.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the chain with the learned reverse step p_xi as a solid arrow and the forward q as a dashed arrow curving back underneath; the lower content is read by column, not by arrows.
insights.avoid: The network that predicts the denoising step is never drawn, so the figure explains the representation but not the model.

figures.lesson: When the generated variable is not coordinates, show each end of the chain twice - as the variable itself (a heatmap of angles per residue) and, below it, the 3-D structure it decodes to - and define the variable once in a small colour-coded chemical schematic between them.

figures.title: FourCastNet: A Global Data-driven High-resolution Weather Model using Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators

arrangement.units: Two round-cornered framed regions: (a) the AFNO architecture filling the left half; a right frame holding (b) fine-tuning, (c) precipitation model and (d) inference as three unframed sub-panels stacked top to bottom, each titled with its letter.
arrangement.inputs_as: a tilted 3-D stack of real gridded weather maps with a patch grid overlay and a dotted list of channel names fanning into its layers; in (b)-(d) a bold symbol X(k) entering from the left
arrangement.losses_at: none in (a); in (b) and (c) small L2 boxes sit above the model chain, fed by X_true / p_true arrows from the top and outputting 'loss' upward
arrangement.shared: the same 'AFNO model' box is drawn twice in (b) for the two unrolled steps; in (c) and (d) the backbone is a separate box with a bold outline (frozen), marked by an asterisk footnote in (c)

insights.structure: The left half is a vertical AFNO stack inside one frame, and the right half stacks three small block diagrams (fine-tuning, precipitation model, inference) that reuse the same 'AFNO model' box.
insights.data: Input and output are tilted 3-D stacks of real jet-colormap weather maps, the input overlaid with an h x w patch grid and a dotted list of channel names whose thin lines fan into each layer, with a row of p x p patch thumbnails between the stack and the embedding.
insights.emphasis: The spatial-mixing block is the only one expanded, through dashed zoom lines into an FFT / Multiply Frequency / IFFT column and again into a z -> MLP -> S(.) box, while all blocks stay uncoloured.
insights.flow: Panel (a) reads bottom to top on short parallel up-arrows between full-width blocks; panels (b)-(d) read left to right, with ground truth dropping in from above to L2 boxes and a loop arrow in (d) feeding X(k+1) back to the backbone input.
insights.avoid: The left half's dashed zoom lines cross each other and the detail boxes float at the frame's left edge, so it is hard to tell which zoom belongs to Spatial vs Channel Mixing; the channel-name list is also tiny italic text.

figures.lesson: Put real data at both ends of a vertical pipeline as 3-D map stacks and keep every block uncoloured, then expand only the novel layer through dashed zoom-in boxes on the side so the contribution is the one place with extra detail.

figures.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection

taxonomy.task: multi-scale feature pyramid for object detection

arrangement.units: One overview (two pyramids side by side, predict boxes at the right) above a dashed detail frame for the merge block; the detail is linked by dashed leader lines, not set off as a separate titled panel.
arrangement.inputs_as: a faded real photo as the lowest, orange-outlined plane of the left pyramid
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn ('predict' boxes at each right-hand level)
arrangement.shared: none drawn (the caption-level fact that heads are shared across levels is not shown)

insights.structure: A shrinking bottom-up pyramid of planes sits on the left, a top-down pyramid of equal levels on the right, joined by one horizontal arrow per level, with a dashed detail frame for the merge block placed underneath.
insights.data: Feature levels are unfilled oblique planes whose outline weight grows with depth on the left, the input is a faded photo as the lowest plane, and outputs are small 'predict' text boxes.
insights.emphasis: The new top-down pathway is the uniformly heavy-outlined right pyramid, and its lateral merge is enlarged in a dashed zoom frame showing '1x1 conv', '2x up' and a circled plus.
insights.flow: Read up the left pyramid on short arrows, across on lateral arrows, down the right pyramid, then right to 'predict'; in the zoom, the lateral input enters from the left and the upsampled input from the top.
insights.avoid: The overview has no labels at all (no stage names, no scales), so the meaning of outline weight and the two pyramids is left entirely to the caption.

figures.lesson: Encode feature strength as outline weight on the pyramid planes, and zoom one lateral merge into a dashed detail frame tied to it by dashed leader lines.

figures.title: SE(3) diffusion model with application to protein backbone generation

taxonomy.task: SE(3) protein backbone diffusion score network layer

arrangement.units: three unframed horizontal lanes (node in a grey orange-outlined container, edge, frame) in the left panel; a grey cyan-outlined EdgeUpdate detail panel at right
arrangement.inputs_as: small glyphs (cell columns, grid, frame axes) with bold math labels
arrangement.shared: updated node embedding feeds edge and backbone lanes

insights.structure: Left panel shows one layer as three horizontal lanes (node h through a grey NodeUpdate container, edge z through an EdgeUpdate box, frames T through a BackboneUpdate box); right panel opens EdgeUpdate with a small glyph legend beneath.
insights.data: Each lane's input is a tiny glyph: h0/h_l as green-yellow cell columns, z_l as a blue cell grid, T_l as a red three-armed frame; outputs are the bold symbols h_{l+1}, z_{l+1}, T_{l+1}.
insights.emphasis: Colour codes the stream: all NodeUpdate parts and arrows orange, all EdgeUpdate parts cyan (outline repeated in the zoom panel), frames black.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each lane; the new node embedding drops down in orange into the edge and backbone updates, and inside the zoom h^m, h^n feed down into concatenations along the z line.
insights.avoid: Orange lines from z and T rise into the IPA box and cross the black lanes, which clutters the lower-left corner.

figures.lesson: Draw the residue frame as a tiny three-axis glyph next to T and give it its own black lane under the coloured node and edge lanes, so the reader sees which stream updates geometry and which updates features.

figures.title: Graph Attention Networks

taxonomy.task: node classification with attention-weighted neighbourhood aggregation

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side on whitespace: the attention-coefficient computation (left) and the multi-head neighbourhood aggregation around one node (right)
arrangement.inputs_as: left: a row of eight small unit circles under two curly braces W h_i and W h_j; right: neighbour feature nodes h2-h6 ringed around the centre node
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the figure shows the layer computation only
arrangement.shared: the attention mechanism of the left panel is not redrawn on the right; its output appears as alpha labels on each spoke

insights.structure: A narrow left panel (input units -> activation unit -> alpha_ij, stacked vertically) sits beside a wide right panel where the hub node h1 is ringed by five neighbours with an output node h1' off to the right.
insights.data: Every quantity is a white circle with a math label (h-vector, alpha_ij, h1'); feature vectors on the left are rows of tiny unit circles under curly braces, and attention weights are spoke labels rather than drawn values.
insights.emphasis: The three heads are the only coloured elements, each with its own line style, so multi-head attention stands out against the otherwise black line art.
insights.flow: Left panel reads bottom-to-top along converging arrows; right panel reads radially inward along the spokes to h1, then left-to-right along the thick concat/avg arrow to h1'.
insights.avoid: The head encoding (blue straight, green zigzag, purple wavy) has no key in the figure, and three parallel lines per spoke plus rotated alpha labels make the hub crowded.

figures.lesson: Show multi-head attention on a graph as one hub node with neighbour spokes, each spoke carrying one parallel arrow per head in a distinct colour and line style, merging into one output arrow.

figures.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks

arrangement.units: a schematic panel (two card stacks for input and output layers joined across a whitespace gap labelled 'hidden layers') and an unframed scatter-plot panel on the right, separated only by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: a small 4-node graph with node features X1-X4 inside the input-layer card stack
arrangement.losses_at: right of the output layer: dashed double-headed arrows from Z1 and Z4 to label nodes Y1 and Y4, coloured like their nodes
arrangement.shared: the graph structure (black edges) is redrawn identically inside the input and output layer stacks

insights.structure: Two card-stack layers (input C, output F) hold the same 4-node graph and face each other across a narrow gap marked 'hidden layers', with label nodes Y outside the output stack and a scatter plot filling the right third.
insights.data: Node features and outputs are tinted circles with math labels (X_i, Z_i), channel depth is the offset stack of card outlines, and the result is a dense t-SNE scatter of coloured dots.
insights.emphasis: Per-node colours carried through the connecting lines and dashed label arrows make the propagation and the partial labelling the visible point; there is no highlight box.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: each input node sends a curved line in its colour that converges into one dashed line through the hidden-layer gap, then fans out to its matching output node.
insights.avoid: The t-SNE panel sits in the same figure without a divider or label, and its class colours (red, yellow, grey, etc.) are unrelated to the node colours of the schematic, inviting a false match.

figures.lesson: To show a graph network, draw the same small graph inside each layer, keep one colour per node across layers, and attach supervision only to the few labelled nodes with dashed double arrows.

figures.title: Protein Representation Learning by Geometric Structure Pretraining

taxonomy.task: protein structure representation (relational GNN with edge message passing)
taxonomy.note: paradigm: relational GCN (R-GCN) style message passing

arrangement.units: three columns titled at top and separated by dotted rules; each method column has a dashed rounded inset of the local neighbourhood above per-type rows
arrangement.inputs_as: 3-D stick render of the protein in the top-left
arrangement.shared: edge-type colour key across all columns

insights.structure: Three titled columns divided by dotted vertical rules: protein graph construction, the relational GNN update of node 4, and the same update one level up for edge (4,7).
insights.data: A real stick model of a residue chain with circled residue centres sits top-left; the graph is numbered nodes with coloured directed edges, and features are small dark bars inside coloured frames.
insights.emphasis: Edge type is the single colour key (blue/yellow sequential, red kNN, green radius) given once in a rounded legend and reused for arrows, row frames and per-type weight bars.
insights.flow: Down within column 1 via a large hollow arrow, then left-to-right in columns 2-3 where each row's per-type transform curves into a circled-plus sum on the right.
insights.avoid: Column 3 recolours edge types (orange, purple, black) that the column-1 legend does not define.

figures.lesson: Fix one colour per edge type in the graph-construction panel and reuse it for the per-relation rows of the message-passing panels, so the reader can follow sequential, radius and kNN edges from the protein to the aggregation.

figures.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

taxonomy.task: believable agent memory, reflection and planning

arrangement.units: one spine with a dashed sub-group around the memory part; Plan and Reflect float outside
arrangement.inputs_as: a 'Perceive' process box
arrangement.shared: memory stream read and written by both loops

insights.structure: A straight spine Perceive -> Memory Stream -> Retrieve -> Retrieved Memories -> Act, with the memory part enclosed in a dashed grey 'Generative Agent Memory' rectangle and Plan above, Reflect below outside it.
insights.data: No data shown; processes are white rounded boxes with italic labels and data stores are bevelled grey 3-D boxes with bold labels.
insights.emphasis: Memory Stream is the largest box with the heaviest bold text, and the two bevelled store boxes stand out against the flat process boxes.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the spine, with two mirror arcs leaving Retrieved Memories, one over the top through Plan and one under the bottom through Reflect, both returning into Memory Stream.
insights.avoid: The bevelled 3-D boxes look dated; encode stores by a flat shape or fill instead.

figures.lesson: Separate stores from operations by shape alone (bevelled square plaques with bold labels for memories, light rounded boxes with italic verbs for processes) and route the plan and reflect loops as symmetric arcs above and below the spine that both write back into the main memory.

figures.title: GeoDiff: a Geometric Diffusion Model for Molecular Conformation Generation

arrangement.units: one unframed horizontal chain with renders under selected states
arrangement.inputs_as: grey noise state C^T with a tangled molecule render
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One wide strip of state circles C^T ... C^t, C^{t-1} ... C^0 from left to right with ball-and-stick molecules tucked under three of them; no containers.
insights.data: Molecules are 3-D ball-and-stick renders: a tangled one under C^T, a ghosted trail of translucent overlapping copies near C^{t-1}, and a clean fused-ring molecule under C^0.
insights.emphasis: Fill alone separates noise from data: noisy states are grey circles and the final clean state is white; the conditioning on the graph G appears in the reverse label p_theta(C^{t-1}|G, C^t).
insights.flow: Solid arrows run left-to-right for the learned reverse process with its label above; a dashed curved arrow beneath returns from C^{t-1} to C^t for the forward q.
insights.avoid: Like most diffusion teasers it omits the denoising network, so it cannot serve as a model figure on its own.

figures.lesson: Show what a denoising step does to the geometry as a ghosted trail of overlapping translucent molecule copies fading into the solid one, placed under the chain's latent circles, and fill clean-data circles white against grey noisy ones.

figures.title: GLIGEN: Open-Set Grounded Text-to-Image Generation

arrangement.units: overview panel (pale blue-grey rectangle) and zoom panel (pale-pink rectangle with thin orange border, titled top-left), side by side
arrangement.inputs_as: row of purple visual token squares
arrangement.shared: token colour legend

insights.structure: Left: a pale blue-grey panel stacking Self-Attention, Gated Self-Attention and Cross-Attention bars with token rows between them; right: a pale-pink bordered zoom panel of the gated layer.
insights.data: Tokens are rows of coloured squares (purple visual, yellow caption, green grounding) with a legend strip under the left panel; grey fan lines between rows show which tokens attend to which.
insights.emphasis: Frozen layers are blue with a snowflake and the inserted layer salmon with a flame; in the zoom, the gate gamma (init as 0) is the only red text beside a circled-times.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top through the stack; two thin orange lines fan from the gated bar's right end to the zoom panel, where a skip line runs up the right side into a circled-plus.
insights.avoid: The dense grey all-to-all fan lines between token rows add noise and are hard to read as attention patterns.

figures.lesson: Trainable versus frozen is encoded twice at once (salmon bar with a flame vs blue bars with snowflakes), and the salmon tint carries into the zoomed detail panel so the inserted layer is found and read without the caption.

figures.title: Grounded Language-Image Pre-training

arrangement.units: Two horizontal lanes, the text lane above the visual lane, with fusion blocks between them; the lanes meet in a word-region score matrix at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: the prompt as coloured text in boxes above, the real photo with coloured boxes below
arrangement.losses_at: both losses leave the matrix at the far right edge (alignment loss, localization loss)
arrangement.shared: fusion blocks drawn between the lanes with short vertical arrows into each

insights.structure: A green text lane (Text Encoder, BERT Layers) sits above a blue visual lane (Visual Encoder, DyHead Modules) with yellow Fusion blocks stacked between them under a 'Deep Fusion' label, and both lanes run right into an N x M word-region score matrix.
insights.data: The prompt is quoted with phrases coloured to match the coloured boxes on the real photo at the left; the matrix's rows are photo crops of detected regions and its columns are word-feature token cells, each cell holding O_i·P_j.
insights.emphasis: Colour-matched words and boxes (green woman, yellow blow dryer, cyan goggles) make the grounding idea visible before any block is read, and the large matrix is the visual destination of both lanes.
insights.flow: Left to right in two parallel rows, with short vertical arrows P_i2t / O_t2i crossing up and down through the fusion blocks; both losses exit to the far right of the matrix.
insights.avoid: Word-token cells split words mid-token ('Pers on', 'Bicyc le') and the two stacked token rows partly overlap, which reads as a rendering glitch.

figures.lesson: Draw grounding-style detection as a word-by-region matrix whose rows are cropped thumbnails of the detected boxes and whose columns are the prompt's word tokens, with the same word colours used for the box outlines on the input photo.

figures.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a layer-wise quantization procedure on one weight matrix; no network is drawn

arrangement.units: two unframed matrix panels side by side, each with a bold title above and a short plain caption below
arrangement.inputs_as: no separate inputs; the two matrices themselves are the objects
arrangement.shared: the current block is marked in both matrices with the same heavy outline, and a double-headed arrow links the two

insights.structure: Two matrices sit side by side as equals, the inverse Hessian on the left and the weight block on the right, joined by a double-headed arrow and keyed by one bottom legend.
insights.data: Matrices are drawn as plain rectangles: the Hessian's Cholesky factor is a grey staircase triangle and the weight matrix is vertical colour stripes whose hue says quantized or pending.
insights.emphasis: A heavy black frame around the current block, repeated on the matching rows of the Hessian, plus saturated orange/blue shades set the active block apart from pale finished and pending parts.
insights.flow: Read the two bold titles left to right, then the captions below each; the only connector is a horizontal double-headed arrow with no label.
insights.avoid: The double-headed arrow carries no label, so what passes between the Hessian and the weights is left to the caption.

figures.lesson: Show a column-by-column algorithm on a matrix by colouring stripes by state (done, current, pending) and outlining the current block with the same heavy frame in every matrix it touches.

figures.title: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting

arrangement.units: lettered unframed panels a)-g) titled at their top: a rollout row of three, a zoom-in row of encoder/processor/decoder, and a bottom strip of seven mesh levels
arrangement.inputs_as: stacked colour weather maps over a gridded globe
arrangement.shared: the GraphCast box opens into the encoder-processor-decoder row via a bracket; processor rays fan to the mesh strip

insights.structure: Two tiers: a top row a)-c) shows the rollout (input state, predict next state, roll out with GC blocks) and, below a bracket opening from the GraphCast box, a second row d)-f) shows encoder, processor and decoder, with a bottom strip g) of seven multi-mesh spheres M0-M6 fanned from the processor.
insights.data: Weather states are stacked coloured lat-lon map layers above gridded 3D globes; the model internals are rendered globe-and-mesh geometry with green (encoder), blue (processor) and magenta (decoder) edges.
insights.emphasis: The processor globe is the largest central object and thin rays fan from it to the M0-M6 refinement series, making the multi-mesh the visual focus.
insights.flow: Left to right in each tier, with the GraphCast box zooming down into the d)-f) tier via a funnel-shaped bracket and the processor fanning down into g).
insights.avoid: Heavy photoreal 3D rendering is costly to reproduce and the green/blue/magenta stage colours carry no legend, so the stage meaning relies on the panel titles.

figures.lesson: Draw the encoder, processor and decoder as three views of the same rendered globe-and-mesh geometry and let edge colour alone (green, blue, magenta) say which stage is acting, instead of drawing three abstract boxes.

figures.title: GraphMAE: Self-Supervised Masked Graph Autoencoders

arrangement.units: one left-to-right pipeline with two dashed sub-boxes (encoder; re-mask+decoder) and a dashed-titled reconstruction target, plus a greyed baseline row beneath
arrangement.inputs_as: a small numbered node graph with feature bars x1-x5
arrangement.losses_at: far right under the reconstructed graph: Scaled Cosine Error(z_i, x_i)
arrangement.shared: a dashed Encoding/Decoding timeline spanning both sub-boxes

insights.structure: Dashed boxes for GNN Encoder and Re-mask + GNN Decoder sit in a row between the input graph at left and a Feature Reconstruction graph at right, with a dashed timeline below labelling 'Encoding' and 'Decoding' spans, and a greyed GAEs row underneath as contrast.
insights.data: Graphs are drawn as numbered circle nodes with small feature-bar glyphs; masked nodes are grey and tagged [MASK]/[DMASK]; codes and reconstructed features are small grids with grey re-masked rows.
insights.emphasis: The method's own steps (Mask Node Features, Re-mask, GNN Decoder, Scaled Cosine Error) are underlined in blue, while the conventional GAE pipeline below is greyed out to show what is replaced.
insights.flow: Left to right with hollow block arrows between stages; one curved arrow drops from the input graph to the greyed GAE baseline row.
insights.avoid: Blue underlined headings look like hyperlinks, and the stacked-card GNN Encoder box makes nodes partially overlap their own labels.

figures.lesson: Draw the baseline as a faded grey dashed row directly beneath the method row, one box per stage and aligned under its counterpart, so the reader compares stage by stage while the baseline never competes with the method for attention.

figures.title: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?

taxonomy.task: graph representation learning with structural encodings

arrangement.units: one framed figure with three columns: attention stack, encoding matrices, example graph
arrangement.inputs_as: a small coloured node-link graph v1-v5
arrangement.shared: a brace mapping the graph to all three encodings

insights.structure: A vertical attention block (Linear Q/K/V, MatMul, Scale, SoftMax, MatMul) on the left, two 5x5 encoding matrices (Spatial, Edge) in the middle, and the example 5-node graph on the right joined to them by a curly brace.
insights.data: Node feature and centrality encoding are coloured token rows at the bottom; spatial encoding is a blue-shade 5x5 grid and edge encoding a multi-colour grid whose cell colours match the dashed edge colours in the graph.
insights.emphasis: The encoding matrices are the largest, most colourful elements and inject into the plain attention block at the add node beside Scale, showing where the contribution plugs in.
insights.flow: Bottom to top through the attention block, with bracketed lines from the matrices entering sideways at the ⊕ before SoftMax; the brace reads right to left from graph to encodings.
insights.avoid: The bracket from the two matrices to the attention block is a thin, ambiguous line that can be read as feeding Linear V instead of the bias add.

figures.lesson: Colour the toy graph's dashed edges with the same hues as the edge-encoding matrix cells for those node pairs (grey cells for non-adjacent pairs) and tint its nodes like the node-feature strip, so each matrix cell traces to its edge by colour alone and one brace is enough to tie all encodings to the graph.

figures.title: From Local to Global: A GraphRAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

taxonomy.task: query-focused summarization over a document corpus via an LLM-built knowledge graph

arrangement.units: Eight equal rounded boxes in two columns (four each) with no frames; a separate key row at the bottom repeats the two box styles.
