arrangement.inputs_as: a box naming the input ('Source Documents'); no data drawn
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Eight same-size boxes form two columns joined at the bottom, the left column holding indexing products from documents down to the knowledge graph and the right column holding community products up to the global answer.
insights.data: Every intermediate is a named box (Text Chunks, Entities & Relationships, Graph Communities), and each transformation is a two-line label beside its arrow such as 'domain-tailored summarization'.
insights.emphasis: Stage membership is shown only by fill colour, lavender for indexing time and green for query time, with a key row at the bottom.
insights.flow: Read down the left column, across the bottom via 'community detection', then up the right column to 'Global Answer' at the top right.
insights.avoid: The knowledge graph and communities are drawn as plain text boxes, so the graph structure the method depends on never appears; a small node-link glyph would let the figure show it.

figures.lesson: For a pipeline whose steps are operations on data, make the boxes the intermediate data products and write each operation as a label on its arrow, folding the chain into a U so it fits a wide figure.

figures.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs

taxonomy.task: inductive node embedding and node classification
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = the unsupervised graph-context objective, drawn as the graph pictogram output next to 'label'

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each a full copy of the same graph with a numbered caption beneath: sampling with dotted hop circles, aggregation with coloured arrows, prediction with output boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: the input graph itself: outlined circle nodes with bracketed feature column vectors next to the nodes
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the right panel ends in a 'label' box and a graph-context pictogram as the two prediction targets
arrangement.shared: the same graph layout is repeated in all three panels; the two aggregators are block-arrow labels at the top of panel 2

insights.structure: Three unframed panels sit in a row, each repeating the same graph, ordered by numbered captions (1. sample, 2. aggregate, 3. predict) beneath them.
insights.data: Nodes are outlined circles, hops are two concentric dotted circles labelled k=1 and k=2 around the red target, and node features are tiny bracketed column vectors beside the nodes.
insights.emphasis: Only the active neighbourhood is coloured (brown sampled edges in panel 1, green hop-2 and blue hop-1 arrows in panel 2) while the rest of the graph fades to light grey, and the target node is red in every panel.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right; inside panel 2 thick arrows run inward from green outer nodes to blue inner nodes to the red centre, and in panel 3 two black arrows leave the centre for the 'label' box and the graph-context pictogram.
insights.avoid: Hop colours are not consistent across panels (all sampled nodes are brown in panel 1 but blue/green per hop in panel 2), and the bracketed feature vectors are too small to read.

figures.lesson: Redraw the same graph once per step and fade everything the step does not touch to light grey, keeping one fixed colour for the target node, so each panel shows only the active neighbourhood.

figures.title: GraphSAINT: Graph Sampling Based Inductive Learning Method

taxonomy.task: scalable minibatch GCN training on large graphs
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = subgraph-sampling minibatch training (sample a subgraph, train a full GCN on it, repeat)

arrangement.units: two unframed halves separated by whitespace and a central pair of circular arrows: left the full graph with a bold sampled subgraph, right a three-row layered network of the sampled nodes
arrangement.inputs_as: the full graph of numbered circle nodes, sampled part bold and unsampled part pale grey
arrangement.shared: the sampled node IDs (0,1,2,3,5,7) appear in both halves and in every layer row on the right

insights.structure: Two unframed halves sit side by side: a numbered 10-node graph on the left and a three-row layered network on the right, joined by two curved arrows that form a circle between them.
insights.data: Nodes are numbered circles; the sampled ones (0,1,2,3,5,7) have bold dark outlines and thick edges while 4,6,8,9 are pale grey, and the right half repeats only the sampled IDs in each row with thin arrows following the subgraph's edges.
insights.emphasis: Contrast is only grey value: the sampled subgraph is dark and the rest faded, with no colour or named module.
insights.flow: The eye moves left to right through the circular arrows, which imply repetition, and inside the right half the arrows run bottom to top from layer to layer.
insights.avoid: There are no words at all (no 'sample', 'GCN' or layer names), so what the cycle and the rows mean relies entirely on the caption.

figures.lesson: Mark the sampled subgraph by fading the unsampled nodes to pale grey, then rebuild the network from only the sampled node IDs beside it, so the reader sees that training never touches the rest of the graph.

figures.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection

taxonomy.note: teaser of tasks and results, not a method figure; architecture/training set to other (not depicted)

arrangement.units: unframed photo columns with tinted category headers, grouped by captions (a)/(b)/(c) and a vertical rule before the application
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos with the text prompt printed below each
arrangement.shared: the same two photos repeated in every column

insights.structure: Three captioned groups left to right: (a) closed-set detection, (b) open-set detection with two columns (novel categories, referring sentences), separated by a vertical rule from (c) image-editing application.
insights.data: Two real photos (lions, World Cup crowd) repeated in each column with coloured detection boxes and the text prompt printed under each image; edited results appear in (c).
insights.emphasis: A double-headed arrow across the top labelled 'Object localization' to 'Text understanding' orders the columns along one axis so the task visibly widens.
insights.flow: Left to right across columns; blue arrows with dot ends carry detections into the stable-diffusion edits.
insights.avoid: Small coloured boxes on busy crowd photos are hard to read at print size.

figures.lesson: Order a detection teaser's columns along one named axis (fixed categories, novel words, referring sentences) on the same photos, with the text prompt printed under each image and the boxes drawn on it, so the reader sees the task widen.

figures.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection

arrangement.units: three numbered panels with purple pill titles, separated by purple rules: overall model on the left, two layer zoom-ins stacked on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted category prompt pill and a real cat photo
arrangement.losses_at: top of the overall panel: Contrastive loss and Localization loss with red arrows
arrangement.shared: beige zoom wedges connect blocks to their detail panels

insights.structure: A purple vertical rule splits the figure: '1. Model Overall' fills the left half, and the right half stacks zoom-ins '3. A Decoder Layer' (top) and '2. A Feature Enhancer Layer' (bottom), each tied to its block on the left by a pale beige wedge.
insights.data: Text features are rows of slanted green bars, image features are blue 3D voxel cubes, queries are small yellow sticks, and outputs feed a contrastive grid with text tokens as columns.
insights.emphasis: Blocks carry a green-to-blue gradient fill (Feature Enhancer, Query Selection, enhancer layer frame) encoding text-image mixing, and the two losses exit as red arrows at the top.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in the overall model from input text and image to losses; zoom wedges run right to the detailed layers, which also read bottom to top.
insights.avoid: Text-feature skip lines loop around the left side and cross with a hop, making the routing to Query Selection and the decoder hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Encode the two modalities as two glyph types and colours (text = row of thin green rods, image = blue grid cube) and fill every block that fuses them with a green-to-blue gradient, so fusion is visible without labels.

figures.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models

arrangement.units: four colour-framed identical mask grids on top, then a tinted rounded mechanism panel and an unframed plot below, separated by rules
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted sentence as a token row
arrangement.shared: frame colour = curve colour across grids and plot

insights.structure: Top row of four framed attention-mask grids (dynamic, strided, local, H2O sparsity); below a horizontal rule, the H2O mechanism panel at bottom-left and an accuracy-vs-memory-reduction plot at bottom-right.
insights.data: Masks are 10x10 grids with blue kept cells (green for heavy hitters); the mechanism shows a token row, key/value card stacks with attention scores, a red X on an evicted key, and a column-summed score table.
insights.emphasis: Each grid's frame colour matches its curve in the plot, and the H2O frame and mechanism panel share a light blue tint, tying the proposal across all three parts.
insights.flow: Top row read left to right as a comparison; mechanism read from the query up to keys, then a dashed arrow to the accumulated-score table.
insights.avoid: Mixing comparison grids, mechanism and result plot in one figure crowds the mechanism into a small corner panel.

figures.lesson: Frame each KV-cache policy's attention grid in the colour of its curve in the accompanying accuracy plot, and give the proposal's frame the same tint as its mechanism panel, so grid, curve and explanation are tied by one colour.

figures.title: Activating More Pixels in Image Super-Resolution Transformer

taxonomy.note: not a method figure: a results/attribution comparison grid (no architecture drawn); architecture set to other (not depicted)

arrangement.units: unframed image tiles in a 2-row x 5-column grid with rotated row labels
arrangement.inputs_as: HR and LR real photos
arrangement.shared: row labels (LAM Attribution, SR Results) shared across columns

insights.structure: A two-row grid: HR and LR reference at left, then one column per method (EDSR, RCAN, SwinIR, HAT (Ours)) with LAM attribution maps above and SR crops below.
insights.data: Attribution maps are red heatmaps on white; SR results are real grayscale crops with a green box; DI and PSNR/SSIM are printed under each tile.
insights.emphasis: HAT is the last column, its heatmap is visibly widest, and its numbers are bold.
insights.flow: Left to right across methods; the red square on the HR image marks the patch analysed.

figures.lesson: Make the result-idea teaser a two-row grid with one column per method - an attribution heatmap above the output crop, a score printed under each tile - and put your method last with its numbers in bold.

figures.title: Heterogeneous Graph Transformer

arrangement.units: one framed layer with three grey titled sub-panels, flanked by an unframed input sub-graph and a stacked output column
arrangement.inputs_as: a small heterogeneous sub-graph with node and edge type annotations
arrangement.losses_at: far right: Predict / Loss arrows between H^(L)[t] and Downstream Tasks
arrangement.shared: residual connection line across the top of the layer frame

insights.structure: A large rounded frame titled 'A Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (HGT) Layer' holds three grey sub-panels — (1) Heterogeneous Mutual Attention top, (2) Heterogeneous Message Passing below, (3) Target-Specific Aggregation at right — between a sub-graph at left and an ×L stack with downstream tasks at right.
insights.data: Nodes are shape-coded (circle t, square s1, hexagon s2) with type labels; node features are small vertical circle stacks H^(l-1); per-type weights are stacked cards W_φ(e).
insights.emphasis: Each source node keeps its own colour (dark blue t, cyan s1, orange s2) through every Linear and line, so type-specific parameters are visible as colour.
insights.flow: Left to right: coloured curved lines fan from the sub-graph into attention and message panels, merge at ⊗/⊕ in aggregation, and a residual line runs across the top; Predict/Loss arrows run vertically at the far right.
insights.avoid: Many curved crossing lines between the attention and message panels make individual paths hard to follow.

figures.lesson: Give each node type one colour and repeat it on everything that belongs to that type - node glyph, hidden-vector capsule, type-specific Linear box and the curve between them - and give each relation-specific weight box a two-tone outline (target colour on top, source colour below), so heterogeneous paths can be traced without labels on the curves.

figures.title: HiFi-GAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Efficient and High Fidelity Speech Synthesis

taxonomy.note: multi-stream = the MRF sums parallel residual blocks of different kernel sizes and dilations; hierarchical = progressive transposed-conv upsampling

arrangement.units: three filled panels in a row at increasing zoom (lavender trapezoid generator, peach rounded MRF panel, pale square ResBlock panel), linked by grey dashed zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: the text label 'Mel-Spectrogram' above a vertical arrow
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three panels at increasing zoom sit in a row (generator, MRF, ResBlock), each opened from a box in the previous one by grey dashed projection lines.
insights.data: No data is drawn: the input and output are text labels ('Mel-Spectrogram', 'Raw Waveform') on a single vertical arrow through each panel, and all sizes are typeset indices like k_r[n] and D_r[n,m,l].
insights.emphasis: Red dashed frames with red italic 'for … ' headers mark every repeated structure, and the inner hyper-parameters are bold math inside each block.
insights.flow: Within each panel data runs straight top to bottom on one centred arrow; the panels themselves read left to right as successive zoom-ins.
insights.avoid: Input and output are bare text labels and the loop bounds (|k_u|, |k_r|, |D_r[n]|) are symbols only, so the figure cannot be read without the caption and text.

figures.lesson: Draw repeated layers as code-like loops: a red dashed frame with a red 'for l = 1 … N' header around the repeated block, nested for nested loops, so the configuration indices map directly onto the drawing.

figures.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: multi-hop retrieval with a knowledge graph memory

arrangement.units: rows = Offline Indexing / Online Retrieval (bold labels at left), columns = three components with headings over a rule; no boxes, alignment does the grouping
arrangement.inputs_as: icon cards for passages and a 'Query' pill
arrangement.shared: the same LLM, encoders and KG drawn in both rows of each column

insights.structure: Three columns (Neocortex/LLM, Parahippocampal Regions/Retrieval Encoders, Hippocampus/KG + Personalized PageRank) each headed by a brain illustration and a two-line underlined title, crossed by two rows: Offline Indexing and Online Retrieval.
insights.data: Passages and query are tiny icon cards, extracted triples and entities are pink/peach rounded text boxes, encoders are trapezoid pairs with circle-token rows, and the KG is drawn as a blue crescent with icon nodes.
insights.emphasis: The brain-region analogy above each column frames the contribution, and the final PageRank step lights the retrieved path in yellow while other nodes fade.
insights.flow: Left to right within each row; dashed arrows link entities to their KG nodes, and the two rows share column alignment.
insights.avoid: Decorative brain illustrations and the hippo mascot take a third of the area without encoding method content.

figures.lesson: The knowledge graph is drawn inside a blob shaped and tinted like the hippocampus marked in the brain illustration heading its column, so the analogy the method is named after is carried by shape and colour instead of by labels.

figures.title: Honeybee: Locality-enhanced Projector for Multimodal LLM

taxonomy.task: visual projector design for multimodal LLMs
taxonomy.note: a facet not in the vocabulary

arrangement.units: a pipeline strip on top and below it one rounded tinted frame divided by dashed vertical lines into three captioned variant panels
arrangement.inputs_as: a real street photo
arrangement.shared: the top pipeline is shared; only the projector varies across panels

insights.structure: A top row shows the generic MLLM pipeline (photo, Vision Encoder, Projector, Large Language Model), and a dashed line drops from Projector into a rounded tinted panel split by dashed dividers into (a) Linear Projector, (b) Abstractor, (c) Locality-enhanced Abstractor.
insights.data: Visual features are grids of hollow ellipses, output visual tokens are yellow ellipses, text tokens blue circles; C-/D-Abstractor show grey or yellow local neighbourhoods on the grid.
insights.emphasis: Each variant carries a check/cross list for Flexibility and Locality Preservation, and only (c) has both green checks.
insights.flow: Top row left to right; the zoom drops down; each sub-panel reads left to right from feature grid through a projector box to output tokens.

figures.lesson: Zoom the one swappable connector box into a shaded panel below through a dashed leader, and score each variant with bold-green check / grey-cross property lines, so the paper's variant wins visually without a table.

figures.title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
figures.venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing

arrangement.units: one rounded grey model frame with stacked bars inside, and an unframed target row plus red box above it
arrangement.inputs_as: a waveform thumbnail
arrangement.losses_at: implicit: arrows from masked positions into target cells above the model
arrangement.shared: the waveform feeds both the model and the unit discovery system

insights.structure: A rounded grey HUBERT frame holds a CNN Encoder bar, a row of x/[MSK] token cells and a Transformer bar; above it sits a separate row of target cells z1-z6 under a red Acoustic Unit Discovery System box.
insights.data: Input is a blue waveform at the bottom; frames are small yellow cells with masked ones in orange labelled [MSK]; targets are pink z cells.
insights.emphasis: Masked cells are orange and only their positions send arrows up to the targets; the target-generation path is drawn as red dashed lines, distinct from grey model arrows.
insights.flow: Bottom to top through the model; a red dashed line leaves the waveform, runs up the right edge and over the top into the discovery box, then dashes down to the targets.
insights.avoid: The long red dashed loop around the whole figure is the only cue that targets come from the same audio and is easy to miss.

figures.lesson: The target generator is drawn on top, outside the model's container, in its own colour family with dashed red arrows, so its route reads as a separate side branch rather than part of the trained network; the targets row is the one place both branches meet.

figures.title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face

taxonomy.task: LLM-controlled planning and dispatch of AI tasks to expert models

arrangement.units: four rounded bordered stage panels in a 2x2 grid (task planning, model selection, task execution, response generation), framed by a full-width request bar above and a full-width response panel below; the LLM logo disc sits at the grid centre
arrangement.inputs_as: the user's request as a quoted sentence in a rounded bar across the top
arrangement.shared: the LLM is drawn once as a central logo disc touched by all four stage panels

insights.structure: A request bar on top, four stage panels in a 2x2 grid meeting at a central ChatGPT logo disc, and a full-width Response panel at the bottom with real result images and the final prose answer.
insights.data: Intermediate plans are drawn as real structured text: dashed task boxes with 'task: pose-det. / args: image: <resource-1>' lines, red task names and green resource placeholders, and outputs as actual images labelled [Image-1]...[Image-4] plus an audio speaker icon.
insights.emphasis: Stage headings are the largest type, the central logo makes the LLM the visual hub, and the expert-execution stage alone is tinted gold with a Hugging Face emoji so the 'LLM controls, experts execute' split reads by colour.
insights.flow: Reading runs Request -> Stage 1 (top-left) -> Stage 2 (top-right) -> Stage 3 (bottom-left) -> Stage 4 (bottom-right) -> Response, with panel adjacency rather than arrows carrying the order and a hollow 'Predictions' arrow bridging Stage 3 to Stage 4.
insights.avoid: The bottom Response paragraph is a dense block of small text with inline emoji and gold model names that cannot be read at figure size, and the task-dependency arrows in Stage 1 cross each other over the task boxes.

figures.lesson: Put the controller as a single logo disc at the junction of a 2x2 stage grid so all four stages visibly touch it, and give the one stage run by other components (the expert models) its own colour family.

figures.title: HUMUS-Net: Hybrid Unrolled Multi-Scale Network Architecture for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction

arrangement.units: one grey rounded panel for the whole denoiser plus one green-framed zoom panel below it that expands the MUST sub-module; sub-blocks are pastel boxes and trapezoids
arrangement.inputs_as: real MRI image thumbnail outside the panel's left edge, output image outside the right edge
arrangement.shared: global residual skip from input to output across the top of the panel

insights.structure: A grey rounded top panel holds the hybrid denoiser (Hi-Res Feature Extraction -> Low-Res Feature Extraction -> MUST -> Hi-Res Image Reconstruction), and dotted zoom lines open the small MUST thumbnail into a full-width green bottom panel showing its U of RSTB-D / RSTB-B / RSTB-U blocks.
insights.data: Real knee MR images sit outside the top panel as 'Noisy image' and 'Denoised image'; intermediate tensors are named F_H, F_L, F_D on the arrows and every U-level edge carries its shape (h/4 * w/4 * 2d etc.) as a math label.
insights.emphasis: The contribution MUST is the one green-tinted box in the top panel, and its green colour is reused as the background of the zoom panel so the detail is tied to it by hue as well as by the dotted lines.
insights.flow: Top panel reads left to right with a long global residual arrow over the top into a circled-plus; the bottom panel reads as a U (down the left, across RSTB-B, up the right) with dashed red horizontal skip arrows; blue lines mean image representation and red lines token representation.
insights.avoid: The figure shows only the denoiser, not the unrolled k-space cascade that makes HUMUS-Net an unrolled network, and it carries two separate legends (bottom-left of each panel) instead of one key.

figures.lesson: Colour the connectors by representation - blue for image-space lines, red for token lines, dashed red for skips - so the switch into and out of the transformer is visible at the patch-embed triangles without labelling each arrow.

figures.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by whitespace, each titled by a bold caption beneath it
arrangement.inputs_as: circled symbols x, y, z
arrangement.losses_at: top of each panel as a red D(.,.) box
arrangement.shared: x-encoder and y-encoder boxes repeated identically across panels

insights.structure: Three unframed side-by-side schematics captioned (a) Joint-Embedding, (b) Generative, (c) Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, each built from the same grey encoder boxes so only the changed part differs.
insights.data: Inputs x, y and the conditioning variable z are drawn as circles at the bottom; embeddings s_x, s_y and predictions are italic math labels on the arrows; no real data is shown.
insights.emphasis: Red is reserved for the energy D(.,.) box (red outline, pink fill) at the top of each panel and the red z circle that marks conditioning, so the eye compares where the loss is computed across the three.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: solid arrows from inputs up through encoders, dashed arrows into the red D box at the top right of each panel.
insights.avoid: Grey low-contrast boxes and very thin dashed arrows make the encoders recede; acceptable for an abstract comparison but too faint for a detailed method figure.

figures.lesson: Compare architecture families with a shared tiny grammar (input circles at the bottom, pale encoder boxes, one red-outlined objective box at the top), and spend the only accent colour on the objective and the latent, the parts that differ between panels.

figures.title: iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer

taxonomy.task: masked image modelling pretraining with an online tokenizer

arrangement.units: one composition with two stacked branches; the teacher's network and patch head grouped in a grey shaded rounded region
arrangement.inputs_as: a square box 'x ~ I' splitting into two coloured patch grids
arrangement.losses_at: right, as arcs and crossing dashed arrows between the output token columns
arrangement.shared: EMA arrow from student f_s to teacher f_t; stop-grad on teacher outputs

insights.structure: Two stacked branches share the left input: student f_s with heads h_s^[CLS], h_s^patch on top and teacher f_t with its heads below, the teacher plus patch head wrapped in a grey rounded region labeled 'online tokenizer', and an EMA arrow points down between them.
insights.data: The two augmented views u (blue) and v (orange) are drawn as 3x3 patch grids and then as vertical token columns, with hatched cells marking masked tokens (e_[MASK] key bottom-left); outputs are again columns of coloured cells.
insights.emphasis: The teacher-as-tokenizer is singled out by the grey shaded backdrop, and the two losses L_[CLS] (grey dashed) and L_MIM (black solid curved arcs) are written large at the top right.
insights.flow: Left to right: input box -> view split -> crossing blue/orange lines that swap views into each branch -> encoders -> heads -> token outputs; on the right, dashed grey arrows cross diagonally between branches for the CLS loss and solid arcs curve up within each view for MIM.
insights.avoid: The crossing view-swap lines and the X of dashed L_[CLS] arrows over the output columns make the right third hard to trace; stop-grad marks are tiny.

figures.lesson: Colour-code the two augmented views (blue / orange) and let that colour run through every token cell and routing line derived from each view, with masked cells as a hatched glyph defined in a corner legend, so the cross-view pairing of the losses can be followed by colour alone.

figures.title: IBRNet: Learning Multi-View Image-Based Rendering

arrangement.units: unframed scene area on the left, a beige tinted network panel in the middle with a rounded zoom inset, and an unframed output column on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real photographs of the scene as tilted source/target view cards
arrangement.losses_at: bottom-right, rendering loss equation with colour swatches
arrangement.shared: one MLP applied to each ray sample (three identical stacks)

insights.structure: Three zones left to right: a scene zone with real source photos (green frames A, B) and a red-dotted target view around a wire cube pierced by an orange ray, a beige tinted network zone with per-sample MLPs feeding a rounded 'Ray Transformer', and a right column with a volume-rendering density plot above a rendering-loss equation.
insights.data: Inputs are real toy photographs; sample points on the ray are blue dots whose projections into source views are dashed coloured lines; per-view features are hatched striped bars keyed as image color / viewing direction / image feature.
insights.emphasis: A callout wedge from the MLP stack opens a rounded inset showing how views A and B feed one MLP, and the loss is shown with actual coloured squares color_pred - color_gt inside a norm.
insights.flow: Left to right along horizontal arrows from ray samples to MLPs to Ray Transformer to sigma outputs, then a hollow block arrow right to the density plot and a hollow arrow down to the loss.
insights.avoid: The colour-coded hatched feature swatches are small and need the inset key to decode; the scene zone has no frame so it is grouped only by proximity.

figures.lesson: Reuse the scene ray as the density plot's x-axis, with the same coloured sample dots placed on it, so the volume-rendering step visibly comes from the ray drawn in the scene.

figures.title: What matters when building vision-language models?

arrangement.units: one pipeline with module boxes (teal encoder, blue projection, tall peach LLM) and no enclosing frames
arrangement.inputs_as: an image icon with resolution text and a text glyph
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single top row Vision encoder -> hidden states -> 'Modality projection + Pooling' feeds a tall peach LLM column at the right, while a text line runs along the bottom into the same column.
insights.data: The image is an icon with 'Up to 980x980'; hidden states are stacked green squares, pooled visual tokens are labelled '64', and text tokens are dark orange squares, so the LLM's input column interleaves green and orange cells.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the message: green visual tokens and orange text tokens alternate in the LLM's input column, showing images inserted into the text sequence.
insights.flow: Left to right, image path on top and text path along the bottom, both curving into the LLM's input column; outputs exit right as orange squares.
insights.avoid: The big serif 'TT' glyph for text and the curved arrows that cross each other just before the LLM are clumsy; no loss is shown.

figures.lesson: Turn the LLM into a tall vertical bar at the right edge and stack its input sequence as one column of squares down its left side, so interleaved image-token runs (green, counted '64') and text tokens (orange) read as one ordered sequence.

figures.title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All

taxonomy.task: joint embedding of six modalities via image-paired data

arrangement.units: a row of samples, then the binding diagram at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos, depth, thermal and video frames, each titled with its source
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A row of five captioned real-data tiles (Web Image-Text, Depth Sensor Data, Web Videos, Thermal Data, Egocentric Videos) leads to a hexagonal graph on the right where the image node sits at the centre connected to the other modality icons.
insights.data: Each data source is a real photograph (or stacked frames for video) with the modality icons it pairs shown beside its title; a caption 'Sheep basking in the sun' stands for text.
insights.emphasis: The binding idea is drawn in the graph: thick solid edges for naturally aligned pairs (all through images) versus thin dashed edges for emergent alignment, with an 'IMAGEBIND' label and arrow pointing at the hub.
insights.flow: Read left to right across the data tiles into the graph; the top legend band is read first.
insights.avoid: It shows no encoders or loss, so it cannot serve as a model-architecture skeleton; the photos dominate and the key result (the graph) is small at the far right.

figures.lesson: When the figure is about data pairings, show one real sample per pairing with its modality icons, and keep the icon key in one strip at the top edge.

figures.title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting

arrangement.units: two blue dashed rounded frames, Encoder and Decoder, titled at the top inside
arrangement.inputs_as: cell strips of sequence tokens with math labels
arrangement.shared: encoder feature map feeds the decoder cross-attention

insights.structure: Two blue dashed rounded frames side by side, Encoder on the left and Decoder on the right, with a purple dashed 'Concatenated Feature Map' tab on the encoder and a Fully Connected Layer plus output row above the decoder.
insights.data: Inputs are two-row cell strips at the bottom (X_en, and X_de = {X_token, X_0} whose right half is filled with zeros); outputs are a cell row whose predicted cells are yellow.
insights.emphasis: Encoder self-attention layers are drawn as narrowing trapezoids stacked (plus a smaller side replica) to show the distilling halving, and the zero-padded decoder input marks the generative one-shot decoding.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each frame; one line leaves the encoder top, runs over and down into the decoder's Multi-head Attention block from the left.
insights.avoid: The unlabeled small trapezoid stack beside the encoder is ambiguous without the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw the decoder input as a token row of filled start tokens followed by cells marked 0 for the horizon, and fill only the matching output cells, so start-token-plus-placeholder generative decoding is read from the cells.

figures.title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: self-attention distilling in a time-series encoder

arrangement.units: one pipeline of 3-D blocks, each block labelled underneath in bold, no enclosing frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D slab of time-step cells with scalar and timestamp rows
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One left-to-right chain of 3-D blocks: input embedding (scalar + stamp) -> Attention Block 1 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 2 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 3 -> Feature Map.
insights.data: The input window is a green slab of cells labelled T = t to T = t + D_x split into Scalar and Stamp; attention blocks are beige translucent boxes holding red head slices; Conv1d outputs are thin blue/cyan slabs; dimensions L, L/2, L/4, d, k, n-heads are written on edges.
insights.emphasis: The shrinking size of successive attention blocks (L -> L/2 -> L/4) makes the distilling halving visible without text.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along teal arrows; dashed projection lines fan from the input slab into the embedding bars.
insights.avoid: Rotated dimension labels overlap the slabs ('MaxPool1d, padding=2' collides with L/2), and the dense 3-D perspective is heavy for what is a 1-D sequence.

figures.lesson: Show sequence-length halving by drawing each successive attention block as a smaller 3-D box with L, L/2, L/4 written on its length edge, so the distilling is read from the geometry before any label.

figures.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

taxonomy.task: LLM planning for robot manipulation with closed-loop language feedback

arrangement.units: vertical columns, one per role (planner dialogue, feedback sources), divided by a dashed rule, plus an unframed photo column
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted human instruction in a chat bubble with avatar
arrangement.shared: feedback bubbles reply to action bubbles across the dashed rule

insights.structure: Three titled columns: 'Robot Planning & Interaction' (a chat transcript), 'Grounded Closed-Loop Feedback' separated by a dashed vertical rule, and 'Robot Environments' with three stacked photos (a)-(c).
insights.data: Everything is real dialogue: human turns in grey bubbles with a person avatar, robot actions in dashed orange-labelled bubbles 'Action: "pick up the coke"', feedback bubbles from Scene Descriptor and Success Detector icons, plus one real scene photo.
insights.emphasis: Feedback outcomes are coloured red 'not successful' vs green 'successful', and a small hub diagram at the top of the middle column shows robot, human, scene descriptor and success detector exchanging messages.
insights.flow: Top to bottom as a conversation; grey diagonal arrows zigzag between the left action bubbles and the middle feedback bubbles to show the closed loop.
insights.avoid: The right environments column is unrelated to the loop and competes for attention; there is no explicit LLM block, so the planner is implicit.

figures.lesson: Draw the closed loop as a chat transcript: robot actions in dashed bubbles on one side, perception feedback in solid bubbles with source icons on the other, joined by zig-zag arrows in time order, with outcome words in red and green.

figures.title: Instant Neural Graphics Primitives with a Multiresolution Hash Encoding

taxonomy.task: multiresolution hash encoding for neural fields

arrangement.units: one pipeline with no frames; each step separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: a query point x arrow into a gridded domain over a faded 3-D object
arrangement.shared: same level colours reused across all steps

insights.structure: Four steps left to right: a 2-D domain with two grid levels over a faded bunny, two hash tables of size T each linked to a voxel square, a concatenated feature vector y, and an MLP m(y; Phi).
insights.data: Grid levels are colour-coded (red l=1, blue l=0) with vertex indices in circles; hash tables are 8-row two-column cell arrays whose looked-up rows are filled in the level colour; the feature vector stacks red, blue and green (auxiliary xi) cells with brackets L*F and E.
insights.emphasis: The two-colour level code runs consistently from grid to hash-table rows to interpolation squares to vector segments, so each level can be followed by hue.
insights.flow: Left to right: a curved arrow brings query x into the grid, elbow lines connect corners to table rows, curved arrows carry interpolated values into y, then straight arrows into and out of the MLP.
insights.avoid: The elbow connectors from table rows to square corners overlap and are hard to trace; step numbers and labels are cut off at the top of the crop.

figures.lesson: Explain a multi-level lookup on a 2-D slice: give each resolution level one colour and repeat it on its grid cell, its table rows and its slice of the concatenated feature column, leaving the downstream network grey.

figures.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning

arrangement.units: the overview column on the left (unframed) and a dashed rounded grey zoom panel on the right for the Q-Former internals
arrangement.inputs_as: two cartoon images under the frozen image encoder and the instruction as a quoted multi-line text card in the bottom-left corner; queries and instruction as token rows at the top of the column
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the response 'left one' is a quoted pill at the bottom of the column
arrangement.shared: the instruction token row is drawn three times (top of the overview, beside the LLM input, under the zoom panel) rather than linked with long lines

insights.structure: A central top-to-bottom column holds the trainable path (Q-Former, Fully Connected, LLM), the frozen image encoder hangs in a left column, and the Q-Former internals get their own dashed panel on the right.
insights.data: Learned queries are rows of coloured squares (red, yellow, green, blue with an ellipsis) and instruction tokens rows of empty squares, each row inside a rounded tray whose outline colour changes after each stage; the instruction itself is a quoted text card.
insights.emphasis: Trainable modules are pale yellow and frozen ones solid blue with snowflakes, and the modified Q-Former is the only module given a zoomed detail panel.
insights.flow: Read down the central column from the token rows to the response pill; the image embeddings arrive from the left with a labelled side arrow, and two dashed grey lines fan right from the Q-Former box to the zoom panel.
insights.avoid: The instruction text card in the bottom-left is far from where the instruction tokens enter at the top of the column, with no line linking them.

figures.lesson: Expand the one modified module into a dashed side panel tied to its overview box by two dashed projection lines, and re-draw the same input token rows under it so the reader sees exactly where the new input (the instruction) enters.

figures.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

taxonomy.task: aligning a language model with human feedback

arrangement.units: three columns divided by thin vertical rules, each titled 'Step N' plus a bold heading
arrangement.inputs_as: a light-blue prompt card with quoted example text
arrangement.losses_at: bottom of each column (trained SFT, RM, reward r_k)
arrangement.shared: the same prompt example reused in steps 1 and 2

insights.structure: Three columns separated by thin vertical rules, headed 'Step 1/2/3' with a bold sentence title; each column pairs left-aligned plain-English sentences with a right-aligned vertical stack of rounded grey cards.
insights.data: Prompts are light-blue cards with a small icon and quoted text ('Explain the moon landing to a 6 year old'); the labeler is a person avatar; models (SFT, RM, PPO) are small network glyphs; rankings are lettered circles 'D > C > A = B'.
insights.emphasis: Each step's sentence-per-card explanation lets a non-expert read it, and blue arrows mark where data trains a model (and the blue feedback loop from r_k back to PPO in step 3).
insights.flow: Top to bottom inside each column with grey arrows, columns read left to right; only step 3 has a return loop on the right edge.
insights.avoid: The heavy prose occupies half of each column, which suits a blog-style overview but not a dense paper figure; no arrows link the steps to each other.

figures.lesson: Set a plain-language sentence beside each card, at the same height, in a left text column, so each column reads as a captioned storyboard and the cards themselves need only a word or an icon.

figures.title: InstructPix2Pix: Learning to Follow Image Editing Instructions

taxonomy.task: instruction-based image editing trained on generated paired data

arrangement.units: Two titled halves divided by a thin vertical rule; the left half holds three stacked grey rounded strips (a), (b), (c), the right half one grey rounded panel (d); every panel has a bold lettered title at its top left.
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted italic captions and instructions; real image pairs (generated) and a real painting at inference
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training of the model is only stated in the caption

insights.structure: Left two-thirds: three lettered grey strips stacked top to bottom (text edits, paired images, training examples); right third: one tall grey panel for inference, with a thin vertical rule between the halves.
insights.data: All text is shown as real quoted strings ('photograph of a girl riding a horse' -> 'have her ride a dragon') and all images as real before/after photo pairs, four pairs in a row in strip (c).
insights.emphasis: The contribution is shown by example rather than by structure: panel (d) is the largest and holds a large before/after painting pair with the InstructPix2Pix box between them.
insights.flow: Inside each strip, short arrows run left to right from inputs through a blue model box to outputs; between strips the reader moves top to bottom, then across the divider to (d).
insights.avoid: No arrow links strip (c) to the model in (d), and no training step or loss is drawn, so how the generated dataset trains InstructPix2Pix is left to the caption.

figures.lesson: When the contribution is a generated dataset plus a model, give the data pipeline lettered strips stacked on the left and the model a single tall panel on the right, and draw every example as real quoted text and real image pairs.

figures.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks

taxonomy.task: vision foundation model aligned with an LLM

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each with a caption below
arrangement.inputs_as: plain text words
arrangement.losses_at: top, objective names joined by arcs
arrangement.shared: shared-weights double arrow between the two LLM trapezoids

insights.structure: Three captioned panels (a) Supervised, (b) Contrastive, (c) InternVL, built from the same white trapezoid encoders, with panel (c) holding three trapezoids (vision encoder, LLM, LLM).
insights.data: Inputs are plain words 'image', 'text', 'prompt' under up-arrows; objectives are plain words 'classes', 'contrastive', 'generative' at the top.
insights.emphasis: Panel (c) is the widest, its encoder label adds a bold 'to 6B #params' with 6B in red, a thick grey double arrow marks 'shared weights' between the two LLMs, and the caption says '(ours)'.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each encoder; curved arcs at the top join pairs of encoders into an objective, with one long arc from the vision encoder to the generative LLM.
insights.avoid: The long arc over panel (c) and the plain-word inputs make it a positioning diagram, not an architecture; nothing about the bridge module is shown.

figures.lesson: Contrast pre-training paradigms with identical blank trapezoids and arched arrows to one objective word each, letting the 'ours' panel differ only by an extra trapezoid and one red-bold number written inside its encoder.

figures.title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

arrangement.units: three unenclosed horizontal lanes (image, latent/U-Net, text); one orange dashed rounded box encloses the two parallel cross-attention modules
arrangement.inputs_as: real image thumbnail (top) and a quoted text prompt (bottom)
arrangement.shared: two horizontal buses above the U-Net carry both attention outputs to every U-Net block

insights.structure: Three horizontal lanes: image branch on top (Image Encoder, Linear, LN, Image Features row) ending in a dashed 'Decoupled Cross-Attention' box at top right, the bowtie Denoising U-Net with x_t and x_{t-1} slabs in the middle, and the text branch at the bottom (prompt, Text Encoder, Text Features row).
insights.data: The image prompt is a real painting thumbnail, the text prompt is a quoted sentence, features are short rows of cells, and the noisy latents x_t / x_{t-1} are 3-D slabs flanking the U-Net.
insights.emphasis: Trainable modules are pink with a flame icon and frozen ones light blue with a snowflake, so the new parts (Linear, LN, image Cross Attention) pop out; a two-swatch legend at bottom right explains the code.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each lane; the two Cross Attention outputs drop as orange and blue buses onto every U-Net block bar, and the text-feature line runs to the right edge and climbs the whole height into the frozen Cross Attention.
insights.avoid: The long text-feature wire looping around the right edge up to the top box is a detour that is hard to follow; place the text and image attention inputs nearer their sources.

figures.lesson: Two parallel buses above the backbone drop a side-by-side pair of arrows (blue from the original condition, orange from the added one) onto every U-Net block, showing that the new conditioning is injected alongside the old at each block without drawing any block internals.

figures.title: Transformers are Sample-Efficient World Models

arrangement.units: repeated unboxed time-step columns labeled by bottom braces; nested thin rectangles enclose the accumulated sequence
arrangement.inputs_as: symbol x_0
arrangement.shared: the same E, D, G, pi arrows repeat in every column

insights.structure: A timeline unrolled left-to-right into time-step columns t=0, t=1, ..., t=s marked by curly braces at the bottom, each column holding a dashed token box z^1..z^K plus action a_t; nested plain rectangles around the growing token sequence show the transformer context expanding.
insights.data: Everything is math symbols: frame x_0, tokens z, reconstructions x-hat, actions a, predicted reward r-hat and done d-hat; no images or blocks for networks, which appear only as letters on arrows (E, D, G, pi).
insights.emphasis: Each network gets a colour on its arrows: green for encoder/decoder E/D, indigo for the world-model G (thick), magenta for policy pi, making the imagination loop readable without boxes.
insights.flow: x_0 drops down via E into tokens, D drops to x-hat, pi hooks back up to a_t, and thick indigo G arrows run right to the next step while branching upward to r-hat and d-hat.
insights.avoid: The nested context rectangles are thin unlabeled outlines whose meaning (growing attention window) is not stated in the figure.

figures.lesson: Show a transformer's growing context by nesting thin outline rectangles, each one time step wider, around the unrolled tokens, instead of drawing attention arrows.

figures.title: ISTA-Net: Interpretable Optimization-Inspired Deep Network for Image Compressive Sensing

arrangement.units: Top row: three pale-green rounded phase panels (1-th, k-th, Np-th) in a line, separated by dotted ellipses; bottom: a wide dashed-outline zoom box containing one enlarged green phase panel.
arrangement.inputs_as: a small real grayscale photo with a red border, followed by thin vertical bars for the image vector x and its measurements y
arrangement.shared: the same phase structure is drawn three times in the top row with superscripts (1), (k), (Np); the k-th copy is expanded below rather than redrawn separately

insights.structure: A top row of identical pale-green phase panels (1-th, k-th, Np-th) joined by dotted ellipses, with the k-th one expanded by a grey dashed zoom outline into a full-width panel underneath.
insights.data: Image vectors and iterates are thin upright bars colour-coded by role (green x, dark blue r, orange y), and inside the detail panel feature maps become stacks of blue rectangles before the threshold and green ones after, each labelled N_f.
insights.emphasis: The learnable transform F(k), its inverse F~(k) and the Soft(., theta) step are the only saturated colour tags, and in the detail the two transforms are boxed in red dotted frames that mirror each other around the threshold.
insights.flow: Everything reads left to right on thick grey arrows; in the detail the path rises through a fat diagonal arrow into the Soft box above the line and drops back down, making the threshold a visible bump in the pipeline.
insights.avoid: Colour encodes three different things at once (vector role, pre/post-threshold feature maps, operator identity), and the tiny red 'CS Sampling' and green 'Initialization' labels are rotated vertically between bars, which is hard to read.

figures.lesson: Draw an unrolled optimiser as a row of identical tinted phase panels with ellipses between them, and pull one phase out through a dashed zoom box into a full-width detail panel, keeping the same tint so the reader knows it is the same unit.

figures.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting

arrangement.units: two unenclosed rows (Transformer view, iTransformer view), each a plot followed by a 3-D cube pipeline
arrangement.inputs_as: multivariate line plots with token markings
arrangement.shared: same pipeline order (embedding, attention, FFN, representation) in both rows

insights.structure: Two stacked rows contrast the vanilla Transformer view (top) with the iTransformer view (bottom), joined by a purple 'Invert' arrow on the left; each row pairs a multivariate line plot with a 3-D cube pipeline of attention and FFN.
insights.data: Inputs are three coloured time-series curves; tokens are red vertical bars across time (top) vs dashed boxes around each whole series (bottom); representations are stacks of coloured cubes, grey for mixed and teal/gold per variate for unmixed.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the argument: red marks the time-step token and 'Mixed', blue marks the variate token and 'Unmixed', and the bottom row keeps per-variate colours through the cubes while the top row turns grey.
insights.flow: Each row reads left-to-right from plot through a hollow arrow into embed, attention slab, FFN slabs and output cubes; the eye compares the rows vertically.
insights.avoid: The translucent attention and FFN slabs are nearly identical between rows, so the difference relies on small rotated labels and cube colours.

figures.lesson: Contrast two tokenizations on the same drawn curves (a vertical bar across all variates at one time step vs a dashed box around one whole variate) and keep the variate colours in the 3-D token cubes only for the proposed row, with grey cubes meaning mixed.

figures.title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models

arrangement.units: each step is a bordered table panel with a header title and formula; panels align in two rows (datastore, test)
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text contexts in table cells
arrangement.shared: the encoder f appears as identical Representation panels in both rows

insights.structure: A grid of titled table panels: the datastore row on top (Training Contexts, Targets, Representations, Distances, Nearest k, Normalization, Aggregation) and the test row below (Test Context, Target, Representation, Classification, Interpolation), each panel headed by its name and formula.
insights.data: Real example sentences about Obama fill cyan cells, targets sit in yellow cells, representations are rows of grey-shaded circles in pink cells, and every intermediate is a small table of words with numbers in a purple column.
insights.emphasis: A consistent colour per data type (cyan contexts, yellow words, pink vectors, green distances, purple probabilities) lets one worked example be traced through every step to Hawaii 0.6.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the top row, the query vector climbs from the bottom row into Distances, the top row ends in Aggregation which drops down into Interpolation where the LM Classification row joins from the left.
insights.avoid: Many crossing arrows between Distances and Nearest k and between Normalization and Aggregation make the sorting step look tangled.

figures.lesson: Colour encodes the kind of value (sentence, word, vector, distance, probability) and stays the same in every table, so one worked example can be traced row by row through the pipeline without a legend.

figures.title: Language Is Not All You Need: Aligning Perception with Language Models

taxonomy.note: the figure draws the MLLM as one decoder bar over embedded multimodal input; paradigm GPT = a causal language model taking interleaved input

arrangement.units: an unframed model schematic across the top half, then three rounded outlined example panels of equal width in a row
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos, a receipt image and a waveform inside one rounded grey tray, labelled Vision and Audition
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; 'output' with an up-arrow at the top-right of the model bar
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The top half is a three-level bottom-to-top schematic (input tray, Embedding chip, model bar) and the bottom half three equal rounded example panels, so model and capability demos are separated by whitespace.
insights.data: Inputs are real images, a receipt and a waveform in one grey tray, and the interleaved input is a sentence with three green token squares inline; demos are chat bubbles, pale blue for prompts and pale pink for model output.
insights.emphasis: The MLLM bar spans the full width in bold type with a robot icon, and 'Kosmos-1' is bold at the start of the sentence beneath it.
insights.flow: Short black up-arrows run tray -> Embedding -> sentence -> MLLM -> output; the example panels below have no arrows and are read left to right.
insights.avoid: The model is a single undifferentiated bar, so the figure says nothing about how the embedding connects to the language model; it works only as a teaser, not as an architecture reference.

figures.lesson: Show that a model reads interleaved modalities by writing a plain sentence with small coloured token squares set inline where the image would go, directly under the model bar.

figures.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models

taxonomy.task: LM agent reasoning, acting and planning via Monte Carlo tree search

arrangement.units: six unbordered columns, one per search operation, each titled with a number and name and holding a small tree or LM chain
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue 'Input' ellipse as the tree root at the top of each panel
arrangement.shared: the LM is redrawn as the same lavender box in the Evaluation and Reflection panels

insights.structure: Six borderless panels in a single row, each a numbered MCTS operation drawn on the same small tree of an Input ellipse and S1/S2/S3 squares, with the Evaluation and Reflection panels replacing the tree by a vertical LM -> Value / LM -> Reflection chain.
insights.data: States are small labelled squares (S1, S2, S3), the root and terminal are blue Input and green Output ellipses, the language model is a lavender 'LM' box and its products are pale yellow 'Value' and 'Reflection' boxes.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the operation: the selected node is solid red, the active branch is pink with red arrows, unexplored siblings are grey, and backpropagation adds thicker red upward arrows beside the downward ones.
insights.flow: Read panels left to right by their 1) to 6) titles; within each panel arrows run top to bottom down the tree, except Backpropagation where paired arrows point back up to the root.
insights.avoid: The 'Value' and 'Reflection' boxes use very small type relative to the S-node labels, and the panels have no separators so 'S' in panel 6 floats without context.

figures.lesson: Show a search algorithm as a filmstrip of the same tree, one panel per operation, recolouring only the nodes the current operation touches.

figures.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: conditional image synthesis in a learned latent space

arrangement.units: three tinted, rounded panels side by side: Pixel Space (red tint), Latent Space (green tint, with a nested Denoising U-Net frame), Conditioning (grey)
arrangement.inputs_as: image x as a purple rounded square at top-left; conditioning types (semantic map, text, representations, images) as stacked coloured cards at right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three tinted panels left to right (pixel, latent, conditioning), with the U-Net nested as a second-level frame inside the latent panel and a glyph legend under all three.
insights.data: Images are symbolic purple squares x and x~, latents are tall dark-green bars labelled z, z_T, z_{T-1}, and the conditioning inputs are overlapping coloured cards rather than real examples.
insights.emphasis: The orange Q/K/V cross-attention squares are the only warm colour inside the blue U-Net, and every conditioning arrow from tau_theta lands on them.
insights.flow: Top row runs left to right (x -> E -> z -> diffusion -> z_T), then the bottom row runs back right to left through the U-Net and decoder to x~, with a small loop marked x(T-1) for repeated denoising.
insights.avoid: Conditioning lines from tau_theta run along the bottom edge and up into each attention block, crossing the grey dashed skip arrows, and the 'switch' glyph is hard to decode without the legend.

figures.lesson: Make the paper's key idea a region rather than a box: tint each 'space' (pixel, latent, conditioning) as its own panel so a reader sees where the computation happens before reading any module.

figures.title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images From Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D

taxonomy.task: lifting image features to a 3-D frustum

arrangement.units: one unboxed scene: a perspective camera sketch beside a labeled matrix with dimension brackets
arrangement.inputs_as: real street photo on a tilted image plane
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two halves: on the left a tilted street photo with rays fanning from a camera icon and bars along one ray; on the right a C x D heat-map grid labeled 'per-pixel outer product'.
insights.data: Depth distribution alpha is drawn as blue bars of varying length along the ray and as a vertical colour strip, feature c as a second strip; their product is a blue-shaded matrix with columns alpha_0 c ... alpha_D c.
insights.emphasis: The darkest column in the matrix matches the longest bar on the ray, visually tying the peak depth to where the feature is placed.
insights.flow: Two black arrows lead from the alpha and c strips into the matrix, left to right; rays converge on the camera at bottom right.

figures.lesson: Draw per-pixel depth as bars of different length laid along the camera ray, then show the lifted feature as a blue-shaded depth x channel matrix with dimension brackets, so the depth peak reappears as the matrix's darkest column.

figures.title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images From Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D

taxonomy.task: bird's-eye-view semantic segmentation from multi-camera images

arrangement.units: four unboxed pictorial stages, each captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of real camera photos
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Four stages in a row with captions underneath: stacked camera photos, a wireframe frustum labeled xN, six photos arranged around a top-down car with blue camera frusta, and a stack of BEV output maps.
insights.data: Inputs are real multi-camera photos stacked with grey arrows, the lift is a line-drawn frustum, the splat is the car icon with photos at their mounting positions, outputs are white maps with coloured blobs.
insights.emphasis: The central splat panel is the largest and most colourful, with blue translucent frusta radiating from the car, making the camera-to-BEV projection the focal point.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right with plain black arrows between stages; captions under each stage name the operation.
insights.avoid: No module boxes or tensor shapes are given, so it conveys the idea but not the network; the frustum xN glyph is abstract.

figures.lesson: Show the camera-to-BEV step as a top-view ego car ringed by its camera images, each under a translucent blue frustum fanning out from the car, so the rig geometry itself is the transform stage rather than a labelled box.

figures.title: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation

arrangement.units: two mirrored towers (user, item), each with stacked layer cards inside a dotted rectangle
arrangement.inputs_as: neighbor node circles with embedding symbols
arrangement.shared: the same LGC layer structure in both towers

insights.structure: Two mirrored columns, user u1 on the left and item i4 on the right, each a stack of Layer 1-3 cards inside a dotted box labeled Light Graph Convolution, with embedding stacks above meeting in a top prediction node.
insights.data: Neighbors are small circles with embedding symbols, the aggregator is a 'Normalized Sum' grey box, layer embeddings e^(k) are three-cell colour rows on a slanted parallelogram, e^(0) sits alone beside them.
insights.emphasis: Red text labels the two contributions ('Layer Combination (weighted sum)', 'Light Graph Convolution (LGC)'), and the dashed yellow loop arrows show layer repetition.
insights.flow: Bottom-up: neighbors feed the Normalized Sum, layers stack upward into embedding rows, which combine via circled-plus nodes into the red Prediction node at top.
insights.avoid: The slanted parallelograms and stacked card shadows add depth that conveys nothing and crowd the labels.

figures.lesson: Draw the user and the item as mirror-image towers, each fed only by its own few labelled neighbour circles and ending in an embedding row, so the towers meet at one score node at the top and the symmetry itself says 'user and item are treated alike'.

figures.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

arrangement.units: three rounded white panels with pill-shaped stage tags; a nested grey sub-panel for RLHF
arrangement.inputs_as: icon of pretraining data
arrangement.shared: a feedback loop from Llama-2-chat back into human feedback

insights.structure: Three rounded white panels with dark pill tags: HUMAN FEEDBACK at top left, PRETRAINING at bottom left, FINE-TUNING on the right containing a grey RLHF sub-panel and the Llama-2-chat block.
insights.data: Data and models are icons (cloud-database, person with speech bubbles, shield and hand icons for reward models); steps are diamonds and models are grey rounded rectangles.
insights.emphasis: Self-supervised learning is the only saturated blue diamond, and Llama-2-chat is the largest dark block; the RLHF loop is drawn as two circular arrows between the sub-panel and the chat model.
insights.flow: Bottom row runs left-to-right from pretraining data to Llama 2 to SFT to Llama-2-chat; a thick line from chat climbs over the top and returns into human feedback, whose reward models feed the RLHF sub-panel.
insights.avoid: Very low contrast pale grey arrows and lavender diamonds on a pale grey background make the flow hard to read in print.

figures.lesson: Encode node kind by shape across a multi-stage training pipeline (diamonds for training procedures, rounded grey boxes for model checkpoints, pale icon circles for data and reward models) and name each stage with an uppercase pill tab on its region's edge, so the stages and the iterative loops stay readable with only light-grey arrows.

figures.title: Visual Instruction Tuning

arrangement.units: horizontal colored bands for modules (LM, projection, encoder) with token rows floating between them
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols X_v Image and X_q Language Instruction
arrangement.shared: one LM band spans all tokens

insights.structure: A wide pale-green 'Language Model f_phi' band spans the figure; below it at left a blue Vision Encoder and peach Projection W band stack, and at the bottom the image X_v and instruction X_q inputs.
insights.data: Tokens are small house-shaped pentagons: light grey for image tokens H_v, darker grey for instruction tokens H_q, green for response tokens X_a; all quantities are math symbols.
insights.emphasis: The response tokens are the only saturated colour (green), and the minimal one-arrow projector makes the simplicity of the bridge the message.
insights.flow: Bottom-up: X_v curves through encoder and projection into H_v, X_q rises into H_q, and thin grey lines fan from all input tokens up through the LM band to the response tokens.
insights.avoid: The fan of thin grey lines through the LM band is faint and does not convey causal decoding; the curved Z_v arrow overlaps the stacked encoder bands awkwardly.

figures.lesson: Token glyphs graded by fill (light grey for visual, darker grey for instruction, saturated green for response) separate inputs from generated tokens without a legend.

figures.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale

arrangement.units: two stacked horizontal lanes, each a dashed-border rectangle titled just outside its top-left corner, with numbered steps inside
arrangement.inputs_as: small numeric matrices X and W with cells coloured cyan (regular) or yellow (outlier)
arrangement.shared: X and W are drawn once at the left and reach both lanes by two curved arrows; the lanes' outputs meet at one circled plus

insights.structure: Two dashed lanes stacked top and bottom, each with numbered steps inside, fan out from one input pair at the left and close at one circled plus at the right.
insights.data: Inputs and intermediates are toy numeric matrices with numbers in every cell, cyan for regular values and yellow for outlier columns, with precision tags as subscripts.
insights.emphasis: The yellow outlier columns are the thread: coloured in the inputs, absent from the 8-bit lane, and reappearing alone in the 16-bit lane.
insights.flow: Start at the large title and the inputs at the left, follow the curved arrows into each lane, read its steps (1)-(4) left to right, then exit right into the plus and the output.
insights.avoid: Equations are set in a sans-serif font with uneven subscripts, and the large method name in the corner takes space without carrying content.

figures.lesson: Put toy numeric matrices in the figure and colour the special entries (outliers) in one hue, then show those same coloured columns pulled out into their own branch, so the split is visible without reading the text.

figures.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

arrangement.units: no enclosures: two side-by-side columns (a frozen-weight square and a stacked pair of trapezoids) between an input bar at the bottom and an output bar at the top
arrangement.inputs_as: a yellow bar labelled x with a brace marking its width d
arrangement.shared: the input x feeds both columns through two hollow block arrows, and their outputs meet at one plus glyph below h

insights.structure: A frozen weight square and a trainable trapezoid pair stand side by side as two parallel paths between one input bar and one output bar.
insights.data: Input and output are flat yellow bars labelled x and h, with their dimension given by a brace (d) rather than a tensor drawing.
insights.emphasis: Saturated orange trapezoids that pinch to a labelled width r set the trainable low-rank path apart from the single blue pretrained block.
insights.flow: Read bottom to top: from x up through both columns along hollow block arrows into the plus and out to h.
insights.avoid: Nothing in the figure marks W as frozen and A, B as trained; that distinction lives only in the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw a low-rank factorisation as two trapezoids that pinch to a narrow waist labelled r, beside one large square for the full matrix, so the size contrast says 'small trainable add-on' without text.

figures.title: LRM: Large Reconstruction Model for Single Image to 3D

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded boxes (encoder, triplane decoder, NeRF) arranged as stacked rows in a Z path
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo of the object with size annotation
arrangement.shared: camera features feed the M modulation diamonds across the decoder

insights.structure: Three dashed containers in a Z-shaped path: Image encoder (top row), Image-to-Triplane Decoder (middle row), Neural Radiance Field (bottom row), each annotated with layer counts and dimensions.
insights.data: Input and output are real renders of a toy giraffe, tokens are tall coloured column stacks (green image features, white positional embeddings, blue triplane tokens), the triplane is three intersecting blue planes and the NeRF is a wireframe cube around the 3-D model.
insights.emphasis: Every tensor carries an explicit 'Dim:' annotation and camera modulation is an orange M diamond explained in a top-right legend, so precise shapes rather than colour emphasize the design.
insights.flow: Top row left-to-right, a curved line drops image features into the decoder's Cross block, middle row runs right to DeConv and Reshape, then down to the triplane and the bottom row runs right-to-left to the rendered image.
insights.avoid: Dense dimension text in small font under nearly every element clutters the figure; the reversed right-to-left bottom row can surprise the reader.

figures.lesson: Fold a long encoder-decoder-renderer into three rows that read as a Z, put the drawn 3-D representation (intersecting feature planes) at the bottom-right turn, and write a 'Dim:' line under every data item so tensor sizes can be followed.

figures.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

arrangement.units: unboxed chain of image grids, token columns and two rounded grey module boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo with a patch-mask grid
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Five-step horizontal chain: masked input grid, column of visible patches, a large grey encoder, a long token column, a smaller grey decoder, a red token column, and the target image grid.
insights.data: Images are real flamingo photos cut into a 5x5 patch grid with masked patches greyed; tokens are coloured cells in vertical columns (teal encoded, grey mask tokens, red outputs).
insights.emphasis: Size encodes the asymmetry: the encoder box is much taller than the decoder, and only the few visible patches enter the encoder while mask tokens join later.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right with grey arrows; vertical token columns interleave teal and grey cells to show mask tokens being inserted.

figures.lesson: Draw the masked input as the photo cut into a grid with most cells filled flat grey, then carry the mask through the network as grey cells in the token columns, so the reader can count how few patches the encoder sees.

figures.title: Magic3D: High-Resolution Text-to-3D Content Creation

taxonomy.note: training-free here means the diffusion priors are frozen and only the 3D representation is optimised per prompt via score distillation

arrangement.units: two tinted rounded panels (pink stage 1, green stage 2) each holding render -> noise -> diffusion prior -> L_SDS; the 3D representation for each stage sits just outside the panel's left edge, the final model at the far right outside both
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in a yellow-glowing rounded box spanning both panels; the initial 3D representation is a rendered voxel-grid rabbit at the left
arrangement.losses_at: inside each stage panel at its right end (L_SDS over a residual image), with a coloured curved 'update' arrow running back under the panel to the 3D model
arrangement.shared: the single text prompt box feeds both stages by two yellow arrows

insights.structure: Two tinted rounded stage panels sit left and right with large numerals '1.' and '2.', each 3D representation placed in the gap before its panel, and a bottom label row with a thick green arrow naming the representation change.
insights.data: Every 3D state is a real render of the same rabbit (octree-voxel NeRF, coloured mesh, final textured model), the prompt is quoted verbatim, and noise is a small colour-noise square above each prior.
insights.emphasis: The prompt box glows yellow and feeds both priors via thick yellow arrows, while bold 'image' vs 'latent' under the two priors marks the one change between stages.
insights.flow: Read left to right: render arrows in orange go from each 3D model into its panel, grey arrows run through noise addition, prior and subtraction to L_SDS, and a coloured arc returns 'update' to the model under the panel.
insights.avoid: The large final render at the right is bigger than both panels and the forward render arrows are faint orange, so the eye lands on the output before the method.

figures.lesson: Show a coarse-to-fine method as two tinted panels with identical internal wiring (render -> add noise -> prior -> L_SDS -> curved update arrow back to the 3D model), so the only visible differences between the stages are the ones that matter.

figures.title: Make-A-Video: Text-to-Video Generation without Text-Video Data

arrangement.units: four perspective film-strip boxes of increasing size, each bordered in its stage colour
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text prompt on a card plus fps token
arrangement.shared: the prior embedding line feeds every stage

insights.structure: A cascade of perspective film-strip boxes receding diagonally: Spatiotemporal Decoder D^t (smallest, back), Frame Interpolation F, Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution SR_l^t and Spatial Super-Resolution SR_h (largest, front), with the text prompt and red prior P at left.
insights.data: Video is drawn as strips of real yoga-at-sunset frames growing in size and resolution, noise as grainy frames, the prompt as quoted text on a white card, the prior as a red 3-D bar.
insights.emphasis: Each stage has its own colour (blue, green, purple, black) for its title, box border and inter-frame arrows, and growing strip size encodes increasing resolution.
insights.flow: Text enters the prior at left, coloured feed lines rise into each stage, and arrows run diagonally front-down from each strip into the next larger one until the Generated Video y-hat.
insights.avoid: The overlapping perspective boxes and many small coloured arrows make it hard to see which frames interpolate or upsample which; ellipsis dots crowd the strips.

figures.lesson: Draw a cascade of video stages as receding film strips in perspective, each stage's strip, frame-to-frame arrows and name in its own colour, so temporal upsampling (more frames) and spatial upsampling (larger frames) show up as strip length and frame size.

figures.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions; a top band of state lanes and a lower band of parameter columns, separated only by position and colour
arrangement.inputs_as: x_t as a cell column at lower left and h_{t-1} as stacked sheets at upper left
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One unrolled recurrence step with no containers: four parallel orange state lanes span the top band from the stacked h_{t-1} sheets at far left through the A column (top centre) to h_t at far right, while x_t, B_t, Delta_t, C_t and y_t hang as green columns in a lower band.
insights.data: Vectors are tall pale-green columns (x_t and y_t as columns of square cells with only the top cell filled), each hidden state is a stack of offset orange sheets to show channels, and every element carries a large italic math symbol.
insights.emphasis: The selection mechanism is the only blue in the figure: a small 'Project' box plus three thick blue arrows into B_t, Delta_t and C_t, labelled once in bold blue 'Selection Mechanism' along the bundle.
insights.flow: State flows left to right along the straight orange lanes; the lower band feeds in by elbow-routed lines rising from B_t into the lanes before A and dropping from the lanes into C_t after A, with dashed fan lines from x_t into Project and a dashed 'Discretize' arrow from Delta_t.
insights.avoid: The GPU SRAM/HBM triangle in the bottom-right corner encodes memory levels only by colour reuse and is easily mistaken for part of the computation; the dense orange elbow crossings around A are hard to trace individually.

figures.lesson: Reserve one hue for the contribution and use it nowhere else: here a single blue box plus its blue arrow bundle, labelled once along the bundle, sits under an orange/green recurrence, so the eye finds the new mechanism without any container.

figures.title: Mask R-CNN

taxonomy.note: family other: two-stage CNN instance segmentation (Faster R-CNN plus a parallel mask head); the taxonomy has no CNN-detector family.

arrangement.units: No enclosed units: one left-to-right row of photo, feature slab, two RoI cubes and output photo, with a spur above the first cube.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo in perspective with one lavender RoI box drawn on it; the output is the same photo faded, overlaid with coloured instance masks
arrangement.shared: the first RoI cube feeds both the class/box spur (up) and the conv mask path (right)
