insights.structure: One row in shared perspective: input photo, a large feature slab, two gridded RoI cubes linked by 'conv' arrows, and the output photo, with the class/box head lifted onto a short spur above the first cube.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are real photos as tilted planes, the output overlaid with coloured instance masks; RoIs are lavender rectangles on the slab and RoI features are cubes with a gridded front face.
insights.emphasis: The RoIAlign step is the only coloured stroke (lavender RoI outlines and the RoIAlign arrow), and the mask branch is the main line ending at the masked photo.
insights.flow: Left to right along thin black arrows; one arrow branches up and right from the first cube to the 'class / box' bar, the rest runs straight to the output.
insights.avoid: The large feature slab and the RoI source (backbone, region proposals) carry no label, so a reader cannot tell what the slab is from the figure alone.

figures.lesson: Make the added branch the figure's main line and push the inherited heads onto a short side spur, so the new output reads as the destination.

figures.title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation

arrangement.units: two side-by-side regions split by a dashed rule: an unframed overview with coloured containers (blue decoder box, green trapezoid) and a framed grey detail panel of one layer
arrangement.inputs_as: query squares at left of the decoder; image features, mask and query features as small glyphs at the bottom of the detail panel
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; class and mask output boxes at right of the decoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Overview on the left and, across a dashed vertical rule, a tall grey detail panel of one decoder layer on the right; in the overview an orange Backbone trapezoid sits bottom-left, a green Pixel Decoder trapezoid widens diagonally up-right, and a light-blue 'Transformer Decoder L x' container with three grey blocks sits above it.
insights.data: Image features are lilac planes that grow in size along the pixel-decoder trapezoid; queries are a vertical rounded bar of four coloured squares that reappears as the output row at the top of the detail panel; class and mask outputs are small cream boxes.
insights.emphasis: In the detail panel the 'masked attention' box is the only saturated (deep pink) block with 'masked' in bold, and a cream 'mask' input enters it from outside the container in the same cream as the overview's mask output.
insights.flow: Overview reads backbone to pixel decoder left to right, then slanted arrows rise from successive feature maps into successive decoder blocks, and the decoder output meets the largest feature map at a circled-times to give the mask; the detail panel reads bottom to top with residual arrows looping up its right side.
insights.avoid: The long slanted arrows from feature maps to decoder blocks cross the gap at different angles and are hard to pair at a glance; the overview never shows where the detail panel's layer sits beyond the shared colours.

figures.lesson: Draw the multi-scale pixel decoder as a widening trapezoid of feature maps whose sizes grow along it, with one arrow from each map to a successive decoder block, so 'one resolution per layer' is read from geometry alone.

figures.title: Per-Pixel Classification is Not All You Need for Semantic Segmentation

arrangement.units: two formulations side by side split by a thin vertical rule; the right one holds N identical rounded-outline prediction boxes under a bracket
arrangement.inputs_as: the same real photo drawn as a tilted plane under each formulation
arrangement.losses_at: as coloured block arrows from ground-truth planes above each prediction; the per-pixel loss as a label at top-left
arrangement.shared: the same input photo is drawn once per formulation

insights.structure: A narrow left column (per-pixel formulation) and a wide right part (per-mask formulation) separated by a thin grey vertical rule; the right part repeats one rounded box N times ('prediction 1', 'prediction 2', ..., 'prediction N') gathered by a long grey bracket.
insights.data: Everything is drawn as tilted parallelogram planes: the input photo at the bottom, a colour semantic map and a K-channel stack on the left, grey binary ground-truth masks above and predicted soft masks inside each box on the right, each with a small column of coloured class cells braced 'K + 1'.
insights.emphasis: The proposed side takes about three quarters of the width and its two losses are the only saturated colours (orange mask-loss arrows, purple classification arrows labelled with the class name in that class's colour or the empty-set symbol).
insights.flow: Bottom to top: hollow white block arrows carry the input photo up into each formulation, and coloured block arrows come down from the ground truth onto the predictions.
insights.avoid: The left formulation's planes are stacked so tightly that the K-channel volume and its K brace are hard to read at small size.

figures.lesson: Contrast two segmentation formulations by drawing the outputs themselves as tilted mask planes: one K-channel volume for per-pixel classification against a row of N binary-mask planes each with its own (K+1) class column, with the two losses as two arrow colours.

figures.title: MAXIM: Multi-Axis MLP for Image Processing

taxonomy.task: multi-axis gated MLP block for image restoration
taxonomy.note: paradigm: gMLP / MLP-Mixer-style token mixing

arrangement.units: two horizontal tinted bands, one per branch, each running from its split grid to its merged grid; a separate framed detail panel at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare arrow into the LayerNorm stem; data as cell grids inside each band
arrangement.shared: stem and tail layers drawn once outside the bands

insights.structure: A main block with two stacked rounded tinted bands (pale pink 'Local Branch', pale green 'Global Branch', titles in bold red/green to their left) between a shared LayerNorm-Dense-GELU stem and a Concat-Dense-add tail, plus a separate pale-blue 'gMLP Block' detail panel at the far right behind a dashed rule.
insights.data: Tensors are drawn as literal 6 x 4 cell grids at each step (split, blocked/gridded, processed, unblocked), with processed cells outlined in different colours to show which tokens are mixed, and bracket shape annotations like [3 x 2, 2 x 2, C/2] whose changing numbers are coloured red or green.
insights.emphasis: The word 'gMLP' is bold blue at each application in both branches and matches the detail panel's blue title, while each branch's colour ties its title, its shape numbers and its axis label together.
insights.flow: Left to right through the stem, splitting into the two bands that run in parallel to a concat, then a dashed shortcut arrow from the stem rejoins at the final add; the detail panel reads bottom to top with a skip arrow up its left side.
insights.avoid: The multi-coloured cell outlines in the processed grids carry a lot of meaning but are too thin to decode at print size, and the gridded global result is hard to tell apart from the blocked local one.

figures.lesson: Draw the token layout as an actual small grid of cells at each reshaping step (split, blocked, processed, unblocked) and colour the shape numbers that change in the branch's own colour, so the reshaping reads from the drawing alone.

figures.title: MedCLIP: Contrastive Learning from Unpaired Medical Images and Text

taxonomy.task: medical image-text contrastive pretraining with decoupled unpaired data

arrangement.units: the unpaired sources in a top row; the paired data below in one frame with two dashed columns
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-rays and quoted report sentences with keywords highlighted
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; positive / negative captions under each column
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two dashed boxes on top ('Medical image datasets' with three X-rays, 'Medical text datasets' with bulleted report lines) above one large solid frame 'Medical image-text datasets' that holds two dashed columns facing each other across a central dashed grey circle.
insights.data: Inputs are real chest X-ray thumbnails and quoted report sentences in boxes with medical keywords ('opacity', 'pneumonia', 'extrapleural mass') highlighted in yellow.
insights.emphasis: The false-negative problem is made visible by colour: the right column's lines, text-box border and 'False negative' caption are red against the black lines and blue 'True positive' caption of the left column, and both texts share the highlighted word 'opacity'.
insights.flow: Inward: lines from the anchor image and its report (left) and from the negative image and its report (right) converge on the central circle that stands for the embedding space.
insights.avoid: The central grey circle is unlabelled, so the reader must infer that it is the shared embedding space; the figure motivates the problem but shows no encoder or loss.

figures.lesson: Show a supervision problem on two real image-report pairs with the words they share highlighted, instead of describing it.

figures.title: Segment Anything in Medical Images

taxonomy.task: universal medical image segmentation (dataset coverage teaser)

arrangement.units: one tiled mosaic of image cells with an overlaid illustration; no enclosed method regions
arrangement.inputs_as: real scans with colour mask overlays
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A 6-row grid of real medical image tiles (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, pathology) behind a large translucent anatomical body illustration placed over the centre.
insights.data: Each tile is a real scan with its segmentation mask laid on as a translucent colour overlay (cyan, green, orange, purple).
insights.emphasis: Coverage is the message: the body silhouette over the tiles ties the many modalities and organs to one model, with no diagram or labels at all.
insights.flow: No reading order; the eye scans the grid roughly head (top rows: brain scans) to pelvis and gut (bottom rows).
insights.avoid: The translucent body covers and washes out the central tiles, and there are no labels naming modality or target, so the figure carries no method information.

figures.lesson: For a 'one model for every task' teaser, tile real scans with their masks as translucent colour overlays, order the rows head to pelvis and lay a translucent anatomical body over the centre, so coverage is the whole message without any diagram.

figures.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

taxonomy.task: LLM inference acceleration with extra decoding heads

arrangement.units: three rounded tinted containers in a row (base model, added heads, predictions) plus a bottom row of grey boxes for input, candidates and output
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey box with a quoted question
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three rounded tinted containers left to right: blue 'Original Model' (Embedding, Transformer Layers, LM Head stacked bottom-up), red 'Medusa Heads' (three stacked numbered heads) and purple 'Top-k Predictions' (one text row per head), with three grey boxes along the bottom for Input, Candidates and Single step prediction.
insights.data: Tokens are shown as quoted text: a real question in the Input box, comma-separated top-k tokens per head ('is, ', the'), and candidate continuations with green-check / red-cross marks.
insights.emphasis: The added heads sit in the only red container with a flame icon in its title, while snowflake / flame icons on the original model mark it as frozen or trained.
insights.flow: Input rises into the original model, 'Last Hidden' fans right into each Medusa head, each head (and the LM head) feeds its own row of top-k tokens, then a return arrow drops into Candidates and on to the final single-step prediction at bottom right.
insights.avoid: The decorative llama-logo mascot at top centre carries no information and takes prime space.

figures.lesson: Mark frozen and trained parts with snowflake and flame icons in the container titles, and draw the added prediction heads as a stack of identical numbered boxes, each wired to its own row of top-k token text, so 'one head per future position' reads at a glance.

figures.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

taxonomy.task: tree attention for verifying candidate continuations

arrangement.units: an unframed token tree with tinted per-head containers on the left and an unframed attention grid on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: candidate tokens as labelled circles
arrangement.shared: the same token groups and tints appear in both the tree and the grid header

insights.structure: A token tree on the left (grey Root, a pink 'Head 1' container with 'It', 'I', an orange 'Head 2' container with two sub-groups of 'is, ', the') and an 8 x 8 attention grid on the right whose column header is the same tokens grouped in the same tinted boxes.
insights.data: Tokens are circles with the word inside; the mask is a grid of empty cells with purple check marks where a query may attend to a key.
insights.emphasis: Colour-matched groups: each head's tint (pink, yellow, green) is repeated in the key header above the grid, so the block structure of the check marks reads as the tree.
insights.flow: The tree branches downward from Root with elbow lines that run right into the grid rows, so each query token on the left lines up with its row; keys read across the top.
insights.avoid: The 'Tree Mask' title with a tree emoji sits at lower left in large bold type, far from the grid it names.

figures.lesson: Align the candidate-token tree row for row with the attention-mask grid and colour the grid's key header with the same per-head tints as the tree, so each allowed cell can be traced back to a tree path.

figures.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

taxonomy.task: virtual context management for LLMs with tiered memory

arrangement.units: a top lane holding the context window as coloured segments in dashed prompt/completion frames under a brace, and a bottom lane holding two grey manager boxes between two storage cylinders
arrangement.inputs_as: no explicit input; the context segments are labelled bars
arrangement.shared: the Function Executor is the single hub connected to archival storage, working context and recall storage

insights.structure: Two horizontal rows: the LLM context window as a strip of four coloured segments under a brace on top, and the managers (Function Executor, Queue Manager) flanked by Archival and Recall storage cylinders on the bottom.
insights.data: Memory regions are solid colour bars sized roughly by role (System Instructions black, Working Context orange, FIFO Queue blue with a magenta head), external stores are database cylinders, and no actual tokens or text are shown.
insights.emphasis: Bold two-line captions under each region state its read/write rule, and colour-matched block arrows (orange, magenta, blue, green) tie each manager action to the exact memory it changes.
insights.flow: Arrows run mostly bottom-to-top from managers into the context strip, sideways between storages and managers, and a large U-shaped blue arrow returns from Recall Storage under the row back to the Function Executor.
insights.avoid: Black and blue double-headed arrows between the two managers and the long U-shaped return arrow carry no label, so the read path from recall storage has to be inferred from the captions.

figures.lesson: Draw a context window as a single strip of coloured segments under a brace, and let every arrow that writes into a segment take that segment's colour.

figures.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework

taxonomy.task: multi-agent software development with shared message pool

arrangement.units: a rounded frame for the agent team around a shared pool on the left, and a larger blue rounded zoom panel for one agent on the right with nested white cards
arrangement.inputs_as: agent profile text and structured messages
arrangement.shared: the shared message pool, drawn once at the centre of the left panel

insights.structure: Left: a rounded frame with five role avatars (Architect, Project Manager, Engineer, Product Manager, QA Engineer) placed around a central purple 'Shared Message Pool'; right: a large blue zoom panel pulled out of the Engineer, holding an 'Agent Profile' card on top and an 'Iterative Programming' loop below.
insights.data: Agents are cartoon avatar portraits with tool icons, one message is expanded as key: value fields (content, cause_by, sent_from, send_to), and the engineer's work is shown as a real code snippet next to a sticky note and a memory tape strip.
insights.emphasis: The shared message pool is the central tinted block with double-headed blue arrows to every agent, and a curved black line zooms from the Engineer into the right-hand panel.
insights.flow: Agents publish to and subscribe from the pool by vertical double arrows; dotted arrows trace the hand-off order around the perimeter; in the right panel the loop runs write code, execution, check/cross, then Debug or Add Code back around.
insights.avoid: Too many small icons (pdf, python, image, document glyphs floating near agents) and two separate loops of dotted arrows make the left panel busy, and the 'Tools' legend sits detached below.

figures.lesson: For a team of role agents, place avatar portraits around a central shared store linked by double-headed arrows, show one message expanded as key: value fields, and pull one agent out into a side panel that zooms into its profile, memory and execute-feedback loop.

figures.title: Multi-Granularity Cross-modal Alignment for Generalized Medical Visual Representation Learning

arrangement.units: three tinted regions, one per alignment objective, between and right of the encoder bars
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-ray thumbnails and quoted report lines and words
arrangement.losses_at: each objective in its own tinted region where the two modalities meet
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Green Image Encoder bar on top and purple Text Encoder bar at the bottom, with three tinted regions for the objectives: yellow CTA between the encoders, pink ITA similarity matrix to the right, blue CPA prototype-clustering panel at the far right.
insights.data: Inputs are real chest X-rays with zoomed patch circles and quoted report lines split into word chips; representations are vertical columns of green or purple squares, token embeddings are multi-coloured cell rows, and the ITA is a 4 x 4 grid with blue diagonal cells.
insights.emphasis: Each alignment objective gets its own tinted region with its acronym in a matching colour (CTA orange, ITA red, CPA blue), explained in a dashed key at bottom right.
insights.flow: Left to right from inputs to encoders to representation columns; green lines run from the image side and purple lines from the text side into each objective, with curved black 'Align' arrows inside CTA.
insights.avoid: The purple 'Query' lines in CTA loop around the cross-attention boxes and cross the green ones, making the token-wise alignment hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Colour the image path green and the text path purple all the way through, and give each alignment objective its own tinted region with its own abbreviation.

figures.title: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models

arrangement.units: one unframed vertical stack: vision block, Linear Layer, Vicuna bar, with dashed text bubbles around it
arrangement.inputs_as: the image (a pink flamingo logo drawing) at the bottom right; the prompt as quoted text in green dashed bubbles at the Vicuna bar's lower edge
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the generated answer is a quoted paragraph in a dashed bubble at the top
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three solid module boxes are stacked bottom-to-top (Q-Former & ViT, Linear Layer, a full-width Vicuna bar) with the text prompt pieces as dashed bubbles flanking the Linear Layer just under the LLM bar.
insights.data: The prompt and the answer are drawn as real quoted text in green dashed rounded bubbles, the answer as a long paragraph whose key phrases are bold magenta, and the image enters as a picture from the bottom right.
insights.emphasis: Colour encodes trainability: the Linear Layer is the lone orange box while every frozen part is blue with a white snowflake.
insights.flow: Read from the bottom up: thick green arrows run picture -> vision block -> Linear Layer -> Vicuna, the side bubbles feed Vicuna from below, and one arrow at the right end of Vicuna rises into the answer bubble.
insights.avoid: The answer paragraph takes about a third of the figure and the input image sits outside any frame, so the model itself is visually smaller than its example output.

figures.lesson: When a model adds one trainable piece between two frozen giants, make it the single warm-coloured box in a stack of cool frozen ones and mark the frozen ones with a snowflake glyph.

figures.title: Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields

arrangement.units: unframed side-by-side sub-figures with letter captions beneath, the same camera-and-grid motif in each
arrangement.inputs_as: camera glyph and pixel grid drawn in perspective
arrangement.shared: the same camera and pixel-grid motif repeated in each panel

insights.structure: Two captioned sub-figures side by side, 'a) NeRF' at left and 'b) Mip-NeRF' at right, each built from the same camera glyph and tilted pixel grid; the Mip-NeRF part is two steps joined by an arrow labelled N.
insights.data: Rays are black lines with point samples, the cone is a translucent purple solid cut into frustum segments between t0 and t1, and the frustum is then shown as stacked purple Gaussian blobs; the encoding is written as gamma(x) versus E[gamma(x)].
insights.emphasis: The only colour is purple on the Mip-NeRF cone and Gaussians plus a red pixel footprint, against a black-line NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Left to right: ray to cone to Gaussians, with curved arrows lifting each sample up to its encoding label.
insights.avoid: Small italic labels (r-dot, t0, t1) sit inside the translucent cone and are hard to read.

figures.lesson: Contrast ray-based and cone-based sampling with the same camera-and-pixel-grid motif in each panel: a black line with point samples versus a translucent purple cone cut into frustum segments, then the same segment as stacked Gaussian blobs.

figures.title: Mixtral of Experts

arrangement.units: one unframed pipeline row: router box, expert deck, merge operator; no enclosing regions
arrangement.inputs_as: a single arrow labelled 'inputs' in monospace; no token or vector is drawn
arrangement.shared: the gating weights are one dotted line from the router that splits to both selected expert outputs

insights.structure: A router box on the left feeds a diagonal deck of overlapping expert cards in the middle, whose outputs merge at a circled-plus on the right, all on one horizontal line with no frames.
insights.data: Data is only named on arrows ('inputs', 'outputs'); the per-expert weights are a separate dotted line labelled 'gating weights' that loops over the top of the deck.
insights.emphasis: The two selected experts are solid and saturated while the others are dashed and faded, which makes top-2 selection the visual focus.
insights.flow: Solid arrows run left-to-right through router, experts and sum, while the dotted gating line climbs from the router, runs across the top and drops down onto the two expert output lines just before the sum.
insights.avoid: The 'expert' label is greyed and partly overlapped by the faded cards in front, and the two solid expert cards overlap so heavily that it is hard to see that exactly two are active.

figures.lesson: Show sparse routing by drawing all experts as one overlapping deck and fading the unselected ones, so 'k of N are active' reads at a glance without drawing N separate boxes.

figures.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision

taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a stack of all-MLP mixer layers (token-mixing MLP then channel-mixing MLP with skips), transformer-like but without attention

arrangement.units: One overview tower, unframed, bottom-centre; two dashed rounded detail frames (Mixer Layer across the top, MLP at bottom-right) set off by whitespace.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo cut into a 3 x 3 patch grid, then laid out as a row of photo tiles
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the tower ends in a plain 'Class' label at its top
arrangement.shared: weight sharing shown by repeating an identical 'MLP 1' / 'MLP 2' pill on every row

insights.structure: The expanded Mixer Layer spans the whole top width in a dashed frame, the compact classification tower sits bottom-centre, and the two-layer MLP internals sit in a second, narrow dashed frame at bottom-right.
insights.data: Patch tokens are coloured pills whose colours reappear as the rows of a patches x channels table and, after a curved 'T' transpose arrow, as its columns, while the input is a real photo split into a 3 x 3 grid of tiles.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is made to stand out by expansion rather than colour: the one 'N x (Mixer Layer)' box is opened into the full-width detail, where repeated identical 'MLP 1' / 'MLP 2' pills show weight sharing.
insights.flow: The tower reads bottom-to-top (photo tiles, per-patch FC, tokens, N x Mixer Layer, pooling, FC, 'Class'), the detail panel reads left-to-right, and skip-connections are labelled lines that arch over the top of the panel.
insights.avoid: The detail frame is tied to its 'N x (Mixer Layer)' box only by name (no zoom lines or matching tint), and the MLP frame's arrow just points up into empty space, so the reader must match the parts by label.

figures.lesson: Give every token its own pastel colour and keep those colours through the transposes, so a striped patches x channels table shows at a glance whether an operation mixes across rows or across columns.

figures.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning

arrangement.units: two vertical unframed columns separated by whitespace: query tower (left) and key tower (right)
arrangement.inputs_as: typeset math symbols; the key samples grouped by a curly brace
arrangement.losses_at: once, at the top centre where the two towers meet ('similarity' then 'contrastive loss')
arrangement.shared: none: encoder and momentum encoder are separate boxes with no drawn link

insights.structure: Two unframed towers stand side by side, query on the left and keys on the right, and meet at a shared apex of 'similarity' and 'contrastive loss' text at the top centre.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are typeset symbols only: x^query and a brace over x_0^key, x_1^key, ... at the bottom, and q and a k_0 k_1 k_2 ... row labelled 'queue' above the encoders.
insights.emphasis: The momentum encoder is set apart only by its pale blue fill against the pale green encoder; nothing else is coloured.
insights.flow: Both towers read bottom-to-top along thin grey arrows, and the last arrows elbow inward to the similarity label between the towers.
insights.avoid: The momentum update that ties the two encoders, the method's core, is not drawn (no arrow between the boxes), and the queue is just a text label on a row of symbols.

figures.lesson: Draw a two-encoder contrastive method as two bottom-up towers whose top arrows elbow inward to a single similarity-then-loss apex, and mark the novel encoder only by a different pale fill.

figures.title: MoDL: Model Based Deep Learning Architecture for Inverse Problems

taxonomy.task: model-based deep learning for MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: three captioned sub-figures stacked vertically, each a different zoom level (module, loop, unrolled); in (c) one red frame per iteration
arrangement.inputs_as: math label x_0 = A^H b on an incoming arrow
arrangement.shared: one 'Shared Weights W' box below the unrolled iterations with an arrow to each denoiser copy

insights.structure: Three captioned sub-figures stacked top to bottom: (a) the residual denoiser D_w as a yellow frame around a tan N_w block of Conv/BN/ReLU layers, (b) the compact two-box loop of yellow denoiser and green CG data-consistency layer, (c) the same loop unrolled into K red-framed iterations.
insights.data: Signals are math labels on arrows (x_0 = A^H b, z_k, x_{k+1}); layers are small teal boxes stacked in dark grey layer columns; the DC block shows the formula (A^H A + lambda I)^{-1}.
insights.emphasis: The colour pairing yellow = denoiser and green = data consistency is kept across (b) and (c), and a single tan 'Shared Weights W' box below (c) sends arrows up into every denoiser.
insights.flow: Each panel reads left to right; (b) has an 'Iterate' arrow looping back along the bottom, and in (c) a line from x_0 runs along the top into every DC block.
insights.avoid: The red iteration frames in (c) and the red skip line in (a) use red only for grouping, which competes with the emphasis colours.

figures.lesson: Draw the method twice: as a compact two-box loop with an 'Iterate' return arrow, then unrolled into K red-framed iterations whose denoisers all take arrows from one 'Shared Weights' box beneath.

figures.title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers

arrangement.units: full-width horizontal bands (grey rounded projection bands, green Transformer slab, unboxed ID rows separated by dashed lines), one band per processing layer
arrangement.inputs_as: three coloured line-chart thumbnails, each split into dotted patch boxes with masked patches greyed
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output mixture distributions at the top
arrangement.shared: one Transformer slab spans all variates' tokens

insights.structure: Horizontal full-width bands stacked bottom-to-top: three variate time-series thumbnails, a grey 'Multi Patch Size Input Projection' band with five patch-size pills, a row of patch-embedding cells, Time ID and Variate ID rows separated by dashed rules, a green full-width Transformer slab, an output-projection band and two mixture-distribution curves on top.
insights.data: Each variate is a coloured line chart (blue, orange, green) cut by dotted boxes into three patches, the last patch of variates 0 and 1 greyed and shown as grey [mask] cells, with the Time ID / Variate ID integers printed in rows directly under each token.
insights.emphasis: The selected 'Patch Size 64' pill is solid blue in both projection bands while the other four sizes are faded, and the two predicted mixtures (green and blue overlapping densities) sit above only the masked tokens' columns.
insights.flow: Strictly bottom-to-top: short vertical arrows lift each patch into its embedding, and only the two masked-token columns continue as lines through the Transformer to the output projection and the distributions.
insights.avoid: The faded unused patch-size pills and the many repeated Time/Variate ID digits take a lot of space for a single idea, and the Transformer slab hides how variates are flattened into one sequence beyond the ID rows.

figures.lesson: Draw the model as full-width bands named in a left-margin column, and lay the variate and time IDs out as plain number rows aligned under every token, so a flattened multivariate token sequence reads like a table.

figures.title: Model-Contrastive Federated Learning

arrangement.units: unboxed icons and network glyphs; only party data stacks are enclosed in dashed boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo stacks per party in dashed boxes at the bottom corners
arrangement.shared: a single server/global model at the top centre shared by all parties

insights.structure: A server database icon at top centre, a global network in the middle and two party networks at the left and right, each party's photo stack boxed in a dashed frame at the bottom corners, with a numbered step list in the bottom centre.
insights.data: Models are drawn as identical small node-link MLP glyphs with cyan circles, local updates shown as red-outlined neurons in the party models, and each party's local data is a real photo (dog, cat) stack.
insights.emphasis: Step 2 (parties update with local data) is written in red in the step list and its circled numeral, matching the red-ringed neurons in the party networks.
insights.flow: A cycle labelled by circled numbers: (1) diagonal arrows from global model down to parties, (2) up from data to local model, (3) elbow arrows up to the server, (4) down from server to global model.
insights.avoid: The figure is a generic FedAvg overview with no MOON-specific content, and the long step list in the canvas duplicates what the numbered arrows already say.

figures.lesson: Number every arrow of the round with a circled step index keyed to a step list in the figure's empty centre, and colour only the step the paper modifies red - in the list and on the changed nodes of the local model glyphs.

figures.title: Model-Contrastive Federated Learning

taxonomy.task: federated image classification with model-contrastive local loss

arrangement.units: three dashed-border boxes, one per model copy, each holding three coloured layer bars
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo stack labelled 'party i' in a dashed frame
arrangement.shared: the same input fans out to all three models; the colour code for layers is shared

insights.structure: Three dashed-box model copies stacked vertically in the middle (local model t-1 top, global model t middle, local model t bottom), the party's photo stack on the left, a dashed 'local loss' box on the right, and a colour legend top-right.
insights.data: Each model is three coloured vertical bars (red base encoder, blue projection head, yellow output layer) so the three copies are visually identical and comparable layer by layer.
insights.emphasis: The losses are named in the right box as 'model-contrastive loss' plus 'supervised learning loss' joined by a bold plus sign, and the contrastive loss is fed from the projection-head bars of all three models.
insights.flow: Left to right: the input image fans out to three models; the projection-head outputs of the three models run down/right into the model-contrastive loss, while only the local model t's output layer feeds the supervised loss.
insights.avoid: The representation arrows from the top two models cross through the middle model box and overlap, making it hard to trace which head feeds which loss.

figures.lesson: Draw one client's network three times - previous local, current global, current local - as identical colour-coded layer stacks titled with their round index, so the loss reads as a comparison between versions of the same model.

figures.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

arrangement.units: two horizontal lanes without frames: top lane a single 'DFT' box, bottom lane the 'Message Passing Neural Net' box holding three graph snapshots; both converge on a 'Targets' box at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey circle holding a white skeletal drawing of the molecule
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the 'Targets' box (E, ω0, ...) is the shared output
arrangement.shared: the input circle and the Targets box are shared by both lanes

insights.structure: A grey input circle on the left forks into two parallel grey boxes, a small 'DFT' box on top and a wide 'Message Passing Neural Net' box below, which both feed one 'Targets' box at top right.
insights.data: The molecule is a white skeletal drawing in the input circle and, inside the MPNN box, three ball-and-stick graphs whose node dots change colour (white, blue, red, purple) from snapshot to snapshot.
insights.emphasis: Large serif annotations '~10^3 seconds' and '~10^-2 seconds' under the two routes make the cost contrast the message, and the MPNN box is the only one with content inside.
insights.flow: Arrows leave the input circle right and fork up and down, the DFT path runs straight into Targets, and the MPNN path turns upward into Targets from below.
insights.avoid: All boxes share the same flat mid-grey fill, so the proposed net is not set apart from the DFT baseline by colour, and the node colours inside the snapshots have no key.

figures.lesson: Put the proposed model and the expensive baseline on parallel paths from the same input to the same target and print each path's cost under its box, so the speed-up reads at a glance.

figures.title: Multi-Stage Progressive Image Restoration

arrangement.units: one unboxed horizontal lane per stage, labelled 'Stage 1/2/3' at its left; Stage 3's ORB chain is enclosed in a grey ORSNet box
arrangement.inputs_as: real degraded photos, split into patches differently per stage
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; restored outputs at the right of each lane
arrangement.shared: the same degraded image enters every lane; SAM outputs pass up between lanes

insights.structure: Three horizontal stage rows stacked with Stage 1 at the bottom and Stage 3 at the top, each starting from a degraded image on the left and ending in a restored image on the right, with a legend box for ORB/SAM/CAB in the bottom-right.
insights.data: Inputs are real rainy car photos split into 4 patches (Stage 1), 2 patches (Stage 2) and whole (Stage 3) with coloured borders; U-Nets are grey trapezoid pairs with small 3D coloured feature cubes labelled 'cat'.
insights.emphasis: Repeated stage-specific modules use saturated fills (orange Conv, green SAM, yellow ORB in a grey ORSNet box) and the cross-stage connections are distinct colours: green solid arrows from SAM to the next stage and magenta dotted arrows between U-Net encoders/decoders.
insights.flow: Each stage reads left to right; information climbs upward between stages via green SAM-output arrows and magenta dotted feature links, so the overall progression runs bottom to top.
insights.avoid: Bottom-to-top stage ordering against top-down reading, plus many crossing coloured inter-stage lines, makes the cross-stage wiring hard to follow.

figures.lesson: Stack the stages bottom to top and re-show the input at each stage as a thumbnail cut into fewer patches (quadrants, halves, whole) with coloured patch borders, so the coarse-to-fine progression is drawn on the image itself.

figures.title: Multi-Stage Progressive Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: supervised attention module for image restoration

arrangement.units: unboxed tensor stacks and small orange Conv tags connected by arrows with circle operators
arrangement.inputs_as: a feature stack F_in (top) and a real degraded photo (bottom)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two horizontal tracks: a feature track on top from F_in (left) to F_out (right) and an image track below from Degraded I through Restored X_S to attention maps M, joined by vertical connections.
insights.data: Features are drawn as stacked viridis-coloured slices labelled H x W x C, images as real rainy viaduct photos labelled H x W x 3, and attention maps as a stack of greyscale slices.
insights.emphasis: The only supervised output, Restored X_S, carries a pink 'Loss' tag beneath it, and the attention maps re-enter the feature track through a multiply circle before the residual add.
insights.flow: F_in branches down via a Conv to a residual R_S added to the degraded image; the restored image goes right through Conv and sigmoid to M, which rises to multiply the conv'd features, then adds back to F_in to give F_out.

figures.lesson: Draw a module's tensors as stacks of real data - viridis activation maps for features, the actual photo for the intermediate image, greyscale maps for attention - each with its shape above, so every arrow visibly changes the data.

figures.title: Motion Transformer with Global Intention Localization and Local Movement Refinement

arrangement.units: dashed-border rounded panels labelled (a), (b), (c); the encoder and scene column are unboxed
arrangement.inputs_as: top-down road-scene sketch with car icons, encoded to agent/map token rows
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output tensor boxes at the top of panel (c)
arrangement.shared: encoder features shared as key/value by the decoder

insights.structure: Three zones left to right: a narrow scene column (road map, polyline encoder, local graph), a central encoder stack with two dashed sub-panels (a) Dense Future Prediction and (b) Dynamic Map Collection above it, and a large grey dashed panel (c) holding the stacked xN decoder layer.
insights.data: Agent features are blue squares and map features grey circles in rounded token rows, scenes are top-down road sketches with car icons, and decoder tensors are white boxes labelled with shapes like K x T x 2 and K x (2+2).
insights.emphasis: The decoder panel (c) is the largest region with a grey background and xN multiplier, and the two dashed sub-panels illustrate their outputs with coloured dotted predicted trajectories and translucent trajectory-specific map regions.
insights.flow: Bottom-up within the encoder (local graph tokens to Transformer Encoder to sub-panels), then a long 'Key & Value' elbow line carries features right into the decoder, which itself reads bottom-up from three query initialisations to GMM Prediction and outputs.
insights.avoid: Long elbow lines (Key & Value, the loop from Dynamic Map Collection back) cross the panel boundaries and are hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Use two token glyphs (blue squares for agents, grey circles for map polylines) in every token row, and pair each module with a top-view mini-scene showing its output as dotted trajectory arrows and translucent map bands, all decoded by a glyph legend along the bottom.

figures.title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text

arrangement.units: two rows (stages) by three columns (retriever, memory, reader), each cell a rounded panel with a coloured header bar
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos and quoted question text with dataset labels
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output tokens y1..yn at the top of the reader panel
arrangement.shared: same three-panel layout and modules repeated in both rows

insights.structure: Two identical rows (Pre-Training Stage top, Fine-Tune Stage bottom), each with three column panels: Retriever Stage, External Memory and Reader Stage, joined by big grey block arrows labelled MIPS and Top_K(M).
insights.data: Queries are real photos plus quoted text with dataset tags (CC, PAQ, VQA); memory entries are rows of pink embedding dots next to text, photos or a Wikipedia snippet; the reader is two node-link transformer layers f_theta and g_theta over ViT/Emb input boxes.
insights.emphasis: Each column header is tinted (blue retriever, yellow memory, pink reader) and the per-row caption states what changes between stages, while ViT boxes are yellow and Emb boxes blue throughout to show which modalities enter.
insights.flow: Left to right within each row via the fat grey arrows; the two rows are read top then bottom as training stages.
insights.avoid: The 'Empty' checkered placeholders and tiny unreadable Wikipedia snippet text add clutter, and generic node-link drawings stand in for transformers without saying anything specific.

figures.lesson: Each encoder box is filled with the tint of a column header (ViT boxes share the External Memory yellow, Emb boxes the Retriever blue-grey), so the interleaved image/text input sequence fed to the reader reads as a colour pattern without a legend.

figures.title: Muse: Text-To-Image Generation via Masked Generative Transformers

arrangement.units: unboxed horizontal tracks of rounded coloured module boxes alternating with token grids
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos at two resolutions and a quoted text prompt
arrangement.shared: one text embedding feeds both transformers

insights.structure: Three horizontal tracks: text prompt and text encoder on top, a 256x256 base track in the middle and a 512x512 super-resolution track at the bottom, each image track being VQ Tokenizer, Mask, token grid, Transformer, reconstructed grid.
insights.data: Inputs are real dog-and-cat photos labelled with resolution, the text prompt is quoted in italics, the text embedding is a row of green cells, and tokens are small blue/grey grids where grey cells are masked.
insights.emphasis: Each module box has its own pastel fill and border (orange and green tokenizers, blue base, purple SuperRes transformer), and the two token grids before and after each transformer make the masked-to-filled change visible.
insights.flow: Left to right in each track; the text embedding arrow drops into both transformers, and a dashed line carries base reconstructed tokens down into the SuperRes transformer.

figures.lesson: Draw a two-resolution cascade as two rows with the same image-tokenizer-mask-grid-transformer-grid sequence, enlarging the input photo and the token grid in the lower row to show the higher resolution, and bring the shared condition down from a top row as elbow arrows into each row's transformer.

figures.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model

arrangement.units: three unboxed panels lettered A, B, C separated by thin rules
arrangement.inputs_as: Go-board state icons on a horizontal timeline
arrangement.shared: the same h/g/f colour code and s-node glyphs across all panels

insights.structure: Three panels: A (left, full height) a search tree, B (top right) acting in the environment over three time steps, C (bottom right) the unrolled training of the model aligned with the same steps; a vertical rule and a horizontal rule split them.
insights.data: Board states are tiny Go-board icons, hidden states are circles labelled s0..s3, policies are green bar histograms in brackets, and functions are single italic letters h, g, f.
insights.emphasis: Each function has its own colour carried across panels: cyan for h (representation), green for g (dynamics) and its s nodes, pink for f outputs p,v, while unexplored tree nodes are pale grey.
insights.flow: A reads top-down along the green path of the tree; B and C read left to right along a dashed-in timeline, with C's h arrow rising from the board row to s0 and g arrows conditioned on actions coming up from below.

figures.lesson: Give each learned function one colour and paint its letter, its arrow and its output in it across every panel, so the same model is recognisable both as a path through a search tree (A) and as a straight unrolled chain (C).

figures.title: N-BEATS: Neural basis expansion analysis for interpretable time series forecasting

arrangement.units: Three rounded tinted panels in one row: left blue panel = one block (FC stack splitting into backcast and forecast heads), middle orange panel = one stack (Block 1, 2, ..., K on a residual spine with a forecast sum), right yellow panel = the model (Stack 1..M summed into the global forecast); a real series plot sits above the right panel without a frame.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real time-series line plot with lookback and forecast horizons marked by double arrows and a red split line; inside the panels inputs are text labels (Block Input, Stack Input)
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; outputs exit at the bottom (Backcast, Forecast, Stack residual) or top right (Global forecast)
arrangement.shared: each panel expands one box of the panel to its right via dashed zoom lines; nothing is drawn twice

insights.structure: Three panels in a row nest model, stack and block from right to left, each panel tinted differently and linked to the box it expands by dashed diagonal zoom lines.
insights.data: The input series appears once, as a real teal line plot across the top right with lookback and forecast horizons marked by double-headed arrows and a red vertical split, and its two horizons drop as labelled arrows into the model panel.
insights.emphasis: The doubly residual idea is made visible by geometry rather than colour: minus circles stack down the left spine of the stack panel while forecast arrows converge on a single plus circle on the right.
insights.flow: Inside each panel data runs top to bottom with right-angle bends; the reader enters at the top-right plot and descends levels by following the zoom lines leftward.
insights.avoid: The right-to-left zoom order fights the usual reading direction, so the most detailed panel (the block) is met first at the far left before its context.

figures.lesson: A three-level hierarchy (model > stack > block) can be drawn as three side-by-side panels whose child boxes take the tint of the next panel and are tied to it by dashed zoom lines, so the reader can descend levels without nested boxes.

figures.title: Simple Baselines for Image Restoration

arrangement.units: three unboxed sub-figures with (a)/(b)/(c) captions below, each a grid of identical block boxes on shared resolution rows
arrangement.inputs_as: text label 'input' on an arrow
arrangement.shared: the resolution rows and their left-side labels are shared across panels

insights.structure: Three sub-figures (a) multi-stage on top full width, (b) multi-scale fusion and (c) UNet (ours) side by side below, all sharing three resolution rows H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4 separated by dashed horizontal lines labelled on the left.
insights.data: Every stage is the same peach rounded 'Block x n_i' box, so only the wiring differs; inputs and outputs are just text labels at line ends.
insights.emphasis: The proposed design is the sparsest panel and is marked '(ours)' in bold in its caption, contrasting with the crossing lines of (b) and the doubled chain of (a).
insights.flow: Left to right with downward arrows to lower resolutions and upward arrows back; skip lines run horizontally along each resolution row.
insights.avoid: All blocks share one colour and the ours panel has no visual highlight beyond the caption, so the comparison relies entirely on reading wiring.

figures.lesson: Compare architecture families on shared horizontal resolution bands (dashed rules labelled H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4 in the margin) with one identical 'Block' box everywhere, so only the wiring differs and the simplest diagram is the proposed one.

figures.title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: Algorithms and Performance Analysis
figures.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

taxonomy.task: federated learning with differential privacy threat model
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = differential-privacy noise added to client uploads

arrangement.units: unboxed icons: a cloud server, device clients with model glyphs and database cylinders
arrangement.inputs_as: database cylinder icons under each client
arrangement.shared: one server broadcasting the same w to all clients

insights.structure: A cloud labelled Server at top-left, a row of clients along the bottom (phone C1, laptop C2, desktop CN with an ellipsis), each with a small network glyph and a database cylinder beneath, and a red devil Adversary at the far left.
insights.data: Clients are realistic device icons, local models small blue node-link networks, and local data grey cylinders labelled Database 1..N; parameters are written as w and w_i on the arrows.
insights.emphasis: The adversary is a red devil icon with a fat blue arrow carrying w1...wN into it, making the eavesdropping threat the eye-catching element.
insights.flow: Solid blue arrows go up from clients to the server (uploading w_i) and dashed blue arrows come back down (broadcasting w); green arrows loop between database and model, orange arrows link device and database.
insights.avoid: Clip-art device and cloud icons dominate and the long diagonal arrows pairs to far clients are crowded; the privacy mechanism itself (noise) is not drawn.

figures.lesson: Separate upload and broadcast by line style (solid w_i up, dashed w down) and key it in a small boxed legend; mark the eavesdropper as the only red icon fed by a heavy arrow of all uploads.

figures.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis

arrangement.units: four unboxed columns each headed by a two-line title and lettered (a)-(d) below
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3D scene sketch with real photo image planes and rays
arrangement.shared: the same scene and rays are reused in (a) and (b)

insights.structure: Four captioned columns (a)-(d) left to right: 5D input on a 3D scene with two camera image planes, output colour and density on the same scene, volume rendering plots for two rays, and rendering loss expressions.
insights.data: Rays are red arrows through a dotted bounding box of a Lego bulldozer with sample points as dots, the MLP F_Theta is three small blue bars between the tuples (x,y,z,theta,phi) and (RGB sigma), and density along each ray is a colour-graded curve over ray distance.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the idea: sample points in (b) take the colour they predict, the curves in (c) are coloured by the same gradient, and the rendered pixel patches in (d) are those colours compared with g.t. in squared-norm bars.
insights.flow: Left to right with curved blue arrows linking a sample point to the input tuple, the network to the output tuple, and each ray's curve to its loss term.

figures.lesson: Draw the radiance-field step inside a wireframe scene cube with real image planes and red rays carrying sample dots, and carry two named rays as parallel lanes into the density plots and the loss so the reader can follow one pixel end to end.

figures.title: NeRF in the Wild: Neural Radiance Fields for Unconstrained Photo Collections

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis from unconstrained photo collections

arrangement.units: one unframed network: a trunk and two heads distinguished by colour, with two rounded output boxes at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: typeset symbols with a small caption word under each (appearance embedding, viewing direction, XYZ position, transient embedding)
arrangement.shared: the orange trunk MLP is one block whose output arrows feed both heads and the static sigma directly

insights.structure: A single orange trunk MLP in the middle left forks into a green static head above and a blue transient head below, with the outputs stacked in two rounded boxes on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are typeset symbols (l^(a), theta phi, XYZ, l^(tau)) each with a one- or two-word caption, entered from the left edge at the height of the network that consumes them; outputs are symbol-plus-word pairs (RGB color, sigma density, beta uncertainty).
insights.emphasis: Colour separates the static path (green) from the new transient path (blue), and rotated bold labels 'static' and 'transient' at the right edge name the two output groups.
insights.flow: Everything reads left to right on straight grey horizontal arrows; the long arrow from the trunk to the static sigma bypasses the green head, which shows that density does not depend on appearance.
insights.avoid: The figure is a raster image with small grey arrows, and the three-bar MLP glyph says nothing about depth or width.

figures.lesson: Draw a shared trunk network in one colour that splits into two differently coloured heads, enter each head's extra conditioning input from the left edge at the head's height, and close each head in a rounded output box tagged by a rotated side label.

figures.title: NeuS: Learning Neural Implicit Surfaces by Volume Rendering for Multi-view Reconstruction

arrangement.units: two unframed sub-figures split by a thin vertical rule, captioned '(a) Illustration' and '(b) Example' below; (a) is internally split by a horizontal rule into two ray-diagram rows
arrangement.inputs_as: the reference photo leftmost in (b); camera glyphs at the left of each (a) row
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A narrow (a) column on the left, split by a horizontal rule into a 'surface rendering' row and a 'volume rendering' row (labels written vertically on the left edge), is separated by a thin vertical rule from a wide (b) strip of four same-pose renders: reference photo, IDR, NeRF, Ours.
insights.data: Each (a) row is a 1-D side view of one ray: blue camera glyph, dashed blue ray, yellow scene bars and a blue image bar; surface rendering shows one grey hit dot on a dotted curved surface, volume rendering a row of grey sampled-point dots with glowing dotted bars; (b) shows a colour photo then grey shaded meshes on white.
insights.emphasis: 'Ours' is simply the rightmost mesh in the strip; its clean walls versus IDR's wavy interior and NeRF's noisy stripes carry the claim with no highlight colour or frame.
insights.flow: Read (a) top to bottom (surface vs volume), then (b) left to right from reference image to baselines to ours; the only arrows are the camera rays pointing right.
insights.avoid: The two halves are only loosely linked: the (a) schematic is tiny and its labels ('surface', 'sampled points') are small compared with the large (b) renders, and the comparison to two baselines carries no indication of what is wrong with them.

figures.lesson: Contrast surface rendering and volume rendering as two stacked 1-D ray diagrams (camera, dashed ray, one hit point vs a row of sampled dots), then let a same-pose strip of grey mesh renders ending in 'Ours' carry the comparison.

figures.title: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM

arrangement.units: unframed rows per modality (row colour carried by arrows and boxes) crossed by five columns marked only by a bottom ruler with tick marks and stage labels; no enclosures
arrangement.inputs_as: modality icons with plain row labels at the far left
arrangement.shared: the single LLM block spans all rows in the centre column

insights.structure: One row per modality (Text, Image, Audio, Video, dashed 'More modalities') labelled at the far left, converging on one tall orange LLM block in the centre and mirrored on the right (output projection, diffusion decoder, output icon); a tick-marked ruler along the bottom names five column stages.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are flat outline icons (document, picture frame, waveform, film strip) coloured per modality; modules are rounded boxes, encoders and diffusion decoders solid modality-coloured fills, projections white with a coloured outline.
insights.emphasis: Trainable projections carry a flame icon and hollow outlined boxes while frozen encoders, decoders and the LLM carry a snowflake and solid fills, so the few trained parts read as light gaps.
insights.flow: Left to right: coloured curves converge into the LLM's left edge and fan out from its right; the text row bypasses all modules with long blue curves arching over the top; a dashed grey curve and ellipsis stand for further modalities.
insights.avoid: White text on pale pastel encoder/decoder fills (Image Encoder, Audio Diffusion) has low contrast and is hard to read.

figures.lesson: Frozen and trainable parts differ in fill as well as icon: frozen encoders, decoders and LLM are solid colour blocks with a snowflake, trained projections are white boxes with only a coloured outline and a flame, so the few trained parts read as light gaps in the pipeline.

figures.title: Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering

taxonomy.note: training other = BPR pairwise ranking loss (not drawn in this figure)

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side split by a dash-dot rule, each captioned in bold below; right panel sub-grouped by nested shaded ellipses
arrangement.inputs_as: graph nodes (circles) with math labels
arrangement.shared: the same users and items appear in both panels

insights.structure: Two unframed panels split by a grey dash-dot vertical line: a two-column bipartite graph (users u1-u3 left, items i1-i5 right) and the same graph unrolled as a tree rooted at u1, each with a bold caption beneath.
insights.data: Users are light-blue circles, items light-grey circles, joined by thin grey lines; on the right grey arrows point upward from items and users at each hop toward u1; hop distance is shown by three nested dotted ellipses with fills paling outward, labelled l = 1, 2, 3 in red italic.
insights.emphasis: The target user u1 is ringed in thick red on the left and sits at the top of the darkest innermost ellipse on the right.
insights.flow: Left panel first (raw graph), then right panel read bottom-up along arrows from outer hops toward u1 at the top.
insights.avoid: Node labels sit in bold italic beside nodes and partly crowd the arrows in the right tree; the outer ellipse is so pale it barely separates l = 2 from l = 3.

figures.lesson: Show high-order connectivity by drawing the bipartite graph once as two columns (users blue, items grey) and once unrolled as a tree rooted at the target user, with nested shaded ellipses marking hop distance l = 1, 2, 3.

figures.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation

arrangement.units: two grey tinted background panels, 'stage 1' (wide) and 'stage 2', titled at top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: a schematic grey plane (no real scan)
arrangement.shared: none: each stage has its own bow-tie U-Net glyph

insights.structure: Two grey stage panels sit side by side (stage 1 wider and darker, stage 2 narrower and lighter) above a full-width legend strip.
insights.data: Images and segmentations are flat coloured planes in perspective (grey image, blue low-res seg, green full-res seg) and each U-Net is an unlabelled grey bow-tie solid.
insights.emphasis: No module is highlighted; the only saturated line colour is the red crop outline that carries a patch from stage 1 into stage 2.
insights.flow: Left to right: image planes shrink through a dotted frustum into the first bow-tie, its blue output grows back through another frustum, and red dotted lines hand the cropped stack to stage 2's bow-tie and green output.
insights.avoid: The U-Nets are unlabelled glyphs and the stage-1 frustum lines overlap the stacked blue and grey planes, so the upsample-then-concatenate step is hard to separate without the caption.

figures.lesson: Show resampling between resolutions as dotted frustum lines joining the corners of a large and a small plane, so down- and up-sampling read geometrically without any arrow or label.

figures.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy

taxonomy.task: generalist robot policy pretraining and finetuning

arrangement.units: two stacked unframed rows ('Pre-Training', 'Finetuning') separated by a thin rule and labelled at the left with up/down arrows; plus a left column of two grey-outlined rounded panels for the tokenizers
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo and quoted instruction words inside the left tokenizer panels
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; action outputs 'a' at the right of Action Head boxes below each row
arrangement.shared: the same Octo Transformer bar and token layout repeat in both rows

insights.structure: A narrow left column of two grey-outlined rounded panels explains tokenization (Task Tokens, Observation Tokens); the wide right side is two rows split by a thin grey rule, 'Pre-Training' above and 'Finetuning' below, each a sequence of tall tinted column groups (Task, Observation, Readout, ...) crossed by one long 'Octo Transformer' bar.
insights.data: Language is quoted words feeding a green Language Encoder, images are a camera photo with a white 3x3 patch grid and older frames stacked behind feeding a blue CNN trapezoid; tokens are rounded pills tinted green (task), blue (observation) and purple (readout), with positional encoding as a circled sine glyph added through circled plus signs.
insights.emphasis: The finetuning row repeats the pretraining row with every unchanged column faded to a ghost, leaving only dashed, saturated new observation tokens, the new action-space readout and a 'New Action Head', each named by a callout box.
insights.flow: Tokenization panels read top to bottom on the left; each right row reads left to right along the token sequence, with readout pills dropping by short elbow arrows into Action Head boxes that output an italic a.
insights.avoid: The transformer bar is drawn on top of the column groups and covers their middles, so the token columns look cut in half rather than passing through the model.

figures.lesson: Show finetuning as a copy of the pretraining row with everything unchanged faded to a ghost, so only the new observation tokens, action space and head - dashed and saturated, each with a callout - stand out.

figures.title: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment

taxonomy.note: family other = neural architecture search / once-for-all supernet; architecture other = weight-sharing elastic supernetwork

arrangement.units: three dotted rectangles, each a stage, with nested smaller dotted rectangles inside later stages; captions below each; connectors are rounded number boxes between stages
arrangement.inputs_as: the full-width channel stack in the first dotted box
arrangement.shared: the same four coloured channel sheets appear in every stage

insights.structure: Three dotted-rectangle stages left to right, each holding a vertical stack of channel sheets with a caption below ('train with full width', 'progressively shrink the width' twice); between stages a rounded black-outlined column of channel-importance numbers with arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'.
insights.data: Channels are flat coloured parallelograms (grey, orange, green, blue) that keep their colour as they are re-ordered between stages; importance scores are printed decimals; nested smaller dotted rectangles mark each sub-network's channel subset.
insights.emphasis: The same coloured sheets visibly change order after sorting, and each nested dotted box has its own output arrow O1, O2, O3 at its lower right, so the shrinking sub-networks read as nested.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along straight black arrows, from full width through the importance column to each shrunken stage; the last stage ends with a trailing 'channel sorting' arrow.
insights.avoid: The nested dotted rectangles in the third stage are very close together and their O1/O2/O3 taps overlap, making it hard to tell which box each output belongs to.

figures.lesson: Show elastic width as the same coloured channel sheets re-sorted between stages by a printed column of importance scores, with nested dotted boxes marking each sub-network's channel subset and its own output tap.

figures.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model

taxonomy.note: training rl-offline = imitation learning on robot demonstrations

arrangement.units: one dashed rounded container for the whole model; one dashed sub-container groups the two vision encoders; other modules unframed rounded boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real camera photo and quoted instruction in a rounded box, outside the container
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One large dashed light-grey rounded container titled 'OpenVLA' holds the model; inside, DinoV2 and SigLIP share a dashed sub-container, an MLP Projector and a Llama Tokenizer sit side by side below a wide 'Llama 2 7B' bar, and an Action De-Tokenizer sits above it; numbered circles 1, 2, 3 tag encoder, projector and LLM.
insights.data: Inputs outside the left edge are a camera photo and a rounded box with a quoted instruction; tokens are rows of small pills, yellow-to-blue gradient for fused vision tokens, green for text, purple for actions; the output is a bracketed column vector [Δx; Δθ; ΔGrip] labelled '7D Robot Action' above a rendered robot arm.
insights.emphasis: The colour of each token row inherits its source (gradient mixing the two encoder colours), and the bold container title plus numbered circles name the model and its three parts.
insights.flow: Inputs enter on thin grey elbow lines that run under the container's bottom edge and turn up into the encoders and the prompt template; inside, short black arrows run bottom to top; the output exits the top right and drops down the right side to the robot.
insights.avoid: The image input line crosses the instruction line and both detour below the container, so the input routing is the hardest part to follow.

figures.lesson: Tint each token row with the colour of what produced it - a yellow-to-blue gradient for tokens fused from two vision encoders, green for text, purple for actions - and end at a bracketed Δx/Δθ/ΔGrip vector above the robot it drives.

figures.title: Simple Open-Vocabulary Object Detection with Vision Transformers

arrangement.units: two rounded light-grey-outlined frames, one per training stage, each titled in large type above
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text strings in typewriter font above, patch-gridded photos below, at each frame's left edge
arrangement.losses_at: right end of each frame as a bold-italic text note (and a +/- matrix in the left frame)
arrangement.shared: text and vision encoders redrawn in identical positions in both frames

insights.structure: Two rounded grey-outlined frames side by side, each titled above ('Image-level contrastive pre-training', 'Transfer to open-vocabulary detection'); in both, a Text Transformer encoder sits above a Vision Transformer encoder in the same position, and the right frame adds two rotated orange heads beside the vision tokens.
insights.data: Text inputs are typewriter-font quoted strings, images are photos with a white patch grid; embeddings are small squares (lilac text, green image, white box); the left loss is a small +/- grid with green plus on the diagonal; detection outputs are rows of printed class scores with the chosen quoted class and rows of (x, y, w, h) tuples.
insights.emphasis: The added detection parts (Linear projection, MLP head, token pooling) are the only orange elements, and the closing bold-italic loss phrases contrast 'images in a batch' with 'objects in an image'.
insights.flow: Each frame reads left to right from inputs through encoders to outputs; in the right frame text query embeddings drop down as column headers of the score table and output rows curve into the set prediction loss note.
insights.avoid: The right frame's many thin curved lines from the pink vision-token tabs to the heads cross and bunch together, and the score digits are tiny.

figures.lesson: Make open-vocabulary detection readable by turning text embeddings into the column headers of a per-box score table, printing the actual scores and the chosen class string in each row next to a parallel row of (x, y, w, h) box tuples.

figures.title: Recommendation as Language Processing (RLP): A Unified Pretrain, Personalized Prompt & Predict Paradigm (P5)

arrangement.units: one hub composition; prompt and answer boxes are pastel rounded rectangles; a dashed horizontal rule splits pretraining tasks (above) from the zero-shot task (below), each labelled in italic
arrangement.inputs_as: real prompt text in task-tinted rounded boxes with bold task titles above
arrangement.shared: the single P5 hub serves all tasks

insights.structure: A central heavy-outlined grey hub box labelled 'P5'; five prompt boxes stacked down the left, each under a bold task name, and small answer boxes stacked down the right; a dashed horizontal line near the bottom separates multitask pretraining from a zero-shot example.
insights.data: Prompts are full real prompt text with user and item IDs written out in serif, inside rounded boxes tinted one pastel per task; answers ('1581', '5.0', 'broke immediately') sit in small boxes of the matching tint.
insights.emphasis: The model is the hub where every curve converges, set in the largest bold italic text inside the only thick-outlined box.
insights.flow: Left to right: smooth black curves converge from every prompt into the hub and fan out to every answer; colour, not lines, pairs each prompt with its answer.
insights.avoid: All curves are identical black and cross near the hub, so line identity is lost and the reader must rely on colour to pair prompts and answers; the model's internals are not shown at all.

figures.lesson: Make the teaser a hub: each task's real prompt text in a box tinted with its own colour on the left, its answer in a small box of the same tint on the right, so colour pairs inputs with outputs through the single model in the middle.

figures.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

taxonomy.task: KV-cache memory management for LLM serving

arrangement.units: three unframed tables side by side, each titled above: logical blocks grid, block table, physical blocks grid
arrangement.inputs_as: a circle labelled 'Request A' with the quoted prompt and output words beside it, at the top left
arrangement.shared: the block table in the middle is the only link between the grids; arrows enter it from logical rows and fan out from it to physical rows

insights.structure: A short logical grid on the left and a tall physical grid on the right flank a small block table, and arrows through the table land on non-adjacent physical rows.
insights.data: Real prompt words (italic) fill the KV cells, one word per cell, so the same words can be found again in the scattered physical blocks.
insights.emphasis: Red 'Logical' and 'Physical' title words and darker yellow-orange cells for newly generated tokens make the two address spaces and the growth step stand out.
insights.flow: Start at the request top-left, read the logical grid, pass through the block table, then follow the arrows right to the physical rows; circled numerals give step order.
insights.avoid: The long thin arrows from the block table cross each other on the way to the physical grid, and the circled numerals on them are too small to read at print size.

figures.lesson: Show an indirection (virtual-to-physical mapping) as two grids of the same row height on either side of a small lookup table, writing the same real words into matching cells so the reader can check the mapping by content.

figures.title: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution System for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast

taxonomy.note: modality = gridded atmospheric fields (3-D pressure-level and 2-D surface variables)

arrangement.units: one composition; two thin blue-outlined square containers (Encoder, Decoder) each holding two grey layer boxes, labelled in bold below
arrangement.inputs_as: colormapped field renders (3-D cubes and flat maps) with tensor sizes underneath
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Mirror-symmetric left to right: input fields and patch tokens on the far left, two thin blue-outlined square containers 'Encoder' and 'Decoder' in the middle each holding two grey layer boxes stacked vertically, then patch tokens and output fields mirrored on the far right, under a bold centred title.
insights.data: Upper-air variables are three rendered 3-D cubes with colormapped faces, surface variables three flat colormapped maps; tokens are columns of five small colormapped cubes; each layer box states block name with repeat count and tensor size in math.
insights.emphasis: Colour is spent on the real data fields while the network stays grey, and identical renderings on both sides make 'field in, same field out' visible; the model name is the large bold title.
insights.flow: Thick orange arrows run left to right, merging the two input rows into Layer 1 and splitting out of Layer 4; dotted orange vertical arrows show down-sampling in the encoder and up-sampling in the decoder.
insights.avoid: The two-level U is drawn inside two separate boxes, so the skip from Layer 1 to Layer 4 looks like an ordinary forward arrow rather than a skip connection.

figures.lesson: Mirror the input and output fields on both sides with identical renderings (3-D cubes for pressure-level variables, flat maps for surface ones) and their tensor sizes underneath, so the model reads as field in, same field out, with a compact grey network between.

figures.title: Scaling Autoregressive Models for Content-Rich Text-to-Image Generation

taxonomy.task: autoregressive text-to-image generation over image tokens

arrangement.units: One composition: orange encoder box (lower left), blue decoder box (centre, raised) and a green rounded ViT-VQGAN container (right) holding the tokenizer and detokenizer; no outer frames.
arrangement.inputs_as: the plain-text sentence 'Two dogs running in a field' under orange token bars at the bottom left, and a real photo at the bottom right feeding the tokenizer
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the Train dashed path from the tokenizer to the decoder's last input token stands in for teacher forcing
arrangement.shared: the same dog photo appears as input below and output above the ViT-VQGAN container

insights.structure: A small encoder at lower left feeds a large decoder in the middle, and a separate green tokenizer container stands at the right with the image above and below it.
insights.data: Text and image tokens are rows of small coloured bars with math labels underneath (t_1..t_N; <sos>, i_1..i_M), the outputs i_1..<eos> are bare labels on arrows above the decoder, and the image is a real photo.
insights.emphasis: Size and position carry importance: the blue decoder is the biggest box and sits highest among the models; the tokenizer is grouped in its own green frame.
insights.flow: Bottom-up arrows into each model, one elbow arrow from encoder to decoder, and two dashed elbow lines labelled Train (tokenizer -> decoder inputs) and Inference (decoder <eos> -> detokenizer) crossing between the decoder and the tokenizer.
insights.avoid: The Train and Inference dashed lines run in opposite directions through the same gap and cross the decoder's output side, so the two modes are easy to confuse; the prompt sentence sits detached below the encoder.

figures.lesson: Show a two-part generator by colour-matching each tokenised input row to its model (orange text bars under the encoder, blue image bars under the decoder) and connect the image tokenizer by dashed lines labelled Train and Inference rather than by solid flow.

figures.title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers

arrangement.units: top: one full-width unframed overview row with a caption; bottom: two unframed vertical layer stacks side by side with a grey rounded zoom box between
arrangement.inputs_as: multivariate series drawn as curve strips (top); a pale 'Input Univariate Series' band at the bottom of each stack
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; reconstructed masked patches as grey bars atop the right stack
arrangement.shared: the zoomed Transformer block between the two stacks

insights.structure: A full-width overview row captioned '(a) PatchTST Model Overview' sits on top; below, two vertical layer stacks (supervised left, self-supervised right) flank a zoomed Transformer block in a grey rounded box tied to the left stack's encoder by orange dashed lines.
insights.data: Series are real curves in thin-framed horizontal strips, green for inputs and blue for outputs; layers are wide flat coloured rectangles (yellow norm/patching and embedding, orange encoder, green head); patches are a row of separated pale-blue vertical bars, masked ones drawn as empty dashed outlines, reconstructions as grey bars.
insights.emphasis: Channel independence is shown by five separate green strips feeding one shared grey 'Transformer Backbone' bar; masking is made visible by dashed empty patches only in the right stack.
