insights.flow: Top row reads left to right with hollow block arrows labelled in bold purple ('Channel-independence', 'Concatenate'); the stacks read bottom to top, with a dotted vertical axis at far left listing each layer's tensor shape.
insights.avoid: The left-margin shape axis aligns only with the left stack, and the bottom stacks carry no titles in the crop, so supervised vs self-supervised must be inferred from the head.

figures.lesson: Draw patches as a row of separated vertical bars between the patching and embedding layers, show masking by turning some of them into empty dashed outlines, and track each layer's tensor shape on a left-margin axis.

figures.title: PCT: Point Cloud Transformer

taxonomy.task: point cloud classification and segmentation (offset-attention module)

arrangement.units: one unframed chain of tensor slabs and operator circles/boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: a light-blue 3-D slab labelled N x d
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: No containers: one left-to-right chain of tensors and operators with a skip line running along the bottom from the input to the subtraction and the final adder, and a top line carrying the input to the value branch; a two-row legend underneath.
insights.data: Tensors are 3-D slanted slabs with gradient shading, one saturated colour per role (input light blue, query orange, key teal, attention map blue, value magenta, attention feature purple, output navy), with proportions following shape (flat key, largest N x N map) and italic shape labels above.
insights.emphasis: The offset-attention change is carried by the minus circle (input minus attention feature) and a lever-like switch selecting the solid SL path over the dotted SS path; the legend names everything.
insights.flow: Thick black orthogonal arrows run left to right, with the key branch dipping below via a T (transpose) box and the long input skip running along the bottom edge.
insights.avoid: The dotted alternative paths (SS, the dotted arrow after the attention feature) end in open space, and the switch glyph is not self-explanatory without the legend.

figures.lesson: Give each tensor role its own colour and a 3-D slab whose proportions follow its shape (flat key, large square attention map), and decode colours and operator glyphs in a legend row underneath so the drawing itself carries only shape labels.

figures.title: PETR: Position Embedding Transformation for Multi-View 3D Object Detection

arrangement.units: one canvas: an unframed image-path row at top, a dashed rounded panel for the 3D Coordinates Generator at bottom left, and free-standing encoder/decoder trapezoids at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a fanned stack of real multi-view street photos (top) and plotted camera-frustum point grids (bottom panel)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs end in 'class' and 'bbox' arrow labels
arrangement.shared: the camera frustum meshgrid is drawn once with 'N x' to mean one per view

insights.structure: An image path (top) and a dashed 3D-coordinates panel (bottom left) both feed a pair of facing trapezoids in the middle right, encoder then decoder, with the query generator stacked under the decoder.
insights.data: Multi-view inputs are a fanned stack of real street photos with 'N x', 2D features a single blue slab with H_F / W_F labels, the 3D coordinates as two blue dot meshgrids with axis glyphs, and queries as rows of small cream squares.
insights.emphasis: The new 3D Position Encoder is the biggest tinted shape at the junction of both inputs, and the coordinate generator gets its own dashed frame with a title, making both contributions the largest regions of the figure.
insights.flow: Elbow (right-angle) black arrows bring the feature slab down and the coordinate panel up into the encoder, a straight arrow carries it to the decoder, queries rise vertically from the Query Generator, and two arrows exit right to 'class' and 'bbox'.
insights.avoid: The two point-cloud plots are dense blue dots of small size whose axis labels (u, v, d, x, y, z) and the 'Front' tag are barely legible, and the figure is embedded as a single raster.

figures.lesson: Give the geometric input its own dashed panel drawn as actual plotted point grids (camera frustum -> world space) under the image path, so both streams visibly arrive at the one new block in the middle.

figures.title: Personalized Federated Learning using Hypernetworks

taxonomy.note: architecture other = a server-side hypernetwork h(.; phi) that generates each client's weights

arrangement.units: two unframed panels (overview of all clients, detail of one client) separated by whitespace; boxes are flat rounded rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols v_i and x with arrows down (right panel)
arrangement.losses_at: below the client box in the right panel (L_i)
arrangement.shared: the grey server box h(.; phi) appears in both panels

insights.structure: Two unframed panels separated by whitespace: left, a grey server box in the centre with three client boxes to its left, below and right; right, the exchange for one client i, server on the left and client on the right.
insights.data: Boxes hold only functions in math notation (h(.; phi), f_k(.; theta_k)); each link is a pair of thin opposite arrows labelled theta_k (to the client) and Delta theta_k (back); in the right panel inputs v_i and x enter from above and the loss L_i leaves below the client.
insights.emphasis: Each client has its own fill (pink, peach, lilac) and the math labels on its arrows are set in the same colour, so what travels per client is legible without a legend; the server stays neutral grey.
insights.flow: Hub-and-spoke on the left with bidirectional arrow pairs; the right panel reads top to bottom (inputs down into h and f_i, loss out below) with the theta_i / Delta theta_i exchange horizontal.
insights.avoid: Math-only labels with no words: a reader who has not read the text cannot tell that h is a hypernetwork or that v_i is a client embedding.

figures.lesson: Draw each client link as a pair of opposite arrows labelled with what travels - weights down, weight update up - and set those labels in the client's own fill colour so the exchange is legible per client without a legend.

figures.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control

taxonomy.note: training 'other' = flow matching for the action expert; built on a PaliGemma-style VLM (SigLIP + Gemma); the VLM and action expert act as two weight sets in one transformer

arrangement.units: one model composition flanked by two bracketed side stacks (training data on the left, target embodiments on the right) of tan rounded boxes; the model has two colored token-column groups (blue VLM, green action expert inside a tan panel)
arrangement.inputs_as: real camera photos under ViT trapezoids plus a quoted instruction and noise/state labels
arrangement.shared: one long white bar across each expert's token columns shows shared attention layers

insights.structure: Three columns: a left stack of tan data boxes (pi dataset, Internet pre-training, OXE) gathered by a bracket, a center model where blue VLM token columns and green action-expert token columns are threaded by one long white bar per expert, and a right stack of three tan embodiment boxes (14/18/7-8 DoF) gathered by a bracket.
insights.data: Inputs sit under the model: three real camera frames feed ViT trapezoids, the instruction appears as the quoted string "fold shirt", q_t and noise arrive as bare labels with arrows, and the output action chunk a_t ... a_t+H is a bracketed token row on top.
insights.emphasis: Color splits the two experts (blue = pre-trained VLM, green = action expert with a tan backing panel), and the dashed looping arrows inside the green panel signal iterative flow-matching denoising of the action tokens.
insights.flow: Left-to-right at the top level (data -> model -> robots), but bottom-to-top inside the model (images/text/noise up through token columns to actions).
insights.avoid: The left data panel and right robot panel connect only through brackets, so it is unclear whether they are inputs/outputs or just context; the parameter counts in grey compete with the expert names.

figures.lesson: Bracket the many training-data sources into the model on the left and fan the model out with a mirrored bracket to the robot embodiments it controls on the right, so the figure reads as many datasets -> one policy -> many robots.

figures.title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks

arrangement.units: two unframed halves split by a vertical dotted rule: the fake pair path (with G) on the left, the real pair path on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real image thumbnails: an edge sketch x on the left of each half and a real shoe photo y on the right half
arrangement.losses_at: no loss box; the discriminator's verdict words 'fake' (red) and 'real' (green) at the right end of each half stand for the objective
arrangement.shared: D is drawn twice as the same three-bar glyph with the same label, one per half; x is drawn twice on the fake side (input and copy to D)

insights.structure: Two mirrored cases sit side by side behind a dotted rule - generated pair on the left with G in front, real pair on the right - and both end in an identical D glyph.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are the actual images (edge sketches, synthesized and real shoe photos) labelled with italic x, y, G(x); networks shrink to three outlined bars.
insights.emphasis: The only colour is the verdict text, red 'fake' and green 'real', and the conditional input is made visible by bracketing x with each photo going into D.
insights.flow: Each half reads left to right along straight black arrows; a dashed curved arrow carries x from the input down to D's bracket on the fake side.
insights.avoid: The three-bar network glyphs carry no information about the architecture, and the generator's training signal (L1 term) is not drawn at all, so the figure explains only half of the objective.

figures.lesson: Show a conditional discriminator as two mirrored cases split by a dotted rule, each bracketing the condition with the image into the same three-bar D glyph, and colour only the outputs (red fake, green real).

figures.title: pixelNeRF: Neural Radiance Fields from One or Few Images

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis from one or few images

arrangement.units: no enclosures; three loose clusters (3-D scene with encoder, MLP with its inputs, rendering plot with loss) separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: schematic image card of colored shapes plus a target camera glyph
arrangement.losses_at: right, under the volume-rendering plot as a norm equation
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Single left-to-right strip: a 3-D scene cluster on the left (input view, yellow CNN encoder slab, gridded feature volume W, wireframe cube with a red ray and target camera), then the MLP f as four green bars, then a volume-rendering plot and a rendering-loss equation stacked on the right.
insights.data: The input view and target view are flat schematic cards of colored shapes, the feature volume is a gridded 3-D slab, query samples are purple dots on the red ray, and the fetched feature W(pi x) is a small blue cuboid icon under f.
insights.emphasis: Color-coding ties symbols together: the purple underline on x and red underline on d match the sample dots and ray, and the blue underline on W(pi x) matches the projected feature patch.
insights.flow: A curved black arrow lifts the ray sample out of the 3-D scene into (x,d), then straight arrows run right through f to (RGB sigma), a curve drops into the density plot, and a final curve drops to the loss below.
insights.avoid: The left 3-D cluster overlaps encoder, feature grid and scene cube so tightly that the projection pi x is hard to see; the projection of x onto W is implied, not drawn.

figures.lesson: Show image-conditioned rendering by projecting the query point on the ray back onto a gridded feature volume and carrying the picked cell, as a matching-coloured cuboid, into the MLP as a side input.

figures.title: pixelSplat: 3D Gaussian Splats from Image Pairs for Scalable Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

taxonomy.task: generalizable 3D Gaussian prediction from image pairs
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = per-pixel probabilistic depth prediction (discrete depth distribution sampled with reparameterization)

arrangement.units: two grey-filled boxes stacked in the middle (probability histograms, Gaussian placement along rays) between unframed 3-D frustums at left and right
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D camera frustum with a gridded feature map and three colored pixel rays
arrangement.shared: per-pixel color coding (red/blue/green) runs across all columns

insights.structure: Three columns: a left camera frustum with feature map F and three colored rays, a middle pair of grey boxes stacked vertically (top: three depth-probability histograms; bottom: three ray lines with sampled Gaussian means), and a right frustum with the resulting 3-D Gaussians.
insights.data: Each of three pixels a, b, c keeps one color (red, blue, green) everywhere: highlighted cells on F, ray arrows, histogram bars, blurred Gaussian blobs on lines, and the parameter tuples.
insights.emphasis: The consistent per-pixel color triple is the main device; the stochastic step is spelled out by the 'sample z ~ p_phi(z)' arrow running from the top box to the bottom box.
insights.flow: F[a],F[b],F[c] curve down into network f, which fans out right into both boxes; top box feeds the bottom via the sample arrow; bottom box exits right and up through the parameter tuples into the 3-D Gaussian frustum.
insights.avoid: The network f is three bare unlabeled bars and the fan-out lines from f to six arrows are long and thin, making the split into (phi) and (Sigma, S) easy to miss.

figures.lesson: Follow three pixels by colour from feature-map cell to ray, depth histogram, sampled Gaussian on a depth axis and finally a blurred Gaussian on its ray inside the camera frustum, so per-pixel prediction reads as geometry.

figures.title: Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis / radiance field optimization
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = an explicit sparse voxel grid storing density and spherical-harmonic coefficients, with no neural network

arrangement.units: four unframed steps in one horizontal strip, separated by whitespace and named by sub-labels a) Sparse Voxel Grid, b) Trilinear Interpolation, c) Volumetric Rendering, d) Optimization
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo (a plant) on a tilted image plane with a camera glyph, labelled 'Training Image'
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right, as a typeset 'minimize L_recon + lambda L_TV' equation under the rendering plot, with no arrow to it
arrangement.shared: the ray is one continuous black arrow drawn again in the zoomed cube

insights.structure: A single left-to-right strip of four steps, where the first two are one 3-D scene (grid then zoomed cell) and the last two shrink to a 2-D plot and an equation at the right edge.
insights.data: The input is a real photo on a perspective image plane, the voxels are coloured dots on a dashed wire grid, the SH coefficients are a palette of shaded spheres, and the rendered output is a single teal colour swatch.
insights.emphasis: The translucent blue voxel and its light-blue zoom cone pull the eye to the enlarged cell, where yellow arrows from the eight corner spheres converge on the sample point.
insights.flow: The camera ray runs as one thick black arrow through the grid and on through the zoomed cube; a dotted curved arrow then jumps up and right to the rendering plot, and step d has no arrow at all.
insights.avoid: The optimization step d is detached text with no arrow back to the voxels, so the loop that trains the grid is not drawn.

figures.lesson: Zoom from one cell of the scene representation into an enlarged copy with a translucent wedge, and show the per-sample computation (trilinear weights) as coloured arrows inside the enlarged cell before handing off to a small plot and the loss equation.

figures.title: Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets

arrangement.units: no enclosures; four glyph groups separated by labeled arrows
arrangement.inputs_as: star-shaped neighbourhood graph of circles
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One horizontal chain of four glyph groups joined by three labeled arrows: a star graph (pink neighbours around a teal center), a stack of purple circles, a three-color stack of circles, and a single teal output circle.
insights.data: Node features are circles; multiplicity of aggregators/scalers is drawn as stacked overlapping circle copies, and the operator lists (mean/max/min/std; identity/amplification/attenuation) are bracketed italic column vectors under the arrows.
insights.emphasis: Growth of the circle stacks (one, then four purple, then twelve in three colors) visually counts the aggregator x scaler combinations, which is the contribution.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with labels above each arrow and the bracketed operator list beneath.
insights.avoid: The node colors (purple, red, blue) for the scaler groups are not explained, so a reader cannot tell which color means which scaler.

figures.lesson: Draw multiplicity instead of writing it: the number of overlapping copies in each stack equals the number of options in the bracket on the arrow before it (four aggregators, four circles; three scalers, three coloured stacks), so a reader counts the combinations straight off the circles.

figures.title: Point-BERT: Pre-training 3D Point Cloud Transformers with Masked Point Modeling

taxonomy.task: self-supervised pre-training of point cloud Transformers

arrangement.units: left/centre: unframed pre-training pipeline around a large Transformer box; right: a dashed rounded panel with the tokenizer and decoder used to make discrete targets
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey point-cloud airplane in a blue dashed rounded frame at the top left, split into pastel dashed-circle point patches below it
arrangement.losses_at: beside the encoder output: the predicted token IDs are compared with tokenizer IDs by double-headed arrows between two curly-brace ID rows; 'Contrastive Leanring' arrow above the MPM head
arrangement.shared: the tokenizer appears twice: trained in the right dashed panel, then copied hatched into the pipeline with a blue 'Freeze' arrow between them

insights.structure: A large white Transformer Encoder box sits centre-left with token rows above and below it, the patching steps run down the left edge, and the tokenizer pre-training is fenced off in a dashed panel at the right.
insights.data: Point clouds are drawn as dot scatters and patches as pastel dashed circles whose colours carry through to embeddings and predicted tokens; discrete token IDs are written as coloured numbers inside curly braces.
insights.emphasis: Checkerboard masked tokens and hatched predicted tokens, keyed in a four-entry corner legend, make the masked prediction the visual centre, with mismatched IDs boxed in black.
insights.flow: The pipeline goes down the left column, right along the bottom embedding row, up through masking and the encoder to the MPM head, then a curved arrow carries predictions right to the ID comparison; the right panel feeds in from the right via the 'Freeze' arrow.
insights.avoid: The U-shaped reading path (down, right, up, right) plus a right-to-left freeze arrow makes the order hard to follow, and the 'Contrastive Leanring' label is a typo floating above the head.

figures.lesson: Encode token state by texture (solid input, checkerboard masked, hatched predicted) and key it in a small corner legend, so a masked-prediction objective reads directly from the token rows above and below the encoder.

figures.title: Masked Autoencoders for Point Cloud Self-supervised Learning

arrangement.units: two panels separated by a thick dashed vertical rule, each titled in bold beneath; sub-groups in thin dashed boxes (point cloud, centers, masked patches)
arrangement.inputs_as: grey point-cloud render of an airplane
arrangement.losses_at: top of the right panel, as GT vs Pred patch pairs with a Chamfer loss label
arrangement.shared: token color code (yellow visible, hatched mask, green encoded) spans both panels

insights.structure: Two panels divided by a thick grey dashed vertical line and titled in bold at the bottom: left 'Masking and embedding' (point cloud, FPS centers, KNN patches, masked patches, token embedding) and right 'Autoencoder pre-training' (encoder, decoder, prediction head stacked bottom-up).
insights.data: Point clouds are grey dot renders, patches are blue circles holding point fragments, masked patches get blue hatching, and tokens are small rounded cells colored yellow (visible), hatched grey (mask) and green (encoded) per a dashed legend box.
insights.emphasis: The three token colors carry the masking story across both panels, and the GT/Pred patch pairs with blue double arrows labeled 'CD l2 loss' cap the right panel.
insights.flow: Left panel reads top-down (point cloud -> FPS -> centers, KNN -> patches -> mask -> embedding -> token row); right panel reads bottom-up from token row through encoder and decoder to predictions.
insights.avoid: The left panel's output token row and the right panel's input row are not connected by any line, and the reading direction flips from down to up between panels.

figures.lesson: Key the token states (visible, encoded, masked) to two flat colours and one hatch pattern in a legend box parked against the panel divider, then reuse the same chips in both panels so the hand-off between stages reads without a connecting arrow.

figures.title: Point Transformer

taxonomy.task: point cloud semantic segmentation and classification

arrangement.units: two unframed rows (segmentation network, classification network) sharing the same encoder blocks aligned in the same columns
arrangement.inputs_as: real point-cloud renders (indoor scan, chair)
arrangement.shared: encoder stages align column-for-column across both rows

insights.structure: Two stacked rows of identical-height rectangles: the top row is the segmentation U-net (down then up blocks with four skip arcs above), the bottom row is the classification net that stops after the encoder; a four-item color legend fills the space right of the shorter bottom row.
insights.data: Each stage is a split rectangle (left half = transition/MLP color, right half = yellow Point Transformer) with its (N/k, C) shape printed beneath; inputs are a real colored indoor scan and a grey chair point cloud, outputs a red/blue segmented scan and the text 'Label: chair'.
insights.emphasis: Color alone codes block type (yellow transformer, blue down, green up, grey MLP, peach pooling), and the shape annotations make the hierarchy visible as N shrinks by 4x per stage.
insights.flow: Left to right along each row; skip connections are rectilinear nested arcs above the top row landing on the matching green up-blocks.
insights.avoid: All blocks are the same size regardless of resolution, so the down/up hierarchy has to be read from the tiny shape labels rather than seen.

figures.lesson: Draw each stage as one two-tone slab - left half tinted by stage type (down, up, MLP), right half always the same colour for the shared core layer - so a small legend replaces all in-box text and the repeated core is visible at a glance.

figures.title: PointCLIP: Point Cloud Understanding by CLIP

taxonomy.task: zero-shot point cloud classification via CLIP

arrangement.units: two mirrored unframed columns (left 2D pairs, right 3D training set in a rounded grey-outline panel) with a shared center column
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos with quoted captions (left), point-cloud renders (right)
arrangement.shared: center 3D test set and class-score chart used by both sides

insights.structure: Mirror-symmetric comparison: left column '2D Image-Text Pairs' (photo x caption grid with green diagonal) trains PointCLIP, right column '3D Training Set' (rounded panel of point clouds) trains PointNet++, and both 'Test' arrows converge on a shared center '3D Test Set' airplane and a bar chart.

insights.emphasis: The proposed PointCLIP is a yellow rounded box versus the baseline PointNet++ in grey, and its training source (2D pairs, no 3D data) is the point of contrast.
insights.flow: Top-down within each side (data -> Train -> model), then diagonal 'Test' arrows inward to the center test set and down to the class scores.
insights.avoid: This is a concept teaser, not a pipeline: PointCLIP's internal projection and encoders are absent, so it cannot serve as an architecture skeleton.

figures.lesson: Mirror the proposed and the classic pipeline around one shared test sample in the centre - method box tinted, baseline box grey - so the only asymmetry the reader sees is what each model was trained on.

figures.title: Rethinking Network Design and Local Geometry in Point Cloud: A Simple Residual MLP Framework

arrangement.units: an unframed overview row above two rounded tinted detail panels (green, blue) that expand individual modules, plus a framed legend
arrangement.inputs_as: rendered point-cloud airplane with a highlighted local neighbourhood
arrangement.shared: color links each overview module to its detail panel

insights.structure: Top row is the overview pipeline (input point cloud -> green 'Geometric Affine' box -> two dashed groups of three ResP Blocks labeled Phi_pre and Phi_pos with N braces -> colored output cloud); the bottom row holds two rounded detail panels, green 'Geometric Affine Module' and blue 'Residual Point (ResP) Block', plus an operator legend box at bottom right.

insights.emphasis: Each detail panel takes the color of the top-row module it expands (green affine, blue ResP) and is linked by a colored dashed arrow, so zoom-ins are traceable.
insights.flow: Top row left to right; dashed vertical arrows drop from modules into their detail panels, which each read left to right.
insights.avoid: The aggregation operator A between Phi_pre and Phi_pos is a bare script letter with no explanation in the figure.

figures.lesson: Each proposed module owns one hue (Geometric Affine green, ResP blue) that runs from its overview element through a dashed drop-arrow of the same hue into a same-tinted detail panel placed directly beneath it, so overview and detail are matched by colour and position without long callout lines.

figures.title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation

taxonomy.note: multi-stream: a classification trunk with a segmentation branch that reuses its local and global features; plug-in-module: the T-Net alignment blocks

arrangement.units: top lane: light-blue dotted rounded panel with the classification network; bottom-right: light-cream dotted rounded panel with the segmentation head; bottom-left: two white dotted boxes detailing the input and feature transforms
arrangement.inputs_as: a white n x 3 tensor box with a rotated bold 'input points' label on the panel edge; no point-cloud drawing
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs are 'output scores' boxes (k for classification at the top right, n x m at the segmentation panel's right edge)
arrangement.shared: the segmentation branch reuses the classification trunk: dashed arrows bring the n x 64 local features and the 1024 global feature down into the segmentation panel

insights.avoid: The figure has no data thumbnails, so a reader never sees a point cloud, and the many small numeric labels (mlp (64,128,1024), 512,256,k) crowd the top lane.

figures.lesson: Draw per-point tensors as tall boxes with n x C size labels and the shared MLP as stacked bars joined by a 'shared' line, so weight sharing across points and the max-pool bottleneck read from the shapes alone.

figures.title: PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space

arrangement.units: a grey-filled backbone panel on the left, then two unframed task heads (Segmentation above, Classification below) titled in bold italic
arrangement.inputs_as: tilted plane with point dots
arrangement.shared: backbone output feeds both heads via two hollow arrows

insights.structure: A grey panel on the left titled 'Hierarchical point set feature learning' holds two 'set abstraction' levels (braced underneath); two hollow arrows branch right into a 'Segmentation' row on top and a 'Classification' row below.

insights.avoid: Skip-link dotted lines run along the very top edge across the panel boundary and are faint, so which level connects to which is hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Each hierarchy level keeps one plane colour (green, blue, red) and the segmentation head reuses them in reverse, so the dotted skip lines running over the top of the figure visibly join planes of the same colour.

figures.title: PointNeXt: Revisiting PointNet++ with Improved Training and Scaling Strategies

taxonomy.task: point cloud semantic segmentation and classification

arrangement.units: top lane: unframed staircase of encoder and decoder blocks; bottom lane: three grey rounded panels detailing SA, InvResMLP (red-bordered) and FP, connected in a row by thin arrows
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo-like render of an indoor point cloud scene at the left, the coloured semantic segmentation of the same scene at the right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: An unframed encoder staircase stepping down and decoder stepping back up fills the top row, and three grey detail panels for SA, InvResMLP and FP sit in a row beneath, each under the block it expands.
insights.data: Input and output are point-cloud scene renders (raw colours on the left, class-coloured segmentation on the right), and every block carries a bracketed [N/k, C] size label under it.
insights.emphasis: Thick red outlines mark only the parts that differ from PointNet++ (stem MLP, InvResMLP blocks and panel, changed size labels), explained by a red-keyword footnote at the bottom right.
insights.flow: Thin grey arrows run left to right and down the encoder steps, back up the decoder steps, with long skip arrows across the top; pink dashed arrows drop from blocks to their detail panels.
insights.avoid: The vertical text inside the tall blocks forces head-tilting, and the many red outlines on small size labels dilute the red accent.

figures.lesson: When a method is a revision of a known architecture, draw the baseline in plain fills and outline only the changed blocks and shapes in a thick red border, with a one-line footnote naming the convention.

figures.title: PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds

arrangement.units: top row of grey stage boxes; below them dashed rounded zoom panels for stage 1 and stage 2, connected by funnel lines
arrangement.inputs_as: real lidar point-cloud render titled 'Point cloud'
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Top row is a four-step pipeline of large grey rounded boxes (Pillar Feature Net, Backbone (2D CNN), Detection Head (SSD)) between input and output lidar renders; below, two dashed rounded panels expand the first two boxes, joined to them by funnel lines.
insights.data: Input and predictions are real lidar renders (predictions with blue/red 3D boxes); intermediate tensors are 3-D cuboids with C/H/W/P axes, the pillar is an orange bar, and a pillar-index strip routes features into the pseudo image.
insights.emphasis: Orange marks the single pillar through every tensor in the Pillar Feature Net panel, letting the reader follow one pillar from points to pseudo-image.
insights.flow: Top row left to right; funnel lines drop from stage boxes to their zoom panels, which also read left to right (the backbone panel top-down then right via Deconv/Concat).
insights.avoid: The backbone zoom panel crowds small cuboids, labels like 2C, H/2, W/2 overlap the box edges, and the detection head gets no expansion.

figures.lesson: Trace one pillar through the encoder in a single accent colour (orange): the column standing on the point cloud, its slab in the stacked tensor, its feature column and its pixel in the pseudo-image, while all other tensor bulk stays white and grey.

figures.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation

arrangement.units: two unframed stacked rows (Fine-tuning, Prefix-tuning) each with fanned overlapping cards for the three tasks
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted tokenized example sentence colored by input/output
arrangement.shared: same example sentence under both rows

insights.structure: Two stacked comparisons titled at the top right: 'Fine-tuning' shows three overlapping pink Transformer cards (Translation, Summarization, Table-to-text); 'Prefix-tuning' shows one grey 'Transformer (Pretrained)' with three overlapping small pink Prefix cards stacked at its left edge.
insights.data: Token positions are tall white slots inside each transformer card; the example input and output are a real tokenized sentence below each block, input words in blue and output words in green with '[SEP]' between.
insights.emphasis: Pink = task-specific trainable parameters versus grey = frozen, so the eye sees whole pink models (top) shrink to small pink prefixes (bottom).
insights.flow: Top to bottom comparison; within each block, tokens read left to right with no arrows.
insights.avoid: No arrows show how the prefix interacts with layers (activations at every layer), so the mechanism is inferred only from placement.

figures.lesson: Show per-task storage cost by fanning stacked copies: full model copies fanned in the trainable colour above, versus one grey frozen model with only a small fan of trainable prefix cards beside it, so the size of the fanned thing is the cost.

figures.title: Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Cross Attention Control

taxonomy.task: text-driven image editing by injecting cross-attention maps

arrangement.units: Two horizontal bands stacked and divided by a dashed rule: the cross-attention mechanism on top, the three control operations below, each operation a whitespace-separated mini-diagram with a caption underneath.
arrangement.inputs_as: a flat 4x4 grid labelled Pixel features phi(z_t); the prompt appears only as token rows labelled Tokens Keys / Values (from Prompt)
arrangement.shared: the attention-map stack M_t defined in the top band is redrawn in beige in each bottom mini-diagram

insights.structure: A top strip computes cross-attention as one row of operands joined by X glyphs; below a dashed rule three equal-width mini-diagrams show the three edit operations on attention-map stacks.
insights.data: Every tensor is a small white or tinted grid with its symbol beneath (phi(z_t), Q, K, M_t, V, phi-hat(z_t)); attention maps are decks of five offset grids, and prompt tokens are long thin rows of cells.
insights.emphasis: Beige fill marks source maps and mint fill target maps throughout the bottom band, so each operation reads as which colour replaces which; the re-weighted output shows deeper beige cells.
insights.flow: Straight black arrows run left to right through the top computation; in the bottom band curved arrows show maps being swapped (Word Swap) or copied into a merged stack (Adding a New Phrase).
insights.avoid: No image, prompt text or diffusion step appears, so the reader cannot see what the edits do; the top band's title sits below its row and the bottom title has a typo.

figures.lesson: Explain the mechanism once in a top strip (symbols under each operand, X glyphs between them), then give each variant of the contribution its own mini-diagram in a bottom strip that reuses the same colour-coded objects, separated only by a dashed rule.

figures.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning

taxonomy.task: multi-task adaptation of a frozen language model with learned soft prompts

arrangement.units: Left half: three task batches (tables) each feeding its own coloured task-model box, with the blue pre-trained model at top; right half: three prompt squares merging into one mixed-task batch table feeding one blue pre-trained model; the halves are split by a dashed vertical rule.
arrangement.inputs_as: small row tables representing batches, with labelled example rows; prompts as coloured squares
arrangement.shared: the blue 'Pre-trained Model (11B params)' box is drawn once per half, in the same blue

insights.structure: The figure is split by a dashed vertical rule into a baseline half with three stacked task-model boxes and a method half with a single pre-trained model box, so the two halves differ visibly in box count.
insights.data: Batches are drawn as small tables whose first rows hold example ids (a1, b1, c1), and in the right half each row of the mixed batch is prefixed with a coloured A/B/C prompt cell.
insights.emphasis: Task identity is carried by one consistent colour per task (yellow, orange, red) across model copies, prompt squares and batch cells, while the shared model stays blue in both halves.
insights.flow: Arrows run left-to-right from batches into models; on the right, three prompt squares fan into the mixed batch with crossing curved arrows, then one arrow goes to the model.
insights.avoid: The crossing curved arrows from the three prompt squares into the batch rows tangle in a small space and are hard to trace to their rows.

figures.lesson: Contrast a baseline and the proposed method in two halves that reuse the same colours for the same tasks, so the cost difference (three model copies vs one model plus three tiny prompts) is visible without reading.

figures.title: PromptIR: Prompting for All-in-One Blind Image Restoration

arrangement.units: an unframed U-net composition with green prompt blocks, plus two translucent tinted zoom panels (PIM, PGM) expanding the bottleneck prompt block
arrangement.inputs_as: real degraded photo at top-left
arrangement.shared: prompt components reused at every decoder level

insights.structure: A four-level U-net of orange Transformer Blocks fills the upper area (encoder column down the left, decoder levels to the right with green Prompt Blocks inserted at each decoder level); a long rounded legend panel runs down the left, and two tinted zoom panels (grey-blue PIM, yellow PGM) sit lower right, fanned out from the Prompt Block.
insights.data: Input and restored images are real tiger photos; feature tensors are labeled H x W x C fractions on arrows; prompt components are stacks of colored slices; ops are small labeled tiles (3x3, 1x1, GAP, sigma) and circled operators.
insights.emphasis: The new prompt modules are green blocks against orange backbone blocks, and the translucent wedge-shaped zoom panels make PIM and PGM visually spring from the Prompt Block.
insights.flow: Downsampling is red downward arrows on the left, upsampling blue upward arrows, the main path left to right with a global skip over the top to an addition before the output.
insights.avoid: The figure is dense: legend, U-net and two zoom panels compete for space, and tensor-size labels crowd the arrows at every level.

figures.lesson: Each submodule box's fill colour becomes the background of its detail panel, and a translucent wedge in that same tint fans out from the small box to the panel, so the link between a box and its expansion needs no arrow or label.

figures.title: Robust deep learning based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN

taxonomy.task: protein sequence design from backbone structure

arrangement.units: one tinted rounded model container holding two white rounded sub-panels (encoder, decoder); input and output as peach boxes outside; two lettered detail panels below without frames
arrangement.inputs_as: ribbon render of two chains above a backbone-atom distance sketch and a peach input box
arrangement.shared: pink/green chain colouring repeated on every feature grid

insights.structure: Panel A spans the top: input cartoon and backbone-atom sketch on the left, one large light-blue rounded 'ProteinMPNN' container holding two white rounded sub-panels (Backbone Encoder, Sequence Decoder) in the middle, and Probabilities -> Iterative decoding circle -> Sequence -> Output on the right; detail panels B (decoding order) and C (tied chains) share the bottom row.
insights.data: Edge and node features are small grids of square cells split into a pink part and a green part matching chain A/B of the input cartoon, so tensors carry chain identity; the input is a ribbon render plus two N-Ca-C triangles joined by dashed distance lines.
insights.emphasis: The model is the only big tinted container, and the input and output are peach rounded boxes with bold 'Input:'/'Output:' prefixes framing it; the novel random-decoding order is called out by text inside the decoder and contrasted against left-to-right decoding in panel B.
insights.flow: Left to right through encoder to decoder, with 3x dashed loops for repeated node/edge updates inside each sub-panel and a long return line from Sequence back into the decoder's Nodes forming the iterative-decoding loop.
insights.avoid: Several long orthogonal lines (Zeros feed, encoder-to-decoder node line) cross panel borders and run under each other, making the routing between encoder and decoder hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Carry chain identity through every tensor: colour each chain once in the input cartoon and then split every node and edge feature grid into the same two colours, so multi-chain conditioning reads without labels.

figures.title: Q-Transformer: Scalable Offline Reinforcement Learning via Autoregressive Q-Functions

taxonomy.task: robot offline RL with per-dimension autoregressive Q-values
taxonomy.note: Q-Transformer itself; paradigm closest listed sequence-model RL

arrangement.units: unframed columns of cells, one per action dimension, separated into time steps by dashed vertical lines
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of real robot camera frames labelled history of states
arrangement.shared: bottom time axis with step bars (t, t+1, T)

insights.structure: One column per action dimension, each a vertical stack of discretised bin cells over a grey token square, grouped into environment steps t, t+1 and T by vertical dashed separators and grey bars along the bottom.
insights.data: Q-value bins are coloured cells by role: green for the dataset action's target, red with a white '->0' glyph for unobserved actions, pale yellow for the max carried from the next dimension; the state history is a stack of real robot photos at the far left.
insights.emphasis: The conservative '->0' red cells dominate the grid and a dotted legend box top right decodes the three cell colours, making the regulariser as visible as the Bellman target.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside a column (token, bins, max), then grey elbow arrows route each 'max' back into the previous column's target cell; across columns left to right along a long time axis, with the Monte-Carlo return box looping a line over the top back to the start.
insights.avoid: The many thin grey back-arrows from 'max' boxes into earlier columns cross each other and are easy to misread as forward flow.

figures.lesson: Keep two time scales apart by stacking them: per-dimension token columns above, environment steps as grey bars on an axis beneath, with dashed vertical rules where one environment step ends - and colour the cells only by their role in the target.

figures.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

taxonomy.note: training: parameter-efficient finetuning with quantized frozen base

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by thin vertical rules, sharing row labels
arrangement.inputs_as: none; components only
arrangement.shared: row headers on the left with bit widths

insights.structure: Three method columns (Full Finetuning, LoRA, QLoRA) separated by thin vertical rules share one set of bold row headers on the left (Optimizer State 32 bit, Adapters 16 bit, Base Model) and each ends in a precision label underneath.
insights.data: Only outlined rounded rectangles whose size encodes memory: one huge optimizer box vs three small ones, and a narrower base-model box for the 4-bit transformer; page icons inside boxes and a dashed CPU box show paged optimizer state.
insights.emphasis: The proposed column alone gains magenta paging arrows to a dashed CPU box and a shrunken base-model box; the added mechanism, not a colour fill, is the highlight.
insights.flow: Blue arrows run down for parameter updates and green arrows run up for gradient flow within each column; columns are read left to right as a progression; a corner legend names the three arrow colours.

figures.lesson: Lay the compared fine-tuning methods out as columns over shared row labels for memory tiers with their bit widths, so the size of each box alone shows the memory saved, and keep arrow colour for the kind of flow (updates, gradients, paging) with a small legend.

figures.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond

arrangement.units: three unframed repeated stacks, one per training stage
arrangement.inputs_as: camera icon with resolution label; document icon for text
arrangement.shared: identical block stack and 'Learnable Query Embs' label repeated per column

insights.structure: Three identical columns side by side, one per training stage, each a bottom-to-top stack of camera icon, ViT block, thin CrossAttn bar and wide QwenLM block, headed by a large serif stage title and footed by its data description.
insights.data: Data appear only as black glyphs: a camera with a tiny 'Low/High Resolution' label below the ViT and a document icon with an up-arrow beside the LM; learnable query embeddings enter the CrossAttn bar as a text label from the left.
insights.emphasis: Each block carries a snowflake or flame and switches fill (lavender-blue frozen, beige trained), so the only thing that changes across columns is which blocks freeze.
insights.flow: Thin up-arrows run bottom to top inside each column; columns read left to right as stage 1 to 3.
insights.avoid: Model names are set in a very large serif that dwarfs everything else, and the mixed serif/sans labels look inconsistent.

figures.lesson: Show a multi-stage training schedule as the same small stack repeated per stage, changing only each block's fill (blue frozen, beige trained) and its snowflake or flame, so the reader compares stages by colour alone.

figures.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

taxonomy.task: knowledge-intensive question answering, fact verification and question generation

arrangement.units: Left column of three example inputs (tinted text boxes with task labels); centre teal rounded frame = retriever; adjacent blue rounded frame = generator; right column of three example outputs. Frames are separated only by a small gap.
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example text in monospace inside tinted boxes, one per task, each labelled with its task name
arrangement.losses_at: no loss box; a grey dashed 'End-to-End Backprop through q and p_theta' arrow runs right-to-left above both frames
arrangement.shared: the retrieved document stack inside the retriever frame feeds the generator by two arrows that cross the frame boundary

insights.structure: Two large rounded frames, teal for the retriever and blue for the generator, sit side by side in the middle, with example inputs stacked on the left edge and example outputs stacked on the right edge.
insights.data: Queries and answers are real monospace sentences in tinted boxes tagged (x) or (y), the query embedding is a dark green bar, and documents are a fanned stack of white pages with wavy lines labelled z1..z4.
insights.emphasis: Each module's name is set large in the frame's own colour with a '(Non-Parametric)' or '(Parametric)' subtitle, and the training path is a long grey dashed arrow across the top.
insights.flow: Arrows run left-to-right from query through q, MIPS (dashed fan-out to document vectors) to the document stack and on to p_theta; the backprop arrow runs right-to-left above, and one line loops under the retriever to bring the raw input to the index.
insights.avoid: The input-to-generator line runs along the bottom under the whole retriever frame and up into the document stack, which reads as if the raw query feeds the index rather than the generator.

figures.lesson: Frame each learned module as a large coloured container named in its own colour, and pair each task's input and output across the figure by giving them the same tinted text box.

figures.title: RandLA-Net: Efficient Semantic Segmentation of Large-Scale Point Clouds

arrangement.units: one tinted rounded container holding a row of plain layer rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: rendered 3-D indoor scan with tensor shape below
arrangement.shared: nested dashed skip arcs over the top

insights.structure: One wide single row inside a light-blue rounded container named 'RandLA-Net' at its bottom edge: encoder boxes, bottleneck, decoder boxes and three FC head boxes in sequence, with input and output renders outside at both ends.
insights.data: Each layer is a white outlined rectangle labelled with its rotated (N, D) shape, height shrinking toward the (N/256, 512) bottleneck and growing back; real rendered indoor scans show the input and colour-labelled output, with tensor shapes under them.
insights.emphasis: No colour separates the novel parts; the operation names on the arrows (LFA/RS in the encoder, US/MLP in the decoder) carry the method.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right on short black arrows with an op label above and below each; nested grey dashed skip arcs span over the top joining mirrored encoder and decoder boxes.
insights.avoid: Box heights barely differ and the rotated shape labels are tiny, so the size-encoding of downsampling is hard to read; the contribution (LFA module) is not visually distinguished.

figures.lesson: Put every layer on one tinted rounded backdrop named after the network, write each layer's operations above and below its arrow, and size each box by its tensor (height for point count, width for channels) so down- and up-sampling are visible without extra marks.

figures.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

taxonomy.task: interleaved reasoning and acting with LLM prompting

arrangement.units: white rounded transcript panels with overlapping grey title tabs, arranged in two task rows
arrangement.inputs_as: question/task text box at the top of each row
arrangement.shared: outcome marks (cross/check) in panel corners

insights.structure: Two task rows split by a long dashed rule: HotpotQA on top (question box, stacked Standard and CoT panels, Act-Only panel, tall ReAct panel on the right) and AlfWorld below (task box over Act-Only on the left, ReAct on the right); each prompting style is a white rounded panel with a grey tab title numbered (1a)-(2b).
insights.data: Everything is monospace transcript text with bold Thought/Act/Obs prefixes, tool verbs (Search, Finish, Think) in bold blue with bracketed arguments.
insights.emphasis: Highlighter rectangles mark the story: red behind wrong reasoning or failed observations, green behind the facts leading to the answer, blue behind Think steps; red crosses vs green checks in each panel corner give outcomes, and ReAct always takes the right-hand, tallest panel.
insights.flow: Read top to bottom inside each transcript, left to right across baselines to the method; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Dense small monospace text makes it a reading figure rather than a diagram; it only works at full page width.

figures.lesson: An agent's reasoning-acting loop can be shown with no arrows at all: print the trajectory as Thought/Act/Obs lines in monospace, colour the tool verbs, highlight right and wrong spans in green and red, and end each competing transcript with a check or a cross.

figures.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

taxonomy.task: retrieval-augmented LM pretraining and open-domain QA

arrangement.units: two unframed vertical pipelines separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: grey dashed text box with a real example sentence
arrangement.shared: same module boxes and green knowledge-corpus note in both halves

insights.structure: Two identical vertical pipelines side by side (pre-training left, fine-tuning right) with no titles or divider, each a spine of input text, retriever, encoder and answer box with corpora hung off the right.
insights.data: Text instances are grey dashed-border boxes with real typewriter examples ([MASK] in red); learned modules are pale-blue rounded boxes; data sources are folded-corner notes, yellow for sampled training data and green for the knowledge corpus; every element carries a blue italic symbol (x, z, theta, phi, y).
insights.emphasis: Only the corpus notes and the example text change between halves, so the reader sees the same retrieve-then-encode architecture serves both stages.
insights.flow: Top to bottom down each spine; dashed arrows labelled 'sample' and 'retrieve' come in from the right-side notes, and a curved skip arrow on the left carries x past the retriever into an (x, z) pair.
insights.avoid: The two halves have no headings, so pre-training vs fine-tuning must be inferred from the example text and data notes.

figures.lesson: Drawing pre-training and fine-tuning as two identical copies of one pipeline, changing only the example text and the data note, shows that the modules are shared without any arrow or label saying so.

figures.title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer

taxonomy.task: accelerated MRI reconstruction with recurrent transformers

arrangement.units: three unframed repeated 3-D scenes each with a cloud call-out
arrangement.inputs_as: MRI slice on a perspective patch-grid plane
arrangement.shared: identical scan and call-out composition repeated in each panel

insights.structure: Three equal unframed panels in a row, captioned (a) Swin/PVT, (b) SwinIR/ViT, (c) ReconFormer (ours), each repeating one scene: scan on a patch plane, layer stack above it, cloud call-out on the right showing the layer's inside.
insights.data: A brain MRI slice lies on a tilted perspective plane cut by a white patch grid; layers are red wireframe slabs joined to the image by a red vertical line; inside the cloud, tokens are pale-blue parallelograms with a coloured attention quad and an FFN up-arrow.
insights.emphasis: The stack shape differs per panel (shrinking pyramid in a, constant in b and c) and only (c) adds overlapping multi-scale coloured attention quads in its cloud, plus '(ours)' in the caption.
insights.flow: Bottom to top from scan to stack, then a thick dashed arrow out to the cloud and back; panels compare left to right.
insights.avoid: The difference between (b) and (c) is a small change inside the cloud that is hard to see at print size, and the earlier reader described the pyramid in (a) as widening upward though it narrows.

figures.lesson: Compare architectures by repeating one identical 3-D scene - the scan on a gridded patch plane, the layer stack above it, the attention sketch in a cloud call-out - and change only the stack's shape and the attention sketch between panels.

figures.title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer

taxonomy.task: recurrent multi-scale attention for MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: three unframed lettered panels, one top band and two bottom halves
arrangement.inputs_as: MRI slice thumbnail with coloured multi-scale patches
arrangement.shared: scale colour coding across (a)

insights.structure: Three lettered unframed panels: (a) multi-scale attention fills the top band with Scale Head 1-3 stacked as rows under Query/Key/Value column headers, (b) the recurrent cell and (c) the transformer layer share the bottom row.
insights.data: (a) starts from an MRI slice with translucent coloured patches of three sizes; Q/K/V are wireframe cuboids subdivided more as scale grows, becoming solid coloured bars after attention and grey bars after the linear layer; (b) uses yellow rounded K/Q/V boxes with circled x/+ and hidden states c^(t), h^(t).
insights.emphasis: One colour per scale (green, orange, blue) is carried from the patches on the scan through the Q/K/V cuboids to the concatenated token row.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel; (b) branches h^(t) into K, Q, V with brackets and merges to c^(t+1) and output; (c) has residual loops beneath to circled +.
insights.avoid: Typos and tiny labels ('Liner', italic 'SoftMax' on arrows) and the three panels are not visually connected, so how (b) and (c) relate to (a) is left to the caption.

figures.lesson: Give each attention scale one colour and carry it from that scale's patches on the input scan, through its Q/K/V cuboids, into its slot of the concatenated token row.

figures.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

arrangement.units: One grey framed 'Agent' region holding the loop of modules; the environment sits below it outside the frame; an algorithm box on the right half.
arrangement.inputs_as: the environment box below the agent frame
arrangement.losses_at: no loss; feedback arrows run inside the frame
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Panel (a) is a light-grey square 'Agent' container holding five rounded boxes (Self-reflection, Evaluator, Actor as LM roles; Trajectory and Experience as memories) with the Environment box below and outside; panel (b) beside it is Algorithm 1 pseudocode at equal height.
insights.data: Components are text-only rounded boxes; LM roles are blue-grey and memories pale yellow, each with its memory type in parentheses on a second line.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the inner loop Trajectory -> Evaluator -> Self-reflection -> Experience -> Actor drawn above the classic Action/Obs-Reward loop, distinguished by the two colour families rather than an accent.
insights.flow: Elbowed orthogonal arrows: Actor out right to Environment (Action), back up the left edge (Obs / Reward) into Trajectory and Self-reflection; inner arrows labelled Internal feedback, External feedback, Reflective text.
insights.avoid: The External feedback line runs along the container's left edge and overlaps the outer loop line, so the two returns are hard to separate.

figures.lesson: Draw the agent as one large container and the environment as a box outside it, close the classic loop with Action / Obs-Reward elbow arrows around the container, and colour the boxes by kind: model roles in one cool tint, short- and long-term memory in one warm tint.

figures.title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models

taxonomy.task: retrieval augmentation for black-box LMs via ensembling

arrangement.units: unframed overview on the left; one tinted rounded detail panel on the right with three parallel rows
arrangement.inputs_as: grey box with the test context sentence
arrangement.shared: colour identity for documents (blue) and context (grey) across both halves

insights.structure: Left ~40%: an unframed overview on a loose 2x2 grid (Retriever, retrieved documents, test context, black-box LM); right ~60%: a pale-yellow rounded 'Ensemble' panel expanding the Input Reformulation step, tied to the overview by a speech-bubble pointer.
insights.data: Documents are light-blue rounded boxes and the test context grey boxes with real example text; the LM is a black cube with an orange question mark; each of three rows ends in a small horizontal bar chart over apple/pear/not.
insights.emphasis: The Retriever is a solid dark-red block and retrieval labels are dark red, while the ensemble panel's per-row bar colours (green, purple, pink) are stacked into one merged chart via a curly brace.
insights.flow: Thick grey arrows: context up to Retriever, right to documents, down into the LM, output 'Apple' below; in the panel three parallel left-to-right rows converge through a brace to the merged distribution.

figures.lesson: The ensemble is drawn as data, not as an operator box: each pass gets its own bar colour, and a curly brace gathers the three bar charts into one stacked chart whose segments keep those colours, so each document's contribution stays visible in the merged result.

figures.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

taxonomy.note: architecture other: a deep stack of conv layers with identity skip connections around each pair (residual blocks); the taxonomy has no residual/skip-connection key.

arrangement.units: Three unframed columns side by side, each headed by its model name; rows aligned across columns by output size, with an 'output size' label in the left margin.
arrangement.inputs_as: a plain text label 'image' at the top of each column
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (each column ends in an 'fc 1000' box)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three tall columns (VGG-19, plain, residual) stand side by side with rows aligned so equal output size sits at equal height, and long empty arrows in the VGG column keep it in register.
insights.data: Every layer is a small tinted box with its kernel, width and stride written inside, and the output resolution is a left-margin label rather than a drawn tensor.

insights.flow: Each column reads strictly top to bottom on short straight arrows; the shortcut arcs bow out to the right and rejoin the column two boxes lower.
insights.avoid: The figure is extremely tall and narrow with very small box text, so it only works at full page height; a shorter version would group repeated layers with a repeat count.

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed network as an exact copy of its baseline column with only the new connections added, and align both columns row by row, so the contribution is the visible difference.

figures.title: Restormer: Efficient Transformer for High-Resolution Image Restoration

arrangement.units: Top row: input photo -> conv -> Transformer level 1 ... refinement -> conv -> output photo, unframed. Left/middle: the U (encoder column down, decoder column up), unframed. Right: two full-width tinted panels (b) GDFN and (a) MDTA, each a borderless tinted rectangle labelled in its top-right corner; lower-left: a framed legend box.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real degraded photo top-left, mirrored by the restored photo top-right, joined by a long global residual line over the top
arrangement.shared: none; repeated Transformer blocks are drawn once per level with an 'x L_i' repeat count

insights.structure: A U-shaped encoder/decoder occupies the left two columns while two tinted detail panels (GDFN above, MDTA below) fill the right, with the glyph legend boxed in the lower-left corner.
insights.data: Only the degraded and restored real photos appear (top-left and top-right); every intermediate is a line labelled with its tensor size such as H/4xW/4x4C, and the attention is a tiny grey C-hat x C-hat matrix inside panel (a).
insights.emphasis: The proposed MDTA and GDFN are coloured yellow and cyan inside one expanded decoder block and blown up into panels whose background tint matches the wedge leading from that block.
insights.flow: The main path reads left to right along the top row, drops down the encoder column via red downsample arrowheads, climbs back up via green upsample arrowheads, and each detail panel reads left to right ending in a circled + at the right edge.
insights.avoid: The 14-entry legend repeats glyphs that are already labelled in place and the translucent wedges cross the decoder's skip lines, so the left-centre gets crowded.

figures.lesson: Put a hierarchical U on the left two-thirds and expand the proposed sub-blocks into tinted detail panels on the right, tying each panel to its tiny source box by a translucent wedge of the same tint.

figures.title: Retinexformer: One-stage Retinex-based Transformer for Low-light Image Enhancement

arrangement.units: three tinted square-cornered background panels: one full-width top band, two half-width detail panels below
arrangement.inputs_as: real low-light photo plus illumination prior map
arrangement.shared: op-type colour coding and a shared legend across panels

insights.structure: A pale-green full-width band (a) holds the illumination estimator (i) on the left and the U-shaped corruption restorer (ii) on the right; below, a cream panel (b) details the attention block and a peach panel (c) details the illumination-guided self-attention, each titled in bold coloured text top-left.
insights.data: Real photos for input, light-up map, lit-up and enhanced images; feature maps as stacks of coloured slabs; layers as oblique 3-D cuboids and thin parallelogram slabs coloured by op type (yellow IGAB, blue LN, green stride conv, orange deconv), with tensor sizes in grey beside each.
insights.emphasis: The light-up feature F_lu is drawn as a real colour-mapped image and routed by long lines from (a) into the IG-MSA blocks of (b) and (c), plus coloured callouts (i over-exposure, ii amplified noise) showing the problem being fixed.
insights.flow: Estimator left to right; restorer encoder runs right along the top row, turns down at the right edge and returns left along the bottom to the enhanced image; panel (c) runs left to right through Q/K/V token stacks to the output feature.
insights.avoid: Very dense: two legend boxes, many grey size labels and long cross-panel lines make it crowded at column width.

figures.lesson: Each detail panel's background tint repeats the fill of the block it expands (cream-yellow panel for the yellow IGAB cuboid, peach panel for the salmon IG-MSA block), and one guidance line runs from the overview across the panel border into both detail panels, so the reader can follow both the zoom-in and the conditioning signal.

figures.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: language modelling with parallel training and recurrent inference

arrangement.units: (a) Parallel representation: unenclosed vertical stack on white; (b) Recurrent representation: a light-blue rounded panel holding the per-step cell, with state and output arrows running out of it; captions (a)/(b) below each
arrangement.inputs_as: the typeset symbol X (and X_n with the word 'Input' in (b))
arrangement.shared: the same symbols Q, K, V and the GN pill appear in both panels; nothing is linked between them

insights.structure: Two panels sit side by side, an unenclosed narrow parallel-form stack on the left and a wider light-blue recurrent-cell panel on the right, each captioned (a)/(b) underneath.
insights.data: All intermediates are typeset math symbols floating on the canvas (Q, K, V, S_{n-1}, O_n) rather than boxed tensors, and the parallel computation is written as one equation instead of drawn.
insights.emphasis: The recurrent form is the only part on a tinted background, and its state line S_{n-1} to S_n runs straight across the panel as the longest line in the figure.
insights.flow: Panel (a) reads bottom-to-top from X to GN; panel (b) reads bottom-up from X_n into Q/K/V, then left-to-right along the state line and out through GN to O_n on the right.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) collapses the whole parallel computation into a single equation with no visual counterpart to the decay matrix D, so the two forms cannot be matched piece by piece.

figures.lesson: When a method has two equivalent forms, draw both side by side with the same variable names and let the second panel add only the extra pieces (the state line, the operators), so the reader sees what changes.

figures.title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens

arrangement.units: one overview made of two rows (retriever on top inside a purple dashed frame, layer stack below with the repeated block in an orange dashed frame) plus a separate red-dashed zoom panel on the right expanding one block
arrangement.inputs_as: a vertical column of chunk-coloured token cells, plus a 'Retrieval dataset' cylinder at top-left
arrangement.shared: the encoded neighbours E1, E2 are drawn in both the overview and the zoom panel

insights.structure: The left two-thirds stacks a retrieval row (dataset cylinder, purple dashed 'Frozen kNN Retriever' with two BERT boxes, Transformer Encoder, encoded neighbours) over a layer row (EMB, orange dashed 'RETRO block (x L)' holding ATTN-CCA-FFW, READ), and the right third is a red dashed zoom panel of CCA.
insights.data: Input tokens are a vertical 12-cell column coloured green/blue/yellow per chunk with curly braces C1-C3, and each chunk's retrieved neighbours are 2x5 cell strips in a paler tint of that chunk's colour.
insights.emphasis: CCA is the only red-outlined block in the stack and the zoom panel repeats that red in its dashed frame, title and inner CA boxes, tying detail to block by colour.
insights.flow: The input column feeds right through the layer row while thin coloured elbow lines climb the left edge from each chunk into the retriever, and the encoded neighbours drop down into CCA as K and V.
insights.avoid: The long chunk-routing elbows run around the whole figure's left and top edges and cross the 'Condition' line, which is hard to trace; route them shorter if copying.

figures.lesson: Each input chunk keeps one fill colour (green, blue, yellow) everywhere it appears, in the input column, in its retrieved neighbours as a paler tint, and in the detail panel, so a reader can follow which chunk attends to which neighbours without reading labels.

figures.title: RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots

arrangement.units: three light-grey tinted bands (Phase 1, Phase 2, Deployment) with dark tab labels, the first two grouped under a section title and separated from the third by a thick grey rule
arrangement.inputs_as: rounded boxes with math symbols (states, actions, history stack, privileged environment factors)
arrangement.losses_at: between lanes: the green 'Regress' double arrow linking the two latents in the gap between Phase 1 and Phase 2

insights.flow: Each band reads left to right into a_t, and dashed elbow arrows close the loop from a_t through the environment picture back over the top and under the bottom to the observation boxes.
insights.avoid: The deployment history box reads 'x_t-50, a_t-51' while phase 2 reads 'x_t-51, a_t-51' — an index inconsistency; keep labels identical across repeated bands.

figures.lesson: Close the agent-environment loop with dashed arrows from a_t through a picture of the environment - a simulator render in training, a real photo at deployment - back to the observation boxes, and outline only the modules trained in that phase in red.

figures.title: Accurate prediction of protein structures and interactions using a 3-track network

arrangement.units: one grey tinted band per track (1D, 2D, 3D) with a boxed tag at its corner; repeated blocks are coloured outline rectangles overlaid across exactly the bands they update
arrangement.inputs_as: real data plots (MSA as a coloured matrix plot, pair features as a matrix with axes) entering the 1D and 2D bands
arrangement.shared: outputs at the right edge (SE(3)-Transformers box, combined pair map) take from both the 1D and 2D bands

insights.structure: Three grey horizontal bands stacked top to bottom (1D track, 2D track, and a 3D track under the right half only), each named by a boxed corner tag, with a yellow outline around the 2-track block and a larger blue outline around the 3-track block spanning all three bands.
insights.data: Every state is a picture of its data: viridis heatmap tiles for 1D features, dark pair maps with a bright diagonal for 2D, rainbow cartoon proteins for 3D, and the inputs are a coloured MSA plot and a pair-feature matrix with axes.
insights.emphasis: The repeated 3-track block is the largest coloured frame and the only one crossing all three bands, keyed against the smaller yellow 2-track block by a two-entry outline legend at top right.
insights.flow: States move left to right along each band, operations (Attention, Outer product & aggregation, Graph-Transformer, SE(3)-Transformer) label vertical and diagonal arrows between bands, and dashed arrows stand for skipped repeated blocks before the outputs branch up to a BB-only model and down to a full-atom model.
insights.avoid: The diagonal arrow labels ('Outer product & aggregation', rotated 'Masked Attention') are rotated and crowd the tiles; small axis tick labels on the input plots are illegible at figure size.

figures.lesson: Draw the 1D, 2D and 3D representations as three stacked horizontal bands in which every state is a thumbnail of its own data (feature tile, pair map, cartoon structure), and mark one repeated block by a coloured outline that spans exactly the bands it updates.

figures.title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears

taxonomy.task: aligning LLMs with human feedback by ranking
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a single policy model scoring several sampled responses against a ranking, contrasted with PPO's four-model setup

arrangement.units: two panels inside one dashed frame separated by a dashed vertical rule, each titled by a bold method name at its top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: lavender rounded pills labelled 'Query'
arrangement.losses_at: top of each panel: Advantage pill at the top of PPO, the bold 'Align by ranking' statement at top-right of RRHF
arrangement.shared: the same colour code for models, responses and queries across both panels

insights.structure: One dashed outer frame split by a dashed vertical rule into a 'PPO' half (four model boxes in a 2x2 grid around Query, Model Response, Value and Advantage pills) and an 'RRHF' half (one Language Model box above three query-response rows and a Human Label/Reward Model box).
insights.data: Models are large yellow (trained) or dark-gold (fixed) rounded boxes, queries are lavender pills, responses and scores are green pills shaded dark-to-light, and scores are numeric pills 100/80/60.
insights.emphasis: The RRHF half needs a single yellow model where PPO needs four, and its takeaway is set in large bold black text 'Align by ranking SFT from best' beside a dashed green group of three score pills.
insights.flow: In PPO the query flows bottom-up into two models with a dashed Advantage loop back around the outer edges; in RRHF responses go right into the reward box, scores rise to the bold text, and a dashed arrow returns left into the Language Model.
insights.avoid: Yellow vs dark-gold is the only cue for trained vs fixed and is never keyed; colour roles should get a small legend or label.

figures.lesson: Keep one colour code for roles across both halves (models as large yellow/gold boxes, text as green pills, queries as lavender pills) so the reader can count the models each method needs, and shade one colour family dark-to-light to tie each candidate response to its score.

figures.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale

taxonomy.note: adapter-conditioning here = FiLM layers conditioning the image backbone on the sentence embedding; rl-offline = imitation learning from demonstrations

arrangement.units: one tall column: a stacked set of rounded cards for the per-frame FiLM-EfficientNet + TokenLearner tower, then separate rounded boxes for tokenized inputs, Transformer and Action, with a left column for the instruction encoder and a right column of text annotations
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of six real robot-camera frames (top right) and a quoted instruction sentence in a rounded box (top left)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the Action box of discrete action tokens ends at a real output photo
arrangement.shared: the per-frame image tower is drawn once as a stack of offset copies (one per frame)

insights.structure: One vertical column holds the whole policy, with the per-frame vision tower drawn as a stack of offset rounded cards, the language encoder parked in a narrow left column, and a right column of headings plus hyper-parameter text bracketed to each stage.
insights.data: The instruction is quoted text above a row of light-blue word tokens, the input and output are real robot-camera photos (a stacked six-frame input at top, a single gripper photo at bottom), and intermediates are rows of small coloured token squares (coral vision, green action) and a 9x9 dotted token grid.
insights.emphasis: Emphasis is by naming rather than highlighting: each stage gets a large right-column title with its parameter count, and FiLM conditioning is shown by repeating the typeset (1+gamma) . + beta row after every MBConv bar.
insights.flow: Data runs straight down the centre with short arrows, the sentence embedding branches out of the left column as thin horizontal light-blue lines into each FiLM row, and six pink arrows fan the per-frame tokens into the concatenated token row.
insights.avoid: The right-column text is a dense list of hyper-parameters in small grey type (pixel sizes, block counts, parameter counts) that competes with the diagram and would not survive scaling to one column.

figures.lesson: For a tall single-path model, put the stage names and their hyper-parameters in a right-hand text column with vertical span brackets, keeping the drawing itself to coloured bars and token rows.

figures.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control

arrangement.units: three tall rounded outline panels left to right (data, model, deployment), each titled in grey text inset into its top border
arrangement.inputs_as: white cards each pairing a real photo with a Q:/A: example
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training is the 'Co-Fine-Tune' arrow label along the bottom
arrangement.shared: purple answer/action boxes recur in the data panel and the model panel

insights.structure: Three grey-outlined rounded panels side by side with titles set into their top border: data examples (left), the RT-2 model (wide middle, a grey box holding a blue ViT and an orange Large Language Model panel), and closed-loop control photos (narrow right).
insights.data: Training data are photo cards with Q:/A: text and a grey token-number answer, the visual input is a 3x3 grid of robot camera frames, tokens are small pill rows, and actions are written as ΔT/ΔR vectors in purple boxes.
insights.emphasis: Actions are drawn in the same purple as the text answers of web VQA examples, and the purple thread runs from braced output tokens through 'De-Tokenize' to a 'Robot Action' box, with 'RT-2' as the largest bold text.
insights.flow: Panels are connected only by two grey elbow arrows along the bottom ('Co-Fine-Tune', 'Deploy'); inside the middle panel the prompt and images enter from the left, rise through the LLM, and output exits down via a purple elbow.
insights.avoid: The token-number answers in light grey ('A: 311 423 ...') are nearly invisible against white; the 3x3 robot frame grid is too small to read.

figures.lesson: Give robot actions the same colour as the text answers in the training-data examples (purple boxes) and carry that colour along the output tokens -> de-tokenize -> ΔT/ΔR box, so 'actions are just another answer' reads without a word.

figures.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

arrangement.units: left: the residual block in a light-grey rounded frame, containing two darker blue-grey sub-panels (Time Mixing, Channel Mixing); right: the full model column with the same grey frame holding collapsed Time/Channel Mixing boxes, topped by a light-blue 'RWKV-LM Head' frame
