insights.data: No tensors or tokens are drawn; inputs and intermediates are single-letter symbol boxes (R, K, V, mu, sigma) and the output is only the text 'Output Probabilities'.
insights.emphasis: Saturated salmon (WKV), orange (sigma) and yellow (mu) fills appear only inside the zoomed Time and Channel Mixing panels, while the collapsed blocks on the right are flat grey.
insights.flow: Both columns read bottom-to-top along a central spine, with residual lines leaving below each LayerNorm, running up the frame's left side and rejoining at a circled-plus.
insights.avoid: Nothing ties the left panel to the right one (no zoom lines or matching tint), so a reader must infer from the names that the left column is the inside of the right column's grey frame.

figures.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos

arrangement.units: one unframed row of modules; time shown by faded copies behind each module rather than by panels
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a diagonal 'time' arrow at the left edge; prompts as the words mask, points, box under the prompt encoder
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the predicted mask is a real frame with a coloured overlay in the middle of the row
arrangement.shared: the memory bank's output is drawn as several return arrows over the top, one per stored frame, all landing on the single memory attention block

insights.structure: All seven parts sit on one horizontal row, with the prompt encoder dropped just below the mask decoder and a memory loop arching back over the top from the memory bank to memory attention.
insights.data: Input and output are real video frames, each a stack of fading copies receding up-left, and the output frame carries a green mask overlay; prompts are the plain words mask, points and box with up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: Recurrence is the visual idea: every module has ghosted copies behind it and the memory feedback lines fade from dark (latest) to pale (oldest), so the memory mechanism stands out without a highlight colour.
insights.flow: Short dark arrows run left to right along the row; the grey return lines leave the memory bank upward, run left along the top with right-angle bends and drop into memory attention.
insights.avoid: The ghosted copies are very faint and the return lines stack close together, which makes it hard to count how many memories feed back.

figures.lesson: Draw a streaming, frame-by-frame model by stacking faded translucent copies behind each module and the input frame, and run the memory feedback as nested right-angle return lines over the top that fade with age.

figures.title: Segment Anything

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each captioned below with a letter and bold keyword; they are facets (task, model, data) rather than sequential stages
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of four drawn prompt squares gathered by a curly brace, plus a photo thumbnail labelled 'image'
arrangement.shared: the pale-yellow model box appears in all three panels

insights.structure: Three panels in a row separated by whitespace and captioned beneath '(a) Task', '(b) Model', '(c) Data': (a) inputs-model-output, (b) an opened pale-yellow model container with three coloured sub-blocks, (c) a model/data annotate-train loop above a large blue dataset card.
insights.data: The four prompt types are drawn literally in identical black-outlined squares (red/green dots, a rectangle, a blue blob, the words 'cat with black ears'), and input/output are photo thumbnails with a translucent blue mask on the output.
insights.emphasis: The model keeps one pale-yellow identity colour in all three panels, and captions bold the keyword and the acronyms SAM and SA-1B.
insights.flow: Panels (a) and (b) read bottom-to-top from prompt/image to 'valid mask'; panel (c) is a clockwise loop of thin arrows labelled annotate and train with a dashed grey arrow down to the dataset card.
insights.avoid: Panel (c)'s dataset card uses a tiny photo and four grey bullets that read as text clutter beside the diagram panels.

figures.lesson: Show a promptable model's interface by drawing every prompt type literally in small identical squares (dots for points, a rectangle for a box, a blob for a mask, the words for text) bracketed into a single input arrow beside the image.

figures.title: Segment Anything

arrangement.units: one unframed pipeline; modules grouped only by colour family (green image side, purple prompt side, orange decoder)
arrangement.inputs_as: a large real photo at the left, with prompts entering as word labels from the bottom
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single main row without containers: photo, a very wide green image encoder, a column of grey embedding squares, a circled plus, an orange mask decoder bar, then three stacked output photos; the purple prompt side (conv trapezoid, prompt encoder bar) sits under the decoder.
insights.data: The input is a large photo, the image embedding is a vertical column of five small grey squares, prompts are plain word labels (mask, points, box, text) with up-arrows, and outputs are three copies of the photo with blue masks of different extent each tagged ', score'.
insights.emphasis: Box size encodes cost: the heavyweight image encoder is the largest box while the prompt encoder and mask decoder are thin bars, and the fan to three masks shows ambiguity handling.
insights.flow: The image path runs left to right along the main row, prompts enter from below with short vertical arrows, and one branching arrow fans out to the three outputs at the right.
insights.avoid: The ', score' text beside each output is a placeholder rather than a value; show actual scores or a symbol.

figures.lesson: Show an ambiguity-aware segmenter's output as a short vertical stack of the same photo with different mask extents, each tagged with a score, fanned from the decoder by one branching arrow.

figures.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation

taxonomy.note: modality 'tabular' stands for item-ID interaction sequences; the photos only depict items

arrangement.units: unframed horizontal rows (embedding, self-attention band, FFN, prediction) named at the right edge, crossed by three time-step columns; a left brace groups attention + FFN as one stackable block
arrangement.inputs_as: real product photos in a curly-bracketed row labelled 'Training Action Sequence'
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the top bracketed row of product photos ('Expected Next Item') is the target
arrangement.shared: the self-attention layer is one band spanning all three columns; FFN boxes repeat per column

insights.structure: Three time-step columns run upward through four unframed rows named at the right edge, with a left brace marking attention + FFN as one stackable block and curly brackets around the input and target photo rows.
insights.data: Items are real product photos at bottom and top, each item's embedding is a solid red, green or blue bar, and the prediction bars mix those colours in proportion.
insights.emphasis: Self-attention is the only element spanning all columns: a wide salmon band with black arrows of varying thickness running from earlier positions to later ones.
insights.flow: Reading goes bottom to top along vertical arrows in each column, and inside the attention band the diagonal arrows only go up and to the right, showing causality.
insights.avoid: The fourth input photo has no column above it and the multi-colour prediction bars have no key, so the shift-by-one target and the colour mixing must be inferred from the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw causal self-attention as one wide band across the time-step columns with arrows that only go up-and-right, and colour each item's embedding so its share in later prediction bars is visible.

figures.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

taxonomy.task: grounding LLM plans in robot affordances

arrangement.units: two unframed halves (baselines, method) side by side; the method half's core is enclosed in a dashed grey rounded container
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue speech bubble with the quoted user request, repeated over each half
arrangement.shared: the same user request bubble heads both halves

insights.structure: Two halves each headed by the same blue speech bubble; the left half stacks three rows of model-name box plus reply bubble (GPT3, LaMDA, FLAN), the right half holds a dashed rounded container with LLM and Value Functions bubbles above a combined SayCan bubble and a numbered plan bubble outside.
insights.data: Candidate skills are quoted italic phrases inside speech bubbles whose font size encodes each skill's score, with small robot photos inset in the Value Functions and SayCan bubbles.
insights.emphasis: The name is split 'Say' in LLM blue and 'Can' in value-function red, and the SayCan bubble fill is a blue-to-pink gradient, so the combination is shown by colour alone.
insights.flow: Reading is left to right from the baselines to the method; inside the container the two scorer bubbles' tails point down into the SayCan bubble, which points right to the plan.
insights.avoid: The smallest scored phrases are illegibly tiny, so the size encoding is visible but the low-scoring text cannot be read.

figures.lesson: Encode each candidate skill's score by its font size inside the speech bubbles, and blend the LLM bubble's blue and the value-function bubble's red into the combined bubble and the two halves of the method's name.

figures.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

taxonomy.task: affordance value functions for robot skills
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a bank of skill-conditioned value functions scoring every skill from one observation

arrangement.units: three unframed panels captioned (a)-(c) below; (b) and (c) share an identical chart-plus-photo skeleton while (a) shows the module
arrangement.inputs_as: a real robot-camera photo above the module box
arrangement.shared: the same five skills listed in (b) and (c)

insights.structure: Three panels in a row captioned (a), (b), (c) beneath: (a) a camera photo over a pink 'Value Functions' box with spokes fanning to two columns of open circles, (b) and (c) each a horizontal bar chart of five 'Pick up the ...' skills beside the camera photo that produced it.
insights.data: Per-skill scores are bold numerals at the left spoke ends coloured green (high) or dark red (low), skill names at the right spoke ends, and bar charts with values 0 to 1.00 on a lavender background.
insights.emphasis: The pink box is the only filled shape in (a) and reuses the Value Functions pink of Figure 1; high bars in (b) are pink against near-zero pale blue bars in (c).
insights.flow: In (a) the photo arrow runs down into the box and hairline spokes fan out left and right; (b) and (c) are read as chart-then-photo pairs left to right.
insights.avoid: Bar-chart text and score numerals are small and low-contrast at column width, and the symmetric left/right spoke fans split score from skill name across the figure.

figures.lesson: Draw a value-function module as a hub whose spokes fan out to every skill with its score printed at the spoke end (green high, red low), then pair a bar chart of those scores with the observation photo that produced them.

figures.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning

taxonomy.note: modality multi = the method is data-agnostic; the figure is a parameter-space sketch with no data

arrangement.units: one unframed vector sketch with labels placed at path ends
arrangement.inputs_as: a dark filled circle labelled x (starting parameters)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; optima squares at the right stand for the objectives
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A parameter-space sketch with no containers: two clients' iterate chains diverge from a start point x (client 1 up, client 2 down), a dark 'server' point sits between them, optima are square markers to the right, and a legend column fills the far right.
insights.data: Iterates are filled circles (dark start and server, blue client iterates, pale grey intermediate averages), optima are squares (blue true optimum x*, orange client optima x1*, x2* joined by a dashed line), and small white squares mark centralised SGD steps.
insights.emphasis: No method is drawn; the problem is made visible as geometry — the server point lands off the true optimum because blue client chains bend toward their orange optima.
insights.flow: Reading is left to right from x along colour-coded thin arrows (blue client steps, green server steps, black vertical drift arrows), ending at the legend.
insights.avoid: Legend arrows are drawn as tiny vertical strokes that are hard to match to the thin diagonal arrows in the sketch; the grey intermediate circles are not keyed.

figures.lesson: Show heterogeneity as geometry: draw each client's local steps as a dot chain bending toward its own optimum marker and the server point as their average, so client drift is visible without a single equation.

figures.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning

taxonomy.note: modality multi = the method is data-agnostic; the figure is a parameter-space sketch with no data

arrangement.units: one unframed vector sketch reusing the teaser's markers
arrangement.inputs_as: a dark filled circle labelled x
arrangement.shared: marker and colour code shared with Figure 1

insights.structure: One row of iterate dots from x to y1 along the bottom left, the two optimum markers (x1*, x*) stacked in a middle column, and a legend column at the right.
insights.data: Iterates are filled circles (dark start, blue later ones), each step is drawn as vector addition: a dashed black local-gradient segment rising up-right plus a red downward correction arrow, with their sum as the blue step.
insights.emphasis: The correction term is the only red element and repeats at every local step, visibly bending the path down toward x* away from x1*.
insights.flow: Left to right along the iterate chain, with each step read as dashed up, red down, blue along.
insights.avoid: The optimum markers are placed in a separate middle column away from the path, so the 'toward x*' direction must be inferred rather than shown by an arrow.

figures.lesson: Draw the inside of a local update as vector addition per step - dashed raw gradient, the proposed correction as a red arrow, the resulting step in the client colour - reusing the marker and colour code of the teaser.

figures.title: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions

taxonomy.task: molecular energy and force prediction from atom types and positions

arrangement.units: Three columns separated by thick dashed vertical rules: left = untinted stack of coloured layer boxes (embedding, 3 x interaction, atom-wise, softplus, sum pooling); middle = yellow framed panel 'interaction'; right = salmon framed panel 'cfconv'.
arrangement.inputs_as: serif math tuples (atom types Z, positions r, features x^l) at the top of each column
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the predicted energy E-hat is a math symbol at the bottom of the left column
arrangement.shared: the positions input is one thick line branching into each interaction layer; the cfconv and interaction internals are drawn once in their own panels

insights.structure: Three columns divided by heavy dashed vertical rules zoom from the full layer stack to the interaction block to the cfconv layer, each expansion a framed panel tinted like the box it expands.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are only serif math tuples (Z, r, x^l, x^{l+1}, E-hat) at the column tops and bottoms, and each layer box states its type and width ('dense, 64', 'rbf, 300').
insights.emphasis: The novel cfconv layer is the single salmon box in the yellow interaction panel and is expanded into a full salmon panel at the right edge.
insights.flow: Every column reads straight top to bottom along a thick black spine, with the position input entering from the top right as a second thick line that bends left into the layers it conditions.
insights.avoid: The columns carry no (a)/(b)/(c) labels and the 'interaction'/'cfconv' panel names sit small in the bottom-right corners, so a reader who misses the colour match has no textual cue that the columns are zooms.

figures.lesson: Use the fill colour of a layer box in a stack as the background tint of the panel that expands it, so two levels of zoom read without connector lines.

figures.title: Solving Inverse Problems in Medical Imaging with Score-Based Generative Models

taxonomy.task: medical image reconstruction (sparse-view CT / undersampled MRI) via score-based sampling
taxonomy.note: the example data drawn are CT images and sinograms; the paper also covers MRI k-space

arrangement.units: an overview grid (left) and a zoom-in of one step (right), unframed and separated by a vertical dotted rule
arrangement.inputs_as: a small grey 'noise' tag at the top-left of the chain, with measurement y as a circled variable at the bottom right
arrangement.shared: the variables x̂_t, y and ŷ_t appear in both panels

insights.structure: Two panels split by a vertical dotted grey line: left a three-row grid of circled variables (sampled x̂_t, corrected x̂'_t, noisy measurements ŷ_t) from 'noise' to a grey 'results' box with ellipsis columns; right one correction step opened up as data.
insights.data: Variables are white circles with serif math labels; in the right panel the iterate and output are grayscale CT thumbnails and the measurement-domain data are magma-coloured sinogram slabs, three stacked in perspective where masks Λ, I−Λ, λΛ combine.
insights.emphasis: Orange is reserved for everything the method adds (measurement path and correction) against black for unconditional generation, keyed in a grey legend box, and the right panel expands that orange step with real data.
insights.flow: Left panel runs right along the top chain, with orange arrows dropping and rising between rows and long orange curves sweeping from y back to every ŷ_t; right panel runs left to right T → mask combine → ⊕ → T^-1.
insights.avoid: The long orange curves from y back to ŷ_tN and ŷ_tN-1 run under the grid and crowd the legend box; the overlapping perspective slabs make which mask applies to which slab hard to read.

figures.lesson: Separate the generative chain from the measurement correction purely by arrow colour (black vs orange, legend below), then open one correction step beside it as images that move into the measurement domain, get masked with y, and come back.

figures.title: Score-based diffusion models for accelerated MRI

arrangement.units: a chain of unenclosed image thumbnails above, and one green rounded box with four flat bars as the zoomed-in step
arrangement.inputs_as: real MR images: pure-noise x_T at top left and the aliased measurement y at bottom left
arrangement.shared: y feeds every reverse step by dotted lines

insights.structure: A top row of seven square MR thumbnails (x_T noise through x_{t+2}...x_{t-1} to x_0) forms the reverse-SDE chain, and below it at the bottom right one step (x_{t+1} to x_t) opens into a green rounded box holding four tall bars: Predictor, Data consistency, Corrector, Data consistency.
insights.data: Every state is a real knee MR image whose noise fades left to right, and the aliased measurement y is a real image at bottom left whose dotted navy lines rise into each step arrow and run into the expanded box.
insights.emphasis: A single long cyan 'Reverse SDE' arrow over the chain names the process, and the zoom-out box with a green outline and colour-coded bars (mint predictor, cyan corrector, the two DC bars sharing grey-blue) carries the method's contribution.
insights.flow: Left to right on thick navy block arrows across the top; a green dashed line drops from the x_{t+1} arrow into the step box, which runs left to right with thin black arrows and exits as x_t on a dashed arrow.
insights.avoid: The dotted y lines join only two of the step arrows and then trail off into '...', so it is unclear that y conditions every step; draw the conditioning into all steps or say so.

figures.lesson: The sampling chain is a row of real image thumbnails going from noise to the clean scan under one long process arrow, with the measured aliased image below sending dashed conditioning lines up into the steps.

figures.title: Concurrent Spatial and Channel 'Squeeze & Excitation' in Fully Convolutional Networks

arrangement.units: four unframed panels each with a centred caption below; a grey-filled notation box at bottom left
arrangement.inputs_as: a white 3-D wireframe feature cuboid U (C x H x W)
arrangement.shared: the same U cuboid and the same squeeze glyphs recur across panels (b)-(d)

insights.structure: Four captioned panels in a 2 x 2 grid: (a) a small top-left schematic of the encoder-decoder before and after inserting red SE blocks, (b) cSE and (c) sSE as single-path blocks, and (d) the largest, bottom-right, stacking sSE above cSE and summing them.
insights.data: The input U is a white wireframe cuboid labelled C, H, W, and each output is a cuboid whose faces are tinted to show the reweighting: vertical coloured slices for channel excitation, a 2 x 2 quadrant of blue/yellow/red/green for spatial excitation, both on the scSE output.
insights.emphasis: The colour of the output cuboids makes the difference between channel and spatial recalibration visible at a glance, and the combined block in (d) is the largest panel.
insights.flow: Left to right in each panel: U branches into a squeeze path (thin bars or a 2 x 2 map with sigma) and a skip that meets it at a circled x, then a circled + in (d) merges the two recalibrated cuboids.
insights.avoid: The panel captions mislabel the blocks ('Spatial Squeeze and Channel Excitation (cSE)' and the scSE caption repeats 'Channel Excitation'), and the grey notation legend is wedged into the bottom-left corner; check captions against the method and give the legend its own row.

figures.lesson: Show what an attention block reweights by colouring its output cuboid - per-channel slices in different tints for channel attention, a 2 x 2 coloured quadrant pattern for spatial attention, both on the combined block - against a plain white input cuboid.

figures.title: Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once

taxonomy.task: universal interactive segmentation with multimodal prompts

arrangement.units: (a) the architecture with two dotted zoom boxes at its right edge, (b) the interaction loop, side by side and captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'Class/Sentence', a real photo and small drawn visual prompts (blob, scribble, box, point) beside a photo along the bottom edge
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; class and mask embeddings as two grey token rows at the top of (a)
arrangement.shared: the SEEM decoder appears in both panels, redrawn as a gradient bar in (b) with the same prompt-token colours

insights.structure: Panel (a) stacks encoders, a joint representation bar, token rows and the decoder from bottom to top, with two dotted zoom boxes stacked at its right; panel (b) repeats the decoder small inside a loop diagram.
insights.data: Every input type becomes a labelled row of coloured squares (green queries, purple image features, orange text, pink memory, blue visual prompt), and visual prompts are drawn literally as tiny thumbnails of a blob, scribble, box and point.
insights.emphasis: The method name SEEM is bold italic with an eyes icon on the decoder bar, and the prompt-type colours recur in the attention zoom and the interaction panel to tie the contribution together.
insights.flow: Short up-arrows carry inputs from the bottom encoders to the top embeddings in (a); dashed lines lead right to the zoom boxes; in (b) dashed red curves loop from the decoder out to the robot and person icons and back into the memory and visual prompt rows.
insights.avoid: Many small elements in thin type (zoom boxes, emoji, faint striped decoder fill) make the figure hard to read at column width, and the two zoom boxes are crowded against panel (a).

figures.lesson: Give every input type its own token colour and tint the encoder that produces it in the same colour, so a later attention zoom can show which token types interact without a legend.

figures.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions

arrangement.units: unenclosed icons with bold 'Step N' headings; generated examples as stacked rounded cards with a 'Task' tab
arrangement.inputs_as: a checklist icon captioned '175 seed tasks'
arrangement.shared: the Task Pool database is both start and end of the loop; the same LM robot icon recurs at three steps

insights.structure: A clockwise loop with no boxes: seed tasks and the Task Pool at top left, Step 1 and Step 2 across the top, two Step 3 branches (Yes / output-first and No / input-first) returning leftward in the lower middle, and Step 4 Filtering at bottom left pointing back to the pool.
insights.data: Steps are flat clip-art icons (checklist, database cylinder, monitor with question bubble, funnel with gears), and generated data are white stacked cards with a dark-blue 'Task' tab holding real example instructions, inputs, labels and outputs.
insights.emphasis: Real example text in the cards does the explaining, and small robot 'LM' icons mark exactly which steps call the language model.
insights.flow: Thick lavender-to-purple gradient arrows run left to right along the top, turn down the right edge, split at a junction into Yes/No arrows pointing left into the two card stacks, then curve left into Filtering and diagonally back up to the Task Pool.
insights.avoid: The decorative gradient arrows and clip-art icons carry no information and the Step 4 return arrow is a vague diagonal; keep the loop but use plainer arrows and a clear return path.

figures.lesson: Draw each generated artifact as a tabbed card stack holding one real example (instruction, input, output) and mark every model call with the same small robot icon on its arrow, so the pipeline reads as concrete data moving around a cycle.

figures.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

arrangement.units: two unboxed side-by-side panels separated by rules, each with 'Step N' text sections; a bottom strip repeats both
arrangement.inputs_as: a real prompt in a grey chip at the top of each panel
arrangement.shared: the same prompt, retriever icon and LM network glyph appear in both panels

insights.structure: A narrower baseline RAG panel at left and a wider 'Ours' Self-RAG panel at right, split by a solid grey vertical rule, with a dotted horizontal rule cutting off a bottom strip that repeats both on a second prompt where Self-RAG skips retrieval.
insights.data: Everything is one worked example in real text: grey prompt chips, retrieved passages in grey rounded boxes numbered by black circled digits, generations in green, errors in red underline, and reflection tokens (Retrieve, Relevant, Irrelevant, Supported, Partially, No Retrieval) as small coloured chips.
insights.emphasis: The Self-RAG title is in red, its panel is wider, and the coloured reflection chips plus the ranking '1 > 3 > 2' in Step 3 show the critique that the baseline lacks.
insights.flow: Top to bottom by blue-numbered 'Step N:' headings; inside steps, dashed grey curved arrows fan from the retriever magnifier to three parallel 'Prompt + k' columns, and a blue dashed arrow loops the chosen segment back to the LM for the next round.
insights.avoid: The panels are dense with small type, callout bubbles overlap the baseline's output text, and a stray red '4' badge sits in the final output; keep fewer words per step and keep callouts clear of the text.

figures.lesson: Running the baseline and the method on the same worked example in adjacent panels, with errors set as red underlined text and the method's judgements as coloured chips beside each segment, lets a reader compare the outcomes without reading every sentence.

figures.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

arrangement.units: four flat pastel boxes with drop shadows, no containers; whole figure inside a thin black frame
arrangement.inputs_as: a small pale-blue 'Input' box
arrangement.shared: one central Model M box used by both loops

insights.structure: A symmetric figure-eight: a lavender Model M box in the centre with a pale-blue Input box above, a pink Feedback box on the left and a peach Refine box on the right, each tied to the model by an outgoing arc from its top and a returning arc into its bottom.
insights.data: There is no data drawn; the model box holds a line-art brain-circuit icon with a light bulb, and each step's meaning is a one-line caption on a light-grey strip beneath its side.
insights.emphasis: Very thick black curved arrows and oversized serif labels in the side boxes make the two-loop idea the whole figure; circled numerals 0, 1, 2 on the arrows give the order.
insights.flow: Input drops down into the model (0), arcs out left and back from Feedback (1), then out right and back from Refine (2), reading left to right across the bottom captions.
insights.avoid: With no example input or output the figure could describe any iterative method; pair the loop with a concrete text example as the paper's second figure does.

figures.lesson: For a self-feedback method, put one model box at the centre and draw each role (critique, revise) as its own loop of thick curved arrows out of and back into that same box, numbering the arrows to fix the order.

figures.title: Self-supervised Graph Learning for Recommendation

arrangement.units: two horizontal lanes split by a double rule; each stage is a small square-framed thumbnail with a bold label below
arrangement.inputs_as: a bipartite user-item graph thumbnail in a square frame
arrangement.shared: the GCN model icon is repeated in all three paths (shared encoder)

insights.structure: Two rows separated by a double horizontal rule: the main supervised path on top (graph, GCN model, representation, L_main) and the self-supervised path below, where the graph splits into two parallel sub-rows, each with an augmentation panel of three variants ED, ND, RW divided by dashed vertical lines.
insights.data: The user-item graph is a small bipartite thumbnail (yellow user circles left, blue item circles right) whose augmented copies show dropped edges as dashed lines and dropped nodes as dashed circles; representations are vertical stacks of small coloured cell columns.
insights.emphasis: Repeating the same GCN icon and representation grid in both rows makes the added SSL branch read as a copy with augmentation, and the representation grids differ in colour between the two views.
insights.flow: Left to right in each row along thin black lines; the two lower sub-rows merge by right-angle lines into one circle for L_ssl.
insights.avoid: The top row has a long empty arrow from Graph Structure to the GCN icon and the GCN icons are tiny and illegible; drop the dead space and use a legible model glyph.

figures.lesson: Stack the main task as a thin top row and the added self-supervised branch below it, both starting from the same small bipartite graph thumbnail, and draw each augmented view as a copy of that graph with the dropped edges and nodes dashed.

figures.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

taxonomy.task: memory-efficient sigmoid image-text loss across devices
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = pairwise sigmoid (binary) loss over all image-text pairs, the paper's replacement for the softmax contrastive loss

arrangement.units: four matrix panels left to right, separated by whitespace only, one per step of the loss computation
arrangement.inputs_as: column headers I1..I12 (images) and row headers T1..T12 (texts) grouped by device
arrangement.losses_at: a 'loss' bar under each matrix (from the second on), split into one segment per device; the last one sums across devices
arrangement.shared: devices are drawn as coloured header strips repeated in every panel; the row-device order rotates between panels to show the swap

insights.structure: Four copies of the same 12 x 12 text-by-image matrix stand in a row, one per computation step, each with device-coloured header strips on its top and left edges.
insights.data: Pairs are cells: '+' on the diagonal for positives, '-' for negatives, a check mark for cells already counted, and the cells being computed now filled yellow inside a device-coloured outline.
insights.emphasis: Only the current block is bright yellow with a thick coloured border while everything finished fades to pale cells, so each panel shows exactly what one device holds at that moment.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right; small coloured arrows drop from each matrix's columns into a per-device loss bar whose percentages (33%, 66%, check) track progress, ending in a 'Cross Device sum' arrow.
insights.avoid: Nothing in the panels names the steps (no step titles or numbers), so the reader needs the caption to know that the rotating row-device labels mean a cross-device swap.

figures.lesson: To explain a distributed computation, repeat the same matrix once per step and colour rows, columns and loss bars by the device that owns them, so the reader tracks ownership by colour alone.

figures.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

arrangement.units: One unframed diagram: two mirror columns of symbols above a shared input circle.
arrangement.inputs_as: an outlined circle with the symbol x (no image), and two outlined view circles reached by arrows labelled with sampled augmentations t ~ T, t' ~ T
arrangement.losses_at: top, as a horizontal double arrow labelled 'Maximize agreement' between z_i and z_j
arrangement.shared: the shared encoder f(.) and head g(.) appear only as identical arrow labels in both columns

insights.structure: One input circle at the bottom centre forks into two mirror columns of symbols (view circle -> h -> z), joined horizontally at two levels by labelled double arrows.
insights.data: Data and features are math only: outlined circles for x and its two views, bare bold symbols for h and z, with no image or tensor drawn.
insights.emphasis: The two horizontal double arrows carry the message as words: 'Maximize agreement' across the top between z's and 'Representation' between the h's, marking what is trained and what is kept.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top: diagonal arrows labelled with the sampled augmentations climb from x to the views, then straight vertical arrows labelled f(.) and g(.) rise in each column.
insights.avoid: With no boxes or tint, f and g read as edge labels rather than networks, so a reader cannot see that the two columns share weights; a richer method would need explicit modules.

figures.lesson: A whole framework can be drawn as a math diagram: circles for data, bare symbols for intermediates, functions as arrow labels, and the objective as a labelled double arrow across the top — enough when the method has few parts.

figures.title: SimMIM: a Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling

taxonomy.task: masked image modelling pre-training by raw-pixel regression
taxonomy.note: paradigm: SimMIM is concurrent with MAE (both regress raw pixels of masked patches); listed under MAE as the closest founding masked-image-modelling method in the list

arrangement.units: One unframed diagram: input grid at the lower left, a patch row along the bottom right, two stacked model boxes above it, and prediction/target patch rows at the top right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo divided into a 3x3 grid of patches, then a row of patch thumbnails with masked ones drawn as hatched squares
arrangement.losses_at: top, as red vertical double arrows between each predicted patch and its original, with the 'l1 loss' label to the left of the row
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: An L-shaped layout: a patch grid at lower left feeds a horizontal masked patch row, above which an encoder box and a one-layer head box are stacked, topped by predicted and target patch rows.
insights.data: Patches are real photo crops, masked ones are grey hatched squares, and predictions are the same crops rendered blurred and faded so prediction vs target reads by image quality.
insights.emphasis: One dark-red accent colours every model outline, arrow and loss double arrow, and only the masked columns have outputs above them, so the loss visibly applies to masked positions only.
insights.flow: Right along the bottom ('Mask' arrow), then up through encoder and head, and finally vertical red double arrows between the two top patch rows.
insights.avoid: The large empty region above the input grid at the upper left leaves the figure lopsided; the input could sit higher or the figure be tighter.

figures.lesson: For masked prediction, stack the predicted patches directly under their target patches, column-aligned with the masked slots below, and join each pair with a short coloured double arrow labelled with the loss.

figures.title: Exploring Simple Siamese Representation Learning

taxonomy.note: training tag: SimSiam has no EMA teacher; it predicts the stop-gradient output of its own other branch, the closest listed value is self-distillation

arrangement.units: Two unframed vertical branch columns separated by whitespace, joined at the bottom by a rounded split line and at the top by the 'similarity' label.
arrangement.inputs_as: text label 'image x' only, no picture; views named x1, x2 as italic labels beside the column feet
arrangement.losses_at: top centre, as the bare word 'similarity' where both branch lines meet; no box
arrangement.shared: the shared encoder is drawn twice, once per branch, as identical light-blue boxes with the same label 'encoder f'

insights.structure: Two mirror columns rise from one input: the left holds encoder f plus a predictor h box, the right holds encoder f alone, and both lines converge at the top on a single 'similarity' word.
insights.data: Data are never drawn: the image and its two views are only italic labels (image x, x1, x2) at the column feet.
insights.emphasis: The predictor is the only orange box against two light-blue encoders, and stop-grad is a separate dashed arrow with an 'x' beside the right branch, so the two design choices are the only visual differences.
insights.flow: Reading runs bottom-to-top: the rounded split at the bottom forks into the columns, each goes straight up, and the tops bend inward with arrowheads pointing at 'similarity'.
insights.avoid: The stop-grad mark floats beside the right column instead of sitting on its output line, so which edge it cuts is inferred rather than shown.

figures.lesson: Show a Siamese method's asymmetry by keeping both branches identical except for one differently tinted extra box on one side and a crossed dashed arrow labelled 'stop-grad' beside the other side's output.

figures.title: SlowFast Networks for Video Recognition

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes (Slow on top, Fast below) separated by whitespace, each a row of input frame stack plus three cuboid stages; a single tall prediction bar spans both lanes at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: stacks of flat grey slanted parallelograms standing for frames (4 sparse vs ~15 dense), captioned 'Low frame rate' / 'High frame rate'
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; only the 'prediction' bar at the right end
arrangement.shared: the prediction head is one tall bar spanning both lanes, its gradient blending the two lane tints

insights.structure: Two unframed horizontal lanes, Slow on top and Fast below, each run frames -> three cuboid stages, and both converge into one tall prediction bar at the right edge.
insights.data: Frames are grey slanted parallelograms whose count (4 vs ~15) encodes frame rate, and feature tensors are 3-D cuboids whose width and depth encode C,T vs βC,αT, labelled in italics on their edges.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the contrast itself: blue wide cuboids vs green thin cuboids, with the prediction bar's blue-to-green gradient showing the two pathways merging.
insights.flow: Both lanes read left to right with straight black arrows, and after each stage a vertical arrow rises from the Fast lane into the Slow lane's horizontal arrow as a lateral connection.
insights.avoid: The axis glyph floats between the lanes with no frame, and the blocks have only faint radial tints so the blue/green coding nearly disappears in print.

figures.lesson: Show a two-rate design by drawing the same stages twice with shape-encoded dimensions (wide shallow cuboids vs thin deep ones, labelled C,T vs βC,αT) and joining them with vertical lateral arrows, so the ratio is visible without a table.

figures.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models

taxonomy.note: architecture: a per-channel scaling transform migrating difficulty between activations and weights, not a network

arrangement.units: two unboxed halves divided by a dashed rule, each a written matrix product
arrangement.inputs_as: tiny integer matrices X and W with real numbers
arrangement.shared: the same matrix layout and colour scale on both sides

insights.structure: Two halves split by a dashed vertical rule, 'Original:' at left and 'SmoothQuant:' at right, each writing out the product X * W with the actual matrices.
insights.data: Matrices are grids of integer cells on a grey-beige base, heat-tinted by magnitude (outlier -16 in purple-red, 8 and -9 orange), with per-channel abs-max vectors in dashed boxes beside each matrix (a row under X, a column right of W).
insights.emphasis: The heat tint makes the activation outlier jump out on the left and visibly flatten on the right, where the transform equations for X-hat, W-hat and s sit above and below.
insights.flow: Left half to right half; within a half, X then a star then W, with small 'Abs Max' arrows marking the reduction axis.

figures.lesson: Put each matrix's per-channel abs-max as a dashed-outline vector right beside it, tinted with the same heat colours as the cells, so the outlier channel and the way the transform spreads it between activation and weight are visible before and after.

figures.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

taxonomy.task: faster autoregressive decoding with a draft model
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a small draft model proposes tokens that the large model verifies; the figure draws only the resulting token trace

arrangement.units: nine unframed text lines, one per decoding iteration
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text: each line starts with a [START] token and the real sentence so far
arrangement.shared: the accepted prefix is repeated in black on every following line

insights.structure: Nine left-aligned lines stacked top to bottom, each one decoding iteration, with the new tokens always at the right end.
insights.data: Data is a real sentence in bold monospace, every token underlined by a tick-ended bracket that shows its boundaries.
insights.emphasis: Green accepted, red struck-through rejected and blue corrected tokens at each line's end carry the whole idea against the black accepted prefix.
insights.flow: Read each line to its coloured tail, then drop to the next line, which repeats the prefix in black and extends it.
insights.avoid: The colour code is explained only in the caption, with no in-figure legend, and repeating the full prefix on every line makes the figure dense.

figures.lesson: Explain a decoding algorithm with a real sentence growing line by line, colouring each step's new tokens by outcome and striking through rejected ones.

figures.title: SplitFed: When Federated Learning Meets Split Learning

arrangement.units: unenclosed clip-art icons with vertical name tags
arrangement.inputs_as: client icons in the centre column
arrangement.shared: two servers shared by all K clients

insights.structure: Two hubs with the clients between them: a Fed Server icon at far left, a column of Client 1, Client 2, ..., Client K in the middle, a Main Server cloud at right, and model-part thumbnails scattered at lower right.
insights.data: Parties are clip-art icons (server rack with sigma, binders plus person silhouettes, a cloud with a rack) each tagged by a dark-grey vertical label; model parts are small framed thumbnails of coloured vertical bars, one bar per layer.
insights.emphasis: Four arrow colours, each pair running opposite ways, distinguish the message types: blue client models up to the fed server, red global model back, green smashed activations to the main server, orange gradients back.
insights.flow: Paired straight thin arrows radiate from each client to both servers, with labels rotated to run along the arrows.
insights.avoid: The text-free arrows for Client 2 and the rotated labels make the four messages hard to read, and the model-part thumbnails float with no link to the parties they belong to; use a legend for arrow colours and attach model parts to their holders.

figures.lesson: With two kinds of server, put them on opposite sides of a client column and give each of the four message types its own arrow colour with the label written along the arrow, so who sends what to whom reads at a glance.

figures.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Physics-Guided Reconstruction Neural Networks without Fully-Sampled Reference Data

arrangement.units: lettered panels: blue-outlined pale-blue / pale-yellow boxes for iterations, grey-filled blue-outlined containers for the network detail
arrangement.inputs_as: the math symbol x^(0)
arrangement.shared: x^(0) feeds every DC block via one grey line

insights.structure: Three lettered panels: (a) one iteration as an R-above-DC loop in a pale-blue box at top left, (b) the unrolled chain of 1st to T-th iterations in pale-yellow boxes at top right, and (c) a full-width bottom row opening the regulariser as two grey containers, ResNet and Residual Block.
insights.data: R is a flat peach rectangle and DC a saturated green one, states x^(i), z^(i) are italic math labels on the arrows, and in (c) layers are thick 3-D perspective slabs (light-blue Conv, green RB, yellow ReLU, red xScale).
insights.emphasis: Repeating the same peach/green R and DC blocks from loop to unroll ties (a) and (b) together, and a grey line from x^(0) over the row into every DC shows the shared measurement input.
insights.flow: Left to right throughout; (a) closes a loop back to x^(i), (b) chains frames with an ellipsis, (c) has long skip lines under the slabs ending in blue circled + signs.
insights.avoid: Panel (c) shows a generic ResNet with no link line back to the R block it expands; draw a zoom connector from R to the ResNet container.

figures.lesson: Draw the iteration three ways in one figure - a single R/DC loop, the unrolled row of framed iterations, then the regulariser's layers as 3-D slabs - keeping R peach and DC green so both carry from the loop into the unrolled copies.

figures.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

taxonomy.task: streaming LLM inference with KV cache

arrangement.units: four unboxed columns under lettered serif titles
arrangement.inputs_as: token cells in the attention grid and cache row
arrangement.shared: identical grid and cache layout reused in every column

insights.structure: Four borderless columns, (a) Dense Attention, (b) Window Attention, (c) Sliding Window w/ Re-computation, (d) StreamingLLM (ours), each stacking an attention grid, a KV-cache row, a cost and PPL scorecard, and a one-line verdict.
insights.data: Each policy is the same lower-triangular grid of square cells: grey masked or evicted, light blue attended, dark-blue diagonal, red current token; below it a row of cache squares with dashed grey evicted ones and curved arrows from the current token.
insights.emphasis: The ours column adds a yellow first-column of 'attention sink' cells, and the scorecards use red crosses versus green ticks on O(.) cost and PPL so only (d) gets two ticks.
insights.flow: Left to right across the four alternatives; within a column top to bottom from grid to cache to verdict.

figures.lesson: Draw every KV-cache policy as the same lower-triangular attention grid (kept cells blue, evicted cells grey) over a matching cache row, and close each column with a cost-and-quality scorecard of green ticks and red crosses, so the proposal is simply the one column with two ticks.

figures.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks

insights.avoid: The baseline and the new design are drawn at different widths and the curved style arrows from one cloud cross the gap at varying angles, so the four 'A' paths look tangled.

figures.title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving

insights.flow: Verb-labelled black arrows: 'predict' left to right on top, 'generate' left to right below, 'supervise' upward on the right joining label to prediction.
insights.avoid: The class legend runs as a cramped single line along the bottom edge; give it more spacing or place swatches near the renders.

figures.lesson: Lay the task out as a 2x2 of real data: camera ring around a top-view ego car and the predicted voxel scene on top, the sparse LiDAR sweep and the dense label it generates below, joined by verb-labelled arrows (predict, generate, supervise) under one semantic colour legend.

figures.title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving

arrangement.units: four headed columns without frames; one black-framed detail panel; a dashed-grey legend box

insights.avoid: The camera pyramid of overlapping coloured slabs is visually busy and the fourth (finest) scale row has no matching 2D-to-3D block, so the row count does not line up across columns.

figures.lesson: Show the coarse-to-fine decoder as a column of cube volumes that grow scale by scale with HxWxZ size labels, each feeding a voxel render of the occupancy at that scale, so the multi-scale outputs read as a stack of increasingly detailed 3-D scenes.

figures.lesson: Draw the baseline and the proposed method on one identical skeleton side by side, so the new components appear as boxes inserted into the right copy, and reserve grey fill for the parts with learned weights.

figures.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

arrangement.shared: attention and Add+Normalize bars span both token columns; experts are per-token copies

figures.title: T2I-Adapter: Learning Adapters to Dig out More Controllable Ability for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

figures.title: Natural TTS Synthesis by Conditioning WaveNet on Mel Spectrogram Predictions
