insights.data: The series is a real-looking blue line split by blue dashed boxes into input patches (input_patch_len=32) and longer green solid output windows (output_patch_len=128), annotated in monospace below.
insights.emphasis: Yellow Token+PE boxes are the only saturated fill; long green dashed arrows run from each output token back down to the next, longer output window to show input-short/output-long patching.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each column; causal attention fan-in lines go from earlier tokens diagonally up to later SA ovals; green dashed diagonals cross the whole figure.
insights.avoid: The green dashed output arrows cut diagonally across every band and the causal attention lines, cluttering the centre.

figures.lesson: Overlay the patch windows directly on the drawn series (short dashed boxes for input patches, longer solid boxes for output patches) and run dashed arrows from each output token back down to the window it forecasts.

figures.title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?

arrangement.units: five unframed columns of identical frame stacks, each captioned underneath
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames tiled into patches
arrangement.shared: row labels frame t-delta / t / t+delta at the left apply to all columns

insights.structure: Five identical columns, one per attention scheme (Space, Joint Space-Time, Divided Space-Time, Sparse Local Global, Axial), each a vertical stack of three frames (t-delta, t, t+delta) cut into 4x4 patch grids.
insights.data: Frames are real video frames split into patches with white gutters; one query patch is blue and the patches it attends to are tinted with translucent colour overlays.
insights.emphasis: Colour encodes attention type and is echoed in the column caption letters (S red, T green, L yellow, G magenta, W/H), so each caption doubles as a legend.
insights.flow: Read column by column left to right comparing schemes; within a column top to bottom across time; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Overlapping translucent tints (red over patches, yellow over magenta) make some attended regions hard to tell apart, and the blue query patch is small.

figures.lesson: Explain attention variants with a grid of real frames: columns = variants, rows = three consecutive frames cut into patches, the query patch in blue and each attended set in a translucent tint whose colour matches the coloured letter in the column label.

figures.title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis

taxonomy.note: architecture = reshaping a 1D series into 2D tensors by period (multi-periodicity), shown conceptually

arrangement.units: unframed three-column progression (1D plot, per-period segments, 2D planes)
arrangement.inputs_as: a plotted 1D time series with period spans marked
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three columns left to right: a single value-time plot with three nested period spans, a middle column of three stacked series segmentations (Period 1/2/3), and right three slanted 2D planes of decreasing period length.
insights.data: Series are grey jagged line plots; same-phase time points are hollow circles joined by dashed lines; segments are tinted blue (interperiod) and red (intraperiod) bands; 2D tensors are drawn as skewed parallelograms holding short squiggles.
insights.emphasis: Two colours carry the whole idea: blue arrows for interperiod variation along rows and red arrows for intraperiod variation along columns, repeated on each 2D plane and in the bottom-left legend.
insights.flow: Long black dashed arrows fan from each period span on the left plot to its segmented copy in the middle, then hollow block arrows point right to the 2D plane.
insights.avoid: The middle column's overlapping, offset series copies with dashed connectors and circles are very busy and partly illegible.

figures.lesson: Explain a 1-D-to-2-D reshape by cutting the drawn series into period segments stacked as offset copies with same-phase points joined, and give the two resulting axes their own colours (blue across periods, red within) on both the curves and the final 2-D planes.

figures.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding

taxonomy.task: language model compression by knowledge distillation

arrangement.units: unframed two-row flow of cylinders and rounded boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: database cylinders for corpora
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two rows: top row Large-scale Text Corpus -> General TinyBERT -> Fine-tuned TinyBERT; bottom row Task Dataset -> Augmented Task Dataset, whose arrow rises into the second top-row arrow.
insights.data: Datasets are drawn as database cylinders and models as rounded rectangles, all black outline with no fill.
insights.emphasis: Only the three process names (General Distillation, Data Augmentation, Task-specific Distillation) are coloured, in red-pink, placed above their arrows so the two-stage method reads as labelled edges.
insights.flow: Left to right along each row; the bottom row joins the top with one vertical arrow into the task-specific distillation step.
insights.avoid: The teacher BERT is not drawn anywhere, so the distillation edges have no visible source model.

figures.lesson: Draw datasets as cylinders and model checkpoints as rounded boxes and name each distillation stage in red over its arrow, so the stages are the arrows and the boxes are only artefacts.

figures.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster

taxonomy.task: faster ViT inference by token merging

arrangement.units: three black-outlined rounded panels with tab titles (a) result strip, (b) block diagram, (c) algorithm steps; (c) is a zoom of the ToMe box in (b)
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo at the left of panel (a); x as a grey pill at the left of (b)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three rounded panels with tab labels: (a) a photo strip top-left, (b) a transformer block top-right with the new ToMe trapezoid between Attention and MLP, and (c) a full-width five-step strip below that a wedge from the ToMe box opens into.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as two columns of small circles (red Set A, blue Set B) with grey candidate edges and dark kept edges; merged tokens become overlapping circles that turn purple, while (a) shows the real dog photo with coloured patch outlines that coarsen from Patchfied to Block 32.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only light-blue trapezoid in panel (b), narrowing in the flow direction, and the zoom wedge from it makes the whole bottom panel its explanation; the title bolds 'To' and 'Me'.
insights.flow: Panels (a) and (b) read left to right on the top row, then the wedge drops the eye into (c), whose steps run left to right joined by black arrows, each with a bold 'Step N:' caption underneath.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) has no arrows or link to (b), so the reader must infer that the merging snapshots are produced by stacking the block in (b).

figures.lesson: Draw a token-reduction module as a trapezoid that narrows in the flow direction, then zoom it into a step strip where tokens are two-colour circles that visibly fuse into overlapping mixed-colour circles.

figures.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

taxonomy.task: self-supervised tool-use data generation for LMs
taxonomy.note: training 'other': self-supervised filtering of API calls by LM loss reduction, then finetuning on the augmented dataset

arrangement.units: one row of pipeline boxes; the three processing steps are grouped on a grey background band, each step heading a column of example text
arrangement.inputs_as: a dataset box plus quoted example text beneath it
arrangement.losses_at: filter criterion written as inequalities under step 3
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One row of five rounded boxes, mauve 'LM Dataset' at each end and three numbered light-blue steps (Sample, Execute, Filter API Calls) sitting together on a grey band that runs down to the figure bottom.
insights.data: Under every box a column continues one worked example: the Pittsburgh text spans x, two candidate calls c_i^1 and c_i^2 as questions, their results r_i, and the filter inequalities on tinted strips (green with '<' kept, pink with '>' dropped).
insights.emphasis: The kept/dropped decision is colour-coded green vs pink-red and carried into the output, where the inserted call '[QA(What ...? -> Steel City)]' appears in bold magenta inline in the sentence.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right: grey arrows from and to the dataset boxes, blue arrows between the steps; the example text is read top to bottom inside each column.
insights.avoid: The two candidate calls are tracked only by row position and superscripts; nothing marks that the dropped c_i^2 is discarded before the output column.

figures.lesson: Run one concrete example under each pipeline stage in aligned columns, and show the keep-or-drop decision by tinting the kept candidate green and the rejected one red, so the tool-call insertion can be read off the bottom row.

figures.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: Game of 24 reasoning with LM-generated and LM-evaluated thoughts

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal rows (a) generation and (b) evaluation, each prompt panel -> LM -> output panel, plus an unframed tree column at left
arrangement.inputs_as: the search tree with real arithmetic nodes; 'Input: 4 9 10 13' at its top
arrangement.shared: the LM box is drawn once per row

insights.structure: A search tree on the left feeds two stacked rows on the right, (a) Propose Prompt -> LM -> Thought Generation and (b) Value Prompt -> LM -> Thought Evaluation, with the same three-column alignment in both rows.
insights.data: Prompts and outputs are panels with a monospace title bar and real prompt text, italic grey placeholders ({one example}, {...more lines...}) for elided parts; tree nodes are bare arithmetic steps coloured green (kept) or red (dead end) with a small '(left: ...)' remainder.
insights.emphasis: Colour links context to module: a grey dashed box around the tree's first level and a grey arrow go to row (a), an orange dashed box around one node and an orange arrow go to row (b), whose title bars are cream-orange.
insights.flow: Left to right: tree -> thick coloured arrows -> prompt panel -> LM box -> output panel; the tree itself reads top to bottom.
insights.avoid: The tree's lower levels have no link back from Thought Evaluation, so how the value verdict prunes the tree is left to the colours alone.

figures.lesson: Tie each highlighted part of a search tree to the prompt row that produces or judges it with a matching coloured dashed box and arrow, so the tree and the prompt templates explain each other.

figures.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as One Big Sequence Modeling Problem

taxonomy.task: offline RL as sequence modelling of discretised trajectories

arrangement.units: one composition: input token row, model bar, output token row; no frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of coloured token tiles with math symbols
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (implied by shifted output row)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three horizontal bands: an input token row at the bottom, one full-width 'Trajectory Transformer' bar in the middle, and the output token row at the top shifted one slot left.
insights.data: Each token is a rounded tile holding a bold math symbol: blue for state dimensions s_t^i, salmon for action dimensions a_t^j, orange for reward r_t; runs are elided by three dots tinted in the run's colour.
insights.emphasis: The shift of the output row by one token makes next-token prediction visible without any text; colour families separate state, action and reward.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: short black arrows from each input tile up into the bar and from the bar up to each output tile.
insights.avoid: Arrows are drawn only in columns that hold a tile on that side, so a few columns look disconnected; there is no causal-mask cue.

figures.lesson: Autoregressive next-token prediction is shown by placing the same colour-coded token row below and above one wide model bar with the upper row shifted one slot left, so the offset reads without a label.

figures.title: TransBTS: Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation Using Transformer

taxonomy.task: 3D brain tumor segmentation from multimodal MRI

arrangement.units: one row encoder -> transformer panel (peach rounded tint) -> decoder; a grey rounded detail inset below
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real MRI slices
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single left-to-right row: green 3-D encoder blocks shrink from stacked MRI slices to a bottleneck, a peach panel holds the Transformer section, blue decoder blocks grow to the segmented slice; a grey inset below the bottleneck expands one Transformer Layer, with legends in both lower corners.
insights.data: Feature maps are extruded 3-D slabs labelled with tensor sizes such as (128, H/8, W/8, D/8); tokens are columns of grey circles; input and output are real MRI slices, the output with red/green/blue tumour overlays.
insights.emphasis: The Transformer bottleneck is the only peach-tinted region, set mid-row and expanded in the inset joined by dotted zoom lines.
insights.flow: Left to right along the row with green downsample and blue upsample arrows; three nested orange dashed skip arcs rise over the top to magenta dashed concatenation boxes on the decoder.
insights.avoid: The legend is split into two lower corners around the inset, so the reader looks in two places for symbol meanings.

figures.lesson: Put the novel bottleneck on its own tinted panel between the shrinking and growing 3-D blocks and drop its internal layer into a detail panel straight below, tied by dotted lines, so the hybrid's new part reads at both scales without interrupting the left-to-right flow.

figures.title: Attention Is All You Need

arrangement.units: two vertical lanes, encoder (left) and decoder (right); each holds a rounded light-grey frame around the repeated layer labelled 'Nx', with embeddings and positional encoding below the frame and (decoder only) Linear + Softmax above it
arrangement.inputs_as: plain words 'Inputs' and 'Outputs (shifted right)' under the two Embedding boxes
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the decoder ends in 'Output Probabilities' text above the Softmax box at the top right
arrangement.shared: the encoder output is one line that leaves the top of the encoder frame and drops into the decoder's second attention block; nothing is duplicated

insights.structure: Encoder and decoder stand as two upright grey-framed towers marked 'Nx', side by side, with the decoder taller by one extra attention sub-layer and topped by Linear and Softmax.
insights.data: Data appears only as words at the ends ('Inputs', 'Outputs (shifted right)', 'Output Probabilities'); no tensors or token cells are drawn, only the operations.
insights.emphasis: Pastel fills code block type (orange attention, blue feed-forward, yellow-green Add & Norm, pink embeddings), so the repeated attention blocks stand out in both towers without any extra highlight.
insights.flow: Both towers read bottom-to-top along a central spine; residual lines loop out the side of each sub-layer back into its Add & Norm bar, and one line crosses from the encoder top into the decoder's middle block.
insights.avoid: The encoder-to-decoder line enters the cross-attention block as three forked arrows that are hard to tell apart from the decoder's own residual line next to them, so which input is K/V versus Q is not readable from the drawing.

figures.lesson: Colour each block by its type (attention, feed-forward, norm, embedding) rather than by stage, so the same operation is recognisable wherever it repeats across two towers.

figures.title: TransFuse: Fusing Transformers and CNNs for Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: polyp and medical image segmentation fusing CNN and transformer

arrangement.units: two coloured rounded branch panels (Transformer orange, CNN green L-shape) with a shared fusion column and decoder between; dashed detail insets
arrangement.inputs_as: real endoscopy image tiles at top-left, real image at bottom-right
arrangement.losses_at: next to each predicted mask at three heads (left bottom, centre, top right)
arrangement.shared: BiFusion boxes in the middle take one input from each branch

insights.structure: Two branch panels face each other: an orange Transformer Branch on the left and a green L-shaped CNN Branch at lower right, with three BiFusion boxes in a central column between them and the attention-gated decoder climbing to the upper right.
insights.data: Features are pale 3-D cuboids labelled t^i, g^i, f^i with resolutions (H/16, W/16) on the arrows; inputs are a real endoscopy photo and its patch tiles; predictions are black-and-white masks next to loss terms L(G, head(.)).
insights.emphasis: The new BiFusion module gets the large pink dashed inset at top centre, joined by red dashed zoom lines to the f^0 box; each branch has its own colour family.
insights.flow: Branch outputs run horizontally into the central BiFusion column (transformer from the left, CNN from the right), then the decoder goes up and right through AG gates; colours of arrows encode operations per the legend.
insights.avoid: Insets fill every gap (transformer layer far left, BiFusion top, legend right) and the CNN panel is notched to let the decoder pass, so the layout feels packed and the eye has no single starting point.

figures.lesson: Operation type is carried by the colour of short thick block arrows rather than by extra boxes, and the legend sets each operation's name in its arrow's own colour, so the arrows read without matching swatches.

figures.title: TransFuser: Imitation with Transformer-Based Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving

taxonomy.task: end-to-end driving waypoint prediction from camera and LiDAR

arrangement.units: a large titled frame holding two grey-tinted branch lanes with four rungs between them; outside it, a waypoint-decoder row at bottom right and a dashed light-green detail panel at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: real sensor images: an RGB camera frame and a LiDAR BEV render, each with a two-line label above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the GRU chain ends in delta-w waypoint outputs
arrangement.shared: each fusion Transformer is drawn once between the bands with arrows to and from both branches

insights.structure: Two grey branch bands (image above, LiDAR BEV below) inside one titled frame are tied together by four green Transformer rungs at matching stages, and a separate waypoint decoder row and a dashed detail panel sit outside the frame on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are a wide dark RGB frame and a square black LiDAR BEV image at the left edge, each stage's feature map is a coloured cuboid with its exact C x H x W printed beside it, and the fused vectors are thin upright bars labelled 512 and 64.
insights.emphasis: Green is reserved for the fusion transformers and their zoomed detail panel (with an 'x L' repeat marker), so the contribution reads as the repeated element bridging two otherwise pastel branches.
insights.flow: Thin black lines run straight left to right along each band through circled-plus nodes, short vertical arrows go up and down between bands and rungs, the two branch outputs converge diagonally to one sum node, and the GRU chain steps right with green dashed arrows rising from a Goal Location bar.
insights.avoid: Lines are hairline-thin and the GRU/goal row plus the detail panel's token cubes are tiny relative to the frame, so the output stage and the attention mechanism are hard to read at column size.

figures.lesson: Draw two-sensor fusion as a ladder: two tinted branch bands with matching stage-by-stage feature cuboids, and the fusion module repeated as same-coloured rungs between them, one rung zoomed into a tinted detail panel in the corner.

figures.title: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries

taxonomy.note: modality: mesh / physical field data

arrangement.units: left: dashed layer box plus a solid zoom panel; right (after a dashed vertical rule): unframed data drawing of the same module
arrangement.inputs_as: a textured 3-D slab of the physical field
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Left third: a dashed pre-norm layer with a zoom into a black-framed block diagram of Physics-Attention (stacked frames for heads); a vertical dashed rule; right two-thirds: the same attention drawn again with the data.
insights.data: The input field is a 3-D slab with a flow-field texture, fanned by navy lines into a staircase of slabs weighted by slice weights, pooled into small blue token cubes, mixed by pink attention lines, then broadcast back to blue-gradient slabs and merged into an output slab; shapes labelled N x C, M x (N x C), M x C.
insights.emphasis: Physics-Attention is the only pink box in the layer and its token step is dark-red text in both the block diagram and the data drawing, tying the two views together.
insights.flow: The left layer reads bottom to top; the right half reads left to right Slice -> Attention for Tokens -> DeSlice, with a brown arc for slice weights over the top.
insights.avoid: The right half's many crossing navy and pink lines make individual slices hard to trace; a lighter or fewer-slice version would read faster.

figures.lesson: Explain the new operator twice side by side — a small block diagram zoomed from its box, then the same steps drawn on the physical field itself (field slab split into weighted copies, pooled into a few token cubes, broadcast back) — and give the shared step the same text colour in both.

figures.title: TransUNet: Transformers Make Strong Encoders for Medical Image Segmentation

arrangement.units: (b) the main architecture with sub-groups (lilac CNN frame, green transformer frame, dashed concatenation squares); (a) a cream rounded detail inset at the far left, linked by dashed zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: a real CT slice above the CNN encoder
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the decoder ends at a segmentation head arrow into a coloured-mask CT slice at top-right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A tall cream inset (a) on the far left expands the transformer layer, while panel (b) runs the CNN (lilac frame) down into the green-framed transformer stack and a diagonal decoder staircase rises to the upper right.
insights.data: The input CT slice sits above the CNN and the coloured-mask CT output at the top-right, with features drawn as translucent 3-D cuboids carrying bold (C, H/k, W/k) shape labels.
insights.emphasis: The transformer stack is the only container with a saturated green outline and the only one opened into a detail panel via grey dashed zoom lines.
insights.flow: Read top-down through the CNN and transformer, rightward along the reshaped bottleneck, then up the decoder staircase via green upsample arrows, with dotted skip curves (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) dropping in from the CNN.
insights.avoid: The dotted skip curves run long diagonal paths across empty space and are labelled only by scale, so which concatenation box each one feeds is hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Tint encoder cubes and decoder cubes differently and draw each skip concatenation as a dashed box holding one cube of each tint, so every merge shows both of its sources without extra labels.

figures.title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation

arrangement.units: left model column (dashed rounded container) and right unframed frame grid; rows separated only by prompt lines
arrangement.inputs_as: source video frames with its quoted prompt
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A narrow left column (orange Tune-A-Video box with flame icon, plus sign, dashed container of three blue bow-tie 'Pretrained T2I' models) beside a wide grid of five rows of six frames.
insights.data: Video is shown as rows of real frames with white gutters; prompts are handwritten italic lines between rows with edited words in blue; one row adds black pose-skeleton thumbnails.
insights.emphasis: The method is the single orange box; edited prompt words in blue point at what changed between source and output rows.
insights.flow: Top to bottom: the source clip on top with down arrows under each frame, then each prompt line introduces the generated row below it.

figures.lesson: In a video-editing teaser, put the source clip as the top row of frames with small down-arrows to the edited rows below, and introduce each edited row with its prompt written between the rows with only the changed words coloured.

figures.title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation

taxonomy.task: one-shot tuning of T2I diffusion for text-to-video

arrangement.units: two unframed sections Fine-Tuning and Inference, separated by a vertical rule, each with a large title
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a quoted prompt below
arrangement.losses_at: reconstruction loss as a line arching over the top of the fine-tuning section
arrangement.shared: the same video drawn as input in both sections

insights.structure: Two sections split by a thin vertical rule, titled 'Fine-Tuning' (wide, left) and 'Inference' (narrow, right); the fine-tuning U-Net container has a blue strip zooming one attention column into ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN, T-Attn.
insights.data: Every video is an offset stack of about six frames (real ski photos or grey noise); the prompt is a handwritten quote; Q and KV projections are small split squares, orange when updated, grey when frozen.
insights.emphasis: Orange 'Updated' vs grey 'Frozen' fill marks exactly which projections are tuned; the edited prompt words are blue in the inference half.
insights.flow: Fine-tuning reads left to right video -> diffusion -> noise -> U-Net -> video, with a 'Reconstruction Loss' line arching over the top; inference is a clockwise loop DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising -> edited video.
insights.avoid: The prompt line in Fine-Tuning runs along the bottom and up into Cross-Attn through the zoomed inset, a long route that is easy to miss.

figures.lesson: Draw every video tensor - clean, noised, edited - as the same offset stack of frames so the noise and editing stages read as changes to one clip, and mark which projections are trained inside the zoomed attention blocks with an orange/grey Q|KV split keyed by a short legend.

figures.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions: one U-shaped composition, levels separated only by vertical position
arrangement.inputs_as: a text label 'input image tile' beside the first one-channel bar
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the right arm ends in a text label 'output segmentation map'
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The contracting path descends the left side and the expanding path climbs the right side, with each resolution level drawn at its own height so the two arms mirror each other across an open gap.
insights.data: Feature maps are flat blue bars sized by channels (width) and resolution (height), labelled with channel counts above and rotated spatial sizes beside, and copied encoder maps appear as white bars joined to the decoder's blue ones.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is accented; the U silhouette and the four long grey copy-and-crop arrows spanning its gap carry the idea on their own.
insights.flow: Read down the left arm (dark red pool arrows), across the bottom, up the right arm (green up-conv arrows), with short navy conv arrows stepping left-to-right inside each level and grey skips running straight across.
insights.avoid: Input and output are plain text labels ('input image tile', 'output segmentation map') rather than a picture of the data, and the many small rotated size labels are hard to read at print size.

figures.lesson: Let vertical position encode resolution and bar width encode channel count, so the descending and ascending arms and the skip bridges between equal heights read as the architecture without a single container.

figures.title: All are Worth Words: A ViT Backbone for Diffusion Models

arrangement.units: one vertical stack plus a right column (legend and block detail) behind a dashed rule
arrangement.inputs_as: tokens t, c and real noisy image patches in a dashed box; tiled x_t photo at lower right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One vertical stack: input tokens, Embedding Layer, five peach Transformer Blocks, Linear, output patches, Rearrange, Conv3x3, Predicted noise; a dashed vertical rule sets off a right column with the legend and Transformer Block internals.
insights.data: Inputs t, c and image patches are a row of small squares in a dashed box captioned 'All as words', with the noisy x_t as a 3x3 tiled photo; outputs are noise patches and a noise image; embedded tokens are numbered tiles.
insights.emphasis: The long skip connections are thick black nested elbows on the stack's right, merging at circled-C nodes, which carries the U-Net idea inside a plain ViT.
insights.flow: Bottom to top along the stack; the skips loop from lower blocks up the right side into upper blocks.

figures.lesson: Each input's tint (grey time, yellow condition, blue patches) continues from its input tile into a matching segment of the shared Embedding Layer bar and onto its embedded token, so which slots belong to which input can be traced without labels.

figures.title: Uformer: A General U-Shaped Transformer for Image Restoration

arrangement.units: three unframed panels (a) overview, (b) block detail in a grey dashed container, (c) modulator detail, separated by dashed vertical rules
arrangement.inputs_as: text label 'Degraded Image'
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three panels in a row separated by black dashed rules and labelled (a)-(c) underneath: (a) the U-shaped overview takes about 60% of the width, (b) the LeWin block internals, (c) how a modulator is added per window.
insights.data: No tensors drawn: shapes like 2C x H/2 x W/2 are light grey-blue text above each encoder column; in (c) a feature map is a 2x2 tinted grid whose quadrant tints repeat on the per-window squares.
insights.emphasis: The new Modulators sit in a labelled dashed box in the bottom-right of (a) as coloured squares, matching the blue Modulator square in (c).
insights.flow: (a) runs left to right along the top encoder row, down to the bottleneck at the right, and back right to left along the bottom decoder row, with vertical skip arrows between partners; (b) and (c) read bottom to top.
insights.avoid: Modulator lines in (a) run back under the whole decoder row to each block, adding long lines that cross the bottom of the panel.

figures.lesson: Fold the U on its side - encoder along the top row, decoder returning along the bottom row, bottleneck dropped at the right end - so input and output share the left edge, every skip is a short vertical arrow, and the freed bottom-right corner holds the new component (a dashed 'Modulators' box) wired into each decoder block from below.

figures.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation via CLIP image embeddings
taxonomy.note: the prior is drawn in two variants (autoregressive, diffusion); diffusion decoder

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes separated by a dotted rule: CLIP training (top) and prior + decoder generation (bottom)
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in large blue type at the far left
arrangement.losses_at: the 'CLIP objective' as a double-headed arrow between the text and image embeddings in the top lane; no loss drawn for prior or decoder
arrangement.shared: one text encoder on the left whose output embedding is split by a bracket into both lanes

insights.structure: Two lanes split by a stepped dotted rule, CLIP training above and generation below, with the text encoder trapezoid on the left spanning both and a bracket fanning its embedding into each lane.
insights.data: The input is a quoted prompt in large blue text, embeddings are vertical columns of shaded cells coloured by modality (blue text, brown image), and outputs are real generated corgi images at the right edge of each lane.
insights.emphasis: The prior's two variants are stacked grey boxes with miniature attention-arc and diffusion-circle diagrams, and the cell colour switching from blue to brown across them shows the text-to-image embedding mapping.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right in both lanes: prompt -> text encoder -> embedding -> (CLIP objective | prior -> decoder) -> image.
insights.avoid: The dotted divider bends diagonally under the text encoder and the two halves have no titles, so a reader must rely on the caption to know the top lane is training-only.

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the target clip at the far right stands in for the reconstruction target
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One container-free left-to-right row: stacked input frames, a wireframe 3-D masking volume, a small column of visible photo-faced token cubes, a green Encoder pill, a column of green latent cubes interleaved with grey mask cubes, a blue Decoder pill, blue output cubes and the stacked target frames.
insights.data: Video clips are offset stacks of four photo frames with a 'Time' arrow above each, and tokens are small 3-D cubes whose face colour encodes state: photo patch (visible), translucent green (encoded), grey (masked), light blue (decoded).
insights.emphasis: The high masking ratio is shown by counts, not a highlight: the masking volume is mostly grey cells with a translucent blue tube through time, and the decoder input column is mostly grey cubes with few green ones.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with short black arrows between stages; captions sit under each stage and a two-swatch keeping/masking legend sits below the masking volume.
insights.avoid: The red-tinted cells in the masking volume are never explained in the legend, and the encoder/decoder pills carry no internal detail or loss marker, so the reconstruction target is only implied by position.

figures.lesson: Put a small 'Time' arrow over every frame stack and draw tokens as small 3-D cubes whose colour tracks their state (visible, encoded, masked, decoded), so the masking ratio is visible in the token counts on either side of the encoder.

figures.title: ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks

taxonomy.task: vision-language pretraining with two co-attention streams

arrangement.units: two rows (visual on top, linguistic below) with no band or frame; the shared repeated block is one dashed rectangle spanning both rows, and a second dashed rectangle wraps the text-only layers
arrangement.inputs_as: a bracketed row of real image-region photos with and a bracketed row of words with /, each labelled v_i / w_i
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (outputs h_v and h_w in brackets at the right)
arrangement.shared: the co-attention block is one dashed rectangle spanning both rows, with curved arrows crossing between them

insights.structure: Two streams run as parallel rows (visual above, text below) and are tied together only by a dashed 'k x' rectangle spanning both rows that holds the Co-TRM and TRM layers.
insights.data: Image regions are real photo crops in a bracketed row labelled v0..vT and text is a bracketed monospace sentence labelled w0..wT; outputs are bracketed h vectors at the right.
insights.emphasis: Co-TRM boxes have a green-to-purple gradient fill, the only bi-coloured shapes, and are where the two curved crossing arrows land.
insights.flow: Both rows read left to right; the only non-horizontal lines are two curved arrows that cross in an X into the opposite stream's Co-TRM.
insights.avoid: The cross-stream arrows start from the Embed and TRM boxes before the block rather than inside it, so the exact exchange (keys/values) is not visible and needs the separate detail figure.

figures.lesson: Mark a module that mixes two colour-coded streams with a gradient of both stream colours, and let the cross-stream arrows appear only at that module.

figures.title: ViLT: Vision-and-Language Transformer Without Convolution or Region Supervision

arrangement.units: one shared encoder bar with unboxed embedding pills below and small boxed heads above
arrangement.inputs_as: caption words as text on the left and photo patches on the right
arrangement.shared: the transformer encoder spans both modalities

insights.structure: A single wide orange 'Transformer Encoder' bar spans the figure; under it the text half (Word Embedding) and image half (Linear Projection of Flattened Patches) sit side by side, and above it three pretraining heads (Image Text Matching, Masked Language Modeling, Word Patch Alignment) sit in a row.
insights.data: Each input token is drawn as a triple of rounded pills (grey modal-type id, teal or lilac position id, embedding), the caption words are printed as plain text with a [MASK] token, and image patches are real photo tiles cut from the photo at the bottom right.
insights.emphasis: The single shared encoder is the largest and only saturated block, making the 'one stream, no heavy visual embedder' claim visible; heads' outputs ('True', 'office') appear in dashed boxes as example predictions.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: raw words and patches up through embeddings into the encoder, then up into the heads; the image enters from the right via a leftward arrow from the full photo to its patch row.
insights.avoid: The WPA head's OT block is fed by small z^D tokens tapped from comb-shaped brackets that are hard to read, and the legend on the right takes a full column for four tiny pill types.

figures.lesson: Each token is drawn as a triplet of touching pills (modal-type id, position index, content), so the embedding sum is shown by adjacency and a short legend instead of plus signs.

figures.title: VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts

arrangement.units: two vertical columns, each named by a coloured footer bar; token strips enclosed in pale yellow rounded panels
arrangement.inputs_as: multimodal prompt (text plus object images) at bottom left; tabletop observation renders at bottom right
arrangement.shared: the object encoder is repeated per timestep

insights.structure: Two columns with labelled footers: a narrow left 'Multimodal Prompt' column (prompt box, frozen T5 trapezoid, Prompt Tokens strip) and a wide right 'Interaction' column (three Object Encoder blocks over tabletop renders, a History Tokens strip, alternating Cross-Attention and Self-Attention bars, action outputs a1 a2 a3).
insights.data: The prompt mixes word bubbles with object images; tokens are small coloured squares (orange text, lilac object, mint action) per a top-left legend, and each timestep's observation is a rendered tabletop with dashed boxes around detected objects whose crops feed the encoder.
insights.emphasis: The cross-attention bars are the most saturated red, and yellow lines from the prompt token strip run across into each cross-attention layer, making prompt conditioning the visible link between columns.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in both columns; the prompt branch then crosses rightward into the decoder via yellow elbow arrows, and actions exit at the top while also reappearing as mint tokens in the history strip.
insights.avoid: Light grey arrows from object crops to encoders and from the history strip are faint and tangle near the scene images.

figures.lesson: Feedback of past actions into the input is drawn without a loop-back arrow: mint action tiles labelled a_1, a_2 are interleaved in the History Tokens row, the same colour and labels as the output actions along the top.

figures.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

arrangement.units: An overview panel on the left and a module-detail panel on the right, separated by a dashed vertical rule and each titled at its top; the detail holds the encoder block inside a grey rounded 'L x' container.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo split into a 3x3 patch grid at the bottom left, unrolled into a row of patch thumbnails
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (the class output pill sits at the top left)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The overview runs up from a patch row through a wide pink projection bar, a token row and a wide grey 'Transformer Encoder' bar to an MLP head, while a dashed rule sets off a right panel that expands the encoder as a grey 'L x' column.
insights.data: The input photo appears twice, as a 3x3 patch grid and as a row of nine patch thumbnails; tokens are paired pills (numbered purple position + pink patch) and the output is an orange rounded pill listing class names.
insights.emphasis: Role colours repeat across both panels (pink embedding, grey encoder, orange head), so the right panel's 'Embedded Patches' box and grey container are read as zooms of the left panel.
insights.flow: Left to right along the bottom (grid to patch row), then upward through vertical arrows into the encoder, then the head's arrow turns left to the class pill; the detail panel reads bottom to top with residual lines looping up the right side.
insights.avoid: The class token is explained by a floating asterisk footnote at the far left ('* Extra learnable [class] embedding'), separated from the '0*' pill it describes; label it next to the token instead.

figures.lesson: Unroll the input image into a numbered row of patch thumbnails directly under the token row, so 'image as a sequence of words' is shown rather than stated.

figures.title: ViViT: A Video Vision Transformer

arrangement.units: one main pipeline panel plus three rounded variant panels separated by dashed vertical rules
arrangement.inputs_as: stacked film-strip video frames
arrangement.shared: the token row 1..N is repeated under each variant

insights.structure: Left half is the full model (film-strip frames, grey 'Embed to tokens' block, token pills, a red-bordered Transformer Encoder with a green Self-Attention sub-box, orange MLP head); right half is three dashed-separated mini-panels comparing factorised variants (Factorised Encoder, Self-Attention, Dot-Product).
insights.data: Input is three stacked penguin frames styled as film strips; tokens are green index pills over peach embedding pills, and variant blocks are hatched purple (Spatial) and yellow (Temporal) rectangles.
insights.emphasis: Colour-matched titles: the encoder border is red and so is the 'Factorised Encoder' title, the self-attention box is green like 'Factorised Self-Attention', and the attention block blue like 'Factorised Dot-Product', tying each variant to the part it changes.
insights.flow: Left to right into the encoder, bottom to top inside it and to the class head; each variant panel reads bottom (tokens 1..N) to top.
insights.avoid: The three variant panels are tall and mostly empty with tiny text, so the comparison costs half the width for little content.

figures.lesson: Put the overview on the left and its design variants as equal panels on the right, colouring each variant's title to match the outline of the container it replaces in the overview, and give spatial and temporal blocks two different hatched tints so their order inside each variant is legible.

figures.title: Learning a Variational Network for Reconstruction of Accelerated MRI Data

arrangement.units: two captioned sub-figures stacked vertically; (b) contains a zoom box drawn as a rectangle linked by trapezoid lines
arrangement.inputs_as: coil sensitivity maps and multi-coil k-space shown as image stacks
arrangement.shared: the GD block is repeated T times with shared structure

insights.structure: Two stacked sub-figures: (a) a pipeline where sensitivity maps and k-space data feed an A* block to give a zero-filled image, and all three enter a tall green 'Variational Network (VN)' block that outputs the reconstruction; (b) a chain GD^1...GD^t...GD^T with GD^t zoomed via trapezoid lines into a pale-green box showing the gradient step.
insights.data: Inputs are real grey-scale coil sensitivity maps and k-space stacks with dimension labels (n_FE, n_PE, n_CH), images are knee MRIs; inside the zoom, learned filters are small grey patch pairs (RE/IM) and activation functions are blue curve plots.
insights.emphasis: All learned blocks share one dark green fill with white text, and the zoom-in from GD^t is the only enlarged region, putting the unrolled gradient step in focus.
insights.flow: Left to right in both parts; in (b) a data-consistency term lambda^t A*(Au^t - f) runs along the top and the filter-activation-filter branches run below, joining at summation circles with +/- signs.
insights.avoid: Part (a) uses a lot of whitespace and long elbow wires for a simple input routing; the sign labels at the summation nodes are small and crowd the arrows.

figures.lesson: Coil data are drawn as decks of offset stacked slices with their array dimensions (n_FE, n_PE, n_CH) printed along the edges, so the multi-coil axis needs no legend.

figures.title: Voicebox: Text-Guided Multilingual Universal Speech Generation at Scale

taxonomy.note: figure shows task formats, not the network; Voicebox is a flow-matching infilling model trained on masked speech (architecture/training not drawn)

arrangement.units: cells of a task-by-stage grid separated by dashed rules, no boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: spectrograms with quoted transcripts
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A 3 x 3 grid: columns are tasks (Denoising, Zero-shot TTS, Text-Only Sampling) with underlined bold headers, rows are Raw data / Model Input / Model Output separated by grey dashed horizontal rules.
insights.data: Audio is drawn as purple-orange spectrogram strips, masked spans as solid yellow-orange blocks, and transcripts as quoted capital text, with content text in red and style/reference text in blue.
insights.emphasis: Coloured outlines label roles: a grey 'noise' box on the noisy segment, blue 'Ref' boxes around the reference audio, and a red 'Target' box around the generated segment, matching the red/blue text colours.
insights.flow: Top to bottom within each column (raw -> input -> output), with no arrows; columns are read independently left to right.
insights.avoid: There are no arrows or model block at all, so the figure explains the input/output format but not how the model works; it should not be reused as a method overview.

figures.lesson: Explain an in-context generative model with a tasks x (raw data, model input, model output) grid of spectrograms, showing masking as a flat solid block and colouring each text snippet like the box around the audio it controls.

figures.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

arrangement.units: three vertical columns each topped by a coloured header pill; only the skill library is enclosed in a yellow panel
arrangement.inputs_as: curriculum of task screenshots
arrangement.shared: the Minecraft environment and self-verification sit centrally under the prompting column and connect to all three

insights.structure: Three titled columns with coloured header pills: Automatic Curriculum (purple, a cycle of circular game screenshots), Iterative Prompting Mechanism (blue, a code panel above a Minecraft screenshot and a magnifier 'Self-Verification' icon), and Skill Library (yellow, a list of item icons with skill names).
insights.data: Tasks are circular Minecraft screenshots, the program is a real JavaScript snippet in a grey code panel with item icons pinned to called functions, and skills are pixel-art item icons beside names.
insights.emphasis: Arrow and text colours match the module they belong to: purple 'New Task' and 'Update Exploration Progress', blue 'Skill Retrieval', red 'Refine Program' with an X, green 'Add New Skill' with a check.
insights.flow: Curriculum feeds a new task rightward into the code panel, the library feeds skills leftward into it, code goes down to the environment and feedback up, and self-verification branches up (refine) or right to the library (add).
insights.avoid: The long thin coloured arrows along the bottom are faint and cross under icons, and skill names in the library change colour (blue/green/black) with no legend.

figures.lesson: Give each agent component its own pastel heading bar and draw its arrows in a darker shade of that hue, then show the real artefacts in place (task screenshots on an arc, the generated code listing, an icon-per-row skill list) with a check or cross deciding which arrow fires.

figures.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

arrangement.units: two horizontal rows divided by a dashed rule, each a chain of unenclosed panels and pills ending in a yellow list panel
arrangement.inputs_as: generated program code (top) and a task question (bottom)
arrangement.shared: GPT-3.5 and Embedding pills repeated in both rows at the same x positions

insights.structure: Two rows separated by a dashed rule: top row 'add' (program -> GPT-3.5 -> description -> Embedding -> Key, program -> Value, both into the yellow Skill Library), bottom row 'retrieve' (task question -> GPT-3.5 -> plan text with environment feedback -> Embedding -> Query -> Skill Library -> Top-5 Relevant Skills).
insights.data: Programs and descriptions are real code panels (description shown as an italic comment), the task is a pink quoted question, model calls are small dark green (GPT-3.5) and black (Embedding) pills, skills are icon lists.
insights.emphasis: The newly added skill 'Combat Zombie' is green in the library to match the green 'Add' arrow, and retrieved skills are blue to match the blue 'Retrieve' arrow.
insights.flow: Both rows run left to right with the same column positions, so the two operations align vertically (GPT-3.5 over GPT-3.5, Embedding over Embedding).
insights.avoid: The Value arrow is a long thin line running the full width under the description panel, and the skill library is drawn twice (as a panel and as a small yellow box) which may read as two different stores.

figures.lesson: Draw writing to and reading from an agent memory as two stacked rows that share the same stages and the same store panel, colouring the write path green and the read path blue down to the text of the added and retrieved entries.

figures.title: Vector Quantized Diffusion Model for Text-to-Image Synthesis

arrangement.units: two rounded grey-bordered panels stacked vertically, each titled with its step; the decoder is a nested blue panel with inner rounded block pairs
arrangement.inputs_as: a photo (step 1) and a quoted caption (step 2)
arrangement.shared: the codebook token indices link the two steps

insights.structure: Two stacked rounded panels titled 'Step1: VQ-VAE' (photo -> trapezoid Encoder -> Q(.) with a lilac Codebook z1..zK above -> green token grid -> Decoder -> photo) and 'Step2: VQ-Diffusion' (a chain of green token-state circles x_T ... x_t, x_{t-1} ... x_0 above a blue 'Diffusion Image Decoder' box of AdaLN + Transformer Block pairs).
insights.data: Discrete latents are green number grids and number strips with 'M' for masked tokens, shown above each diffusion state; the text prompt is a quoted sentence going through BPE and a peach trapezoid Text Encoder.
insights.emphasis: The token strips over x_T to x_0 show masks being replaced by indices step by step, and the forward q and reverse p_theta transitions are labelled with their equations on dashed and solid arcs.
insights.flow: Step 1 runs left to right; in Step 2 the state chain runs left to right on top, while the decoder below takes x_t, t and the text embedding and loops its output back up to x_{t-1}.
insights.avoid: Many thin grey feedback lines inside the decoder box (t and text embeddings to every block) crowd the lower panel.

figures.lesson: One green token motif carries the discrete latent through the whole figure - a 2-D index grid after quantization, then 1-D index strips with grey 'M' mask cells above each Markov-chain state - so the reader sees corruption go from all-masked x_T to fully filled x_0 without reading a formula.

figures.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

arrangement.units: one large rounded VQGAN panel at the bottom plus two rounded side panels (Codebook, Transformer) above it
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo with patch callouts
arrangement.shared: the codebook is shared between VQGAN quantization and the transformer

insights.structure: A large rounded 'VQGAN' panel spans the bottom (photo -> CNN Encoder E -> 3-D latent grid z-hat -> quantization -> coloured index cube z_q -> CNN Decoder G -> photo), a dashed CNN Discriminator D rises from it to a real/fake grid, and above sit a Codebook Z table and a Transformer panel.
insights.data: Latents are 3-D cubes, the quantised one with coloured cells carrying codebook indices; the codebook is a table of coloured rows linked by yellow/blue lines to image patches on the large photo; the transformer shows a coloured index sequence with a '?' next token and a bar-chart distribution.
insights.emphasis: Index colours are shared across the codebook, z_q cells and the transformer sequence, so one colour = one code throughout; the generator and discriminator use dashed trapezoid outlines in one teal.
insights.flow: Bottom row left to right, with a dashed double arrow from the argmin quantization up to the codebook and a two-way arrow pair between codebook and transformer; the discriminator flows upward to its patch output.
insights.avoid: The big top-left dog photo with patch call-outs duplicates the small input photo and pushes the encoder input into a cramped corner.

figures.lesson: Every discrete code keeps one colour and one integer wherever it appears (image-patch zoom box, codebook row, quantized-cube cell, transformer token), so the hand-off from the autoencoder stage to the sequence-model stage reads without a legend.

figures.title: VS-Net: Variable splitting network for accelerated parallel MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: Identical dashed-outline stage frames in a row, each titled 'Stage k' above; the last is separated by a bold dotted ellipsis.
arrangement.inputs_as: real grayscale MR images: the zero-filled input above, then stacks of undersampled k-space images, coil sensitivity maps and line masks down the left edge
arrangement.shared: auxiliary inputs are drawn once at the left and fan into every stage through long horizontal bus lines, one line style per input (solid, dotted, dashed)

insights.structure: A row of identical dashed stage frames, each with DB and DCB stacked on its left feeding WAB on its right, sits above a band of long bus lines that carry the shared inputs.
insights.data: Input and output are real grayscale knee MR images at the top corners, and the auxiliary inputs (undersampled k-space, coil sensitivities, mask) are offset stacks of small images labelled above, stacked down the left edge.
insights.emphasis: Block types are coded only by grey level (white DB, dark grey DCB with white text, light grey WAB), repeated identically in every stage, so the unrolled structure itself is the message.
insights.flow: The main path runs left to right across the top through the stages, while each auxiliary input runs right along its own line style (solid k-space, dotted sensitivities, dashed mask) and turns up with an arrowhead into the DCB and WAB of every stage.
insights.avoid: Three auxiliary line styles are told apart only by dash pattern with no legend, and they cross each other where they turn up into the stages, making the bus band dense and hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Draw an unrolled network as identical dashed stage frames with fixed grey levels per block type, and route each auxiliary input (k-space, sensitivities, mask) as its own line style along a bus under the stages so it can reach every stage without crossing the main flow.

figures.title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models

taxonomy.note: no network drawn; worked numeric example of a pruning metric on a weight matrix

arrangement.units: two unboxed panels separated by a vertical rule, each a row of three captioned matrices
arrangement.inputs_as: weight matrix with numeric entries (plus activation-norm row for Wanda)
arrangement.shared: same weight matrix values in both panels

insights.structure: Two side-by-side panels split by a grey vertical rule: 'Magnitude Pruning' (Weights -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights) and 'Wanda' (Weights plus an activation-norm row -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights), each a three-step left-to-right chain of 3 x 4 matrices.
insights.data: Matrices are grids of real small integers with cells coloured yellow (kept) or light blue (pruned/zero); activation norms ||X||_2 are a row of orange-shaded cells whose depth scales with value; the scoring formula S sits above each importance matrix.
insights.emphasis: Dashed boxes show the comparison group: one box around the whole matrix ('grouped per layer') for magnitude pruning versus one dashed box per row ('grouped per output') for Wanda, and the darkest orange activation (8) visibly flips which weights survive.
insights.flow: Left to right with small grey arrows inside each panel; the two panels are read in parallel as baseline versus proposed.

figures.lesson: Use a tiny integer-valued weight matrix with cells tinted kept versus pruned, and draw the comparison group as dashed boxes (whole matrix versus one per row), so a reader can check each pruning decision by reading the numbers.

figures.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

arrangement.units: one unframed stack of horizontal tiers (waveform, CNN, latents with quantizers, Transformer band, context outputs), named by a left margin column of labels
arrangement.inputs_as: a real raw audio waveform drawn as a dense black trace across the full width
arrangement.losses_at: top: a single loss symbol L above the context row, reached by curved arrows from the quantizer circles and from the masked context square
arrangement.shared: the CNN is drawn as five identical overlapping triangles, one per time step

insights.structure: Five horizontal tiers stacked bottom to top (waveform, CNN triangles, latents plus quantizers, Transformer band, context squares), each named in a left label column with its math symbol.
insights.data: The input is a real dense waveform trace, latent and context vectors are small blue squares per time step, quantized targets are green 'q' circles, and the masked position's output is the one grey square.
insights.emphasis: The loss is pulled out to the top as one italic L that curved arrows converge on, and the wide yellow Transformer band is the only warm colour in the figure.
insights.flow: Straight short arrows run upward through each tier, while long curved arrows sweep from the green q circles over the Transformer to the loss at top, making the target path visibly bypass the context network.
insights.avoid: The curved loss arrows cross the Transformer band and each other, so which q pairs with which context output is hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Label each horizontal tier once in a left margin column with its name and math symbol (X, Z, Q, C) so the drawing itself can stay free of text and the reader matches tiers to the paper's notation.

figures.title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
figures.venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing

arrangement.units: one grey rounded container around the CNN and transformer blocks
arrangement.inputs_as: waveform thumbnail with an overlapped green segment
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single grey rounded container holds two stacked orange blocks, a thin 'CNN Encoders' bar and a large 'Transformer Encoder with Gated Relative Position Bias' block, with a row of frame tokens between them; target tokens z1..z6 sit above the container and a green 'Mask Prediction Loss' pill on top.
insights.data: The input is a blue waveform with a green overlapped segment (simulated interfering speech); frame features are blue x_i boxes and masked ones are brown [M] boxes; targets are grey z_i boxes.
insights.emphasis: Red dashed lines from z2, z3, z4 converge on the loss pill, showing loss only on masked positions, and the green-overlaid waveform shows the denoising input without a separate label.
insights.flow: Strictly bottom to top with vertical black arrows: waveform -> CNN -> tokens (masked) -> transformer -> outputs -> loss.
insights.avoid: The overlapped-speech augmentation, the key difference from HuBERT, is only a green tint on the waveform with no label, so readers can miss it.

figures.lesson: Masked positions are shown by absence as well as by colour: the CNN sends no arrow into the [M] slots, and only those columns get the red dashed curves into the loss, so the training objective reads from the drawing without a text label.

figures.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision

taxonomy.task: multitask multilingual speech recognition and translation

arrangement.units: top-left: grey rounded panel of data examples; top-right: unboxed model area with teal/red block stacks grouped by curly braces; bottom: full-width grey rounded panel that zooms into the decoder input strip
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example sentences with speaker/notepad icons in a panel, feeding a log-Mel spectrogram raster via a hollow block arrow
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a 'next-token prediction' label on the arrow out of the decoder top
arrangement.shared: token-type colour code (orange/blue/green) reused across the model's token strips and the format panel

insights.structure: Three zones: a tall grey rounded data panel at top-left, an unboxed encoder/decoder pair at top-right (teal encoder stack and red decoder stack side by side, each grouped by a coloured curly brace), and a full-width grey 'Multitask training format' panel at the bottom that flares up in a wedge from the decoder's input token strip.
insights.data: Training data is shown as paired lines per task (speaker icon + navy quoted speech, notepad icon + green transcript, in English, Spanish and Korean), audio input is a small log-Mel spectrogram raster under a lilac Conv1D trapezoid, and decoder input/output are rows of adjacent square cells coloured orange (special), blue (text) and green (timestamp), the output row shifted one cell left.
insights.emphasis: The model itself is drawn as stock Transformer blocks; the contribution (data scale and token format) gets the two big bold-titled panels, and red arrows with labels name the task each special token selects (Language identification, X->X Transcription, X->English Translation, VAD, Custom vocabulary).
insights.flow: Read left to right: data panel -> large hollow block arrow -> spectrogram, encoder up bottom-to-top, a 'cross attention' bus leaving the encoder top and dropping into every decoder block, decoder up to next-token output; then down into the bottom state machine read left to right from a start dot through PREV / SOT / LANGUAGE TAG / TRANSCRIBE-or-TRANSLATE / timestamps to EOT, with dotted skip paths to EOT.
insights.avoid: The bottom state machine is dense (crossing arrows between TRANSCRIBE/TRANSLATE and begin-time/NO TIMESTAMPS, a long dotted line along the panel bottom from NO SPEECH to EOT) and the block-internal labels (MLP, cross attention, self attention) are set very small inside thin bars.

figures.lesson: A token-type colour code is defined once in a small legend and reused in the model's input and output strips and in the state-machine panel that wedges out of the input strip, so that panel reads as an expansion of those tokens without any connecting arrow.

figures.title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems

arrangement.units: four horizontal dashed bands (Sparse Features, Dense Embeddings, Hidden Layers, Output Units) crossed by three unframed model columns named in a grey chevron band at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of grey and yellow circles for the sparse features
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a single yellow output unit tops each column
arrangement.shared: the layer bands and their bold labels are shared by all three columns

insights.structure: Three model columns (Wide, Wide & Deep, Deep) stand on four shared horizontal dashed bands, with the band names in bold between the middle and right columns and the model names in a grey chevron strip at the bottom.
insights.data: Sparse features are a row of grey circles with a few yellow active ones, dense embeddings are grey rounded bars holding four dark-to-light circles, and hidden and output units are yellow circles with a black activation stroke.
insights.emphasis: The proposed model is placed between its two parents, and its one output unit collects both a long fan of lines from the sparse features and the lines from its hidden stack.
insights.flow: Everything reads bottom to top along thin grey lines that fan in from features to embeddings, hidden layers and a single output unit per column.
insights.avoid: The dashed bands start at different x positions and their labels sit inside the gap between columns, and the dense identical grey fans make individual wide connections hard to follow.

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed hybrid as the middle column between its two parent models on shared layer bands, so the reader sees it is literally the union of the wide fan and the deep stack.

figures.title: World Models

taxonomy.task: visual reinforcement learning with a learned world model and a compact controller
taxonomy.note: training 'other': the controller C is optimised by evolution strategies (CMA-ES), separately from the VAE and MDN-RNN

arrangement.units: one blue dotted rounded frame for the world model (V over M); environment box, observation image and controller triangle float outside it on whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: one real game frame (VizDoom screenshot) captioned 'observation', fed by an arrow from the environment box above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the figure shows only the inference/control loop
arrangement.shared: the action output of C is split: one line returns up the right edge to the environment, another runs along the bottom back into M, both labelled 'action'

insights.structure: V (hourglass) sits above M (rounded box) inside one dotted 'world model' frame in the centre, with the environment box above, the observation frame to the left and the controller triangle to the right, so the loop circles the frame.
insights.data: The observation is a real game screenshot while the latent signals are just single italic letters on the arrows (z out of V, h out of M), with no tensor drawings.
insights.emphasis: Colour is spent only on the blue dotted frame and its blue label, so the named model stands out without filled boxes.
insights.flow: Clockwise loop: environment -> observation -> V -> z down to M and across to C, h from M to C, then 'action' arrows exit C back up to the environment and back along the bottom into M.
insights.avoid: The two 'action' lines and the h line cross and bend around C's lower-right corner, so the return path into M is hard to trace.

figures.lesson: Draw an agent as a closed loop around the environment and wrap only the learned model in one coloured dotted frame, so the reader sees which part is 'the world model' and which is the small policy.

figures.title: Wuerstchen: An Efficient Architecture for Large-Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

arrangement.units: three unboxed full-width horizontal bands divided by dashed rules, each one training stage with a large text label at its left edge
arrangement.inputs_as: photo thumbnail drawn as a slanted 3-D slab with its pixel size on the edges
arrangement.losses_at: top of each band (teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model, Stages B and C)
arrangement.shared: modules reused across bands keep the same frustum shape and fill (light-green f4 encoder in A and B, peach Semantic Compressor in B and C)

insights.structure: Three full-width horizontal bands (Training of Stage A / B / C) separated by dashed grey rules, each with a large left-hand stage label and its own left-to-right pipeline; Stage A is a mirror-symmetric hourglass, Stages B and C split into a main row and a second row for the Semantic Compressor or noising path.
insights.data: Input and output images are photo thumbnails drawn as slanted slabs with pixel sizes written along their edges (1024/1024/3, 768/768/3), latents and VQ tokens are small 3-D cubes tiled with multicolour cells, and tensor shapes (4x256x256, 1280x24x24, 16x24x24) are written on the arrows.
insights.emphasis: Each band's diffusion model is the largest shape with the largest label ('Model' plus italic symbol): a pale-yellow notched U-Net-like block in Stage B and a slate-purple cuboid in Stage C, the darkest fill in the figure; encoders and the Semantic Compressor are translucent frustums whose narrowing shows the downsampling factor (f4, f32).
insights.flow: Each band reads left to right; loss paths leave the latent cube, run up and across to a teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model and back down from the output, and the conditioning branch (Semantic Compressor -> 1x1 conv -> c_sc) enters the Stage B model from below with text-conditioning joining it.
insights.avoid: The same role gets different fills across bands (yellow model in B, purple in C) and the Stage A band draws no loss at all; small connector labels (1024->786 in a pale-yellow box, against 768 written on the Stage C image) are tiny and visibly inconsistent.

figures.lesson: For a multi-stage training figure, give each stage its own full-width band under a dashed rule and redraw a module that is reused across stages with the same shape and fill colour in every band, so the reader can track the reused parts without separate frozen or shared markers.

figures.title: xDeepFM: Combining Explicit and Implicit Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems

taxonomy.task: CTR prediction with explicit feature interactions
taxonomy.note: architecture other: the Compressed Interaction Network, a stack of layers each formed by outer products with the input field embeddings and compressed into feature maps, sum-pooled per layer

arrangement.units: three unboxed sub-figures side by side, each named by a bold sub-caption beneath it
arrangement.inputs_as: circle-grid embedding matrices (x^k, x^0) with brace-labelled dimensions
arrangement.shared: x^0 field-embedding matrix drawn in every panel; peach for active slices

insights.structure: Three sub-figures in one row with bold captions (a)-(c): (a) outer product of x^k and x^0 producing the tensor Z^{k+1}, (b) the k-th layer compressing Z^{k+1} into H_{k+1} feature maps, (c) the whole CIN with layers x^1...x^k side by side and x^0 below.
insights.data: Embedding matrices are boxes holding grids of circles (rows = fields, columns = embedding dims) labelled by curly braces (m, D, H_k); the intermediate tensor Z^{k+1} is an oblique 3-D slab of stacked sheets; layer outputs in (c) are tilted sheets of grey ellipses.
insights.emphasis: Colour marks only the data taking part in the step: the active column slice is peach and boxed by a dashed rectangle while other circles are grey, and in (b) olive and teal fans of lines converge from the peach circles onto two coloured feature-map dots.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right as zoom-out from one operation to the module; inside (a) and (b) the flow goes bottom to top (matrices up to the tensor, tensor up to feature maps), in (c) thick blue block arrows go from x^0 to every layer and between layers, then sum-pooling arrows rise to a top bar of yellow circles and a gold output arrow.
insights.avoid: Panel (b)'s two fans of about two dozen thin crossing lines are cluttered, and panel (c)'s sheet labels (H_1, H_2, D, Sum pooling) are very small; the three panels also use different projections for the same tensor.

figures.lesson: Draw the field-embedding matrix as a grid of circles (m fields × D dims) and colour only the slice being combined against grey dots, so a tensor operation reads as which dots light up.

figures.title: Zero-1-to-3: Zero-shot One Image to 3D Object

taxonomy.task: single-image novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction

arrangement.units: one unframed composition: a top conditioning row in brackets and a bottom noise -> model -> output row
arrangement.inputs_as: a photorealistic render of an object plus the math tuple (R,T) inside large square brackets; Gaussian noise as a colour-noise square at the left of the bottom row
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two rows: a bracketed condition [input view, (R,T)] on top, and noise -> yellow 'Zero-1-to-3' box -> output view below, joined by a curly brace pointing down into the box.
insights.data: Input and output are the same photorealistic retro computer rendered from two viewpoints, so the viewpoint change is visible, while the camera transform is only the symbol (R,T).
insights.emphasis: The single saturated yellow box carries the method name in large type over a tiny network icon, the only coloured shape in the figure.
insights.flow: The bottom row reads left to right through two thick black block arrows, and the condition enters from above through the brace.
insights.avoid: The figure hides the denoising loop and the network internals entirely, so it cannot show where the pose conditioning is injected; it works only as a concept sketch.

figures.lesson: For a conditioning contribution, write the condition as a bracketed tuple of real data and a pose symbol, then use a curly brace to funnel it into a single bright model box sitting on the noise-to-output row.
